1.1: 1.1 Here begins, from Epiphanius, book On the Lives of the Prophets. Isaiah was born of noble family in Jerusalem and prophesied there; under King Manasseh he was cut in two parts and died. He was buried under the oak of Rogel, near the passage of the waters which King Hezekiah had once blocked by throwing in dust. God made the spring Siloam on account of the Prophet, since before he died he prayed a little that He would deign to form waters there. And at once He sent down to him living water from heaven, whence that place received the name Siloam, which, if one interprets it, means 'sent down.' Also under King Hezekiah, before he had built the pool and cisterns, it came about by the prayers of Isaiah that a small stream gushed forth, because the people were held in siege by enemies, so that the city should not perish deprived of water. In perpetual memory of this the people carefully restored the Prophet there to the ground with glory and honor, so that through his intercessions until the end of the age the fruit of such water might be obtained, the use of which they ascribed to him as received. The tomb of Isaiah stands near the burial place of the princes, behind the tombs of the priests toward the south. For Solomon, building Jerusalem, raised the mausolea of the kings, as David had described them. Here begins JEROME on Isaiah. Isaiah, a noble man of urbane eloquence, having nothing of rusticity in his speech, is to be called not so much a prophet as an evangelist: for he pursues the mysteries of Christ and the Church so clearly that one would think he was weaving a history of past events. He prophesied in Jerusalem and Judah, the ten tribes not yet being taken captive; and concerning both kingdoms he wove his oracles, now together, now separately. And although at times he looks to the present history, and signifies the return of the people into Judea after the Babylonian captivity, yet he directs all his care to the calling of the nations and the coming of Christ. The vision of Isaiah, etc. There are three kinds of vision: the first bodily, by which we see heaven and earth and the like; the second spiritual, by which we see, as in dreams, images of men and the like; the third intellectual, which is in reason, by which we know the Creator and, by the revelation of the Holy Spirit, understand whatever it may be. 'To see' is also often put for 'to understand': whence we often ask, saying: 'Do you see?', that is, 'do you understand?' Prophets too are called 'seers' from this, that is, 'those who understand.' Isaiah saw this vision by the Holy Spirit, namely, as He disclosed it inwardly, he understood the things that were to come. Hence in the beginning he does not set down visions as Daniel does, nor does he say what he saw; but immediately says: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth. JEROME on Isaiah, vol. 4. Not only Isaiah, etc., up to: 'They were not therefore ignorant,' according to Montanus, who saw in this way. The same, ibid. Isaiah is interpreted, etc., up to: 'and when he has done all things, he says: I am an unprofitable servant; what I ought to do, I have done.' Son of Amos. The same, ibid. Amos, the father of Isaiah, is not the third of the twelve Prophets, etc., up to: 'they contend that he was a Prophet.' Concerning Judah and Jerusalem. The same, ibid. Isaiah principally concerning the two tribes, etc., up to: 'that these things were foretold for the correction of the two tribes.' The vision of Isaiah, etc. JEROME, ibid. For Judah, in whom the two tribes are signified, etc., up to: 'of which it is said: Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem, for your light is come.' In the days of Uzziah. The same, ibid. Uzziah is the same who is also Azariah, etc., up to: 'so that our histories may appear older than those of the Gentiles.'
1.2: 1.2 Hear, O heavens, etc. The same, ibid. Above, who the Prophet is, etc., up to: 'since this belongs to the power of God, and not to earthly understanding.' The Lord has spoken. The same, ibid. Not to you, but to me, so that what I heard in the spirit I may relate to you, who do not deserve to hear Him yourselves. I have nourished children. The same, ibid. That which he says: I have adopted them as sons, etc., up to: 'whence: He gave them power to become sons of God.'
1.3: 1.3 The ox knows, etc. The same, ibid. Whence: You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together (Deut. 22). Like Ebion, etc., up to: 'to whom it is said: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened.' The ass. A Gentile, or one converted, wanton, formerly unclean, burdened with sins, who believed in the incarnation of Christ, who, when born, was at once laid in the manger, that by the bridle of His flesh He might refresh all. Israel. JEROME, as above. The scribes and Pharisees, holding the key of knowledge and of the law. Whence they were called Israel, 'seeing God.' He has not known Me. Whose day Abraham saw and was glad (John 8); whose coming the choir of the Prophets prophesied by awaiting it.
1.4: 1.4 Woe to the nation, etc. JEROME, ibid. In this title he recalls the person, the cause, and the time; secondly, he makes them attentive; thirdly, he relates what the Lord spoke; fourthly, he rebukes the sinful nation as if in its excesses. Woe to the nation, etc. He threatens eternal destruction, because they reject the Son, who brought salvation. Iniquity. The same, ibid. Whence: Iniquity sits upon a talent of lead (ZECH. 5); whence elsewhere: Like a heavy burden they are heavy upon me (Ps. 37). Wicked. Others read 'of the worst,' so that the fault is not of the seed, but of their malice, who by their own will forsook God. For the nature of the good and of the evil is not to be thought different. They have blasphemed. Saying: You have a demon, and you are a Samaritan (John 8); and: We have no king but Caesar; and: Is not this the son of the carpenter? They are estranged. JEROME, ibid. They who were called the portion and sons of God (John 19; Matt. 13). It is said of them: Strange sons have lied to me (Ps. 17), whence: No one putting his hand to the plow, etc. (Luke 9), whence the Apostle: Stretching forth to the things that are before, forgetting those that are behind (Phil. 3).
1.5: 1.5 Upon what shall I strike you, etc. The same, ibid. As if he were to say, etc., up to: 'and he shows that there is now no place fit for medicine, thus: Every head is sick,' etc. Every head is sick. The same, ibid. As the gladness of the mind sometimes mitigates the pains of the body, etc., up to: 'whence: From the sole of the foot,' etc.
1.6: 1.6 Wound and bruise. The same, ibid. As if he were to say, etc., up to: 'and they killed the pious physician sent to them.' Nor dressed with ointment. The same, ibid. Whence: We have healed Babylon, and she is not healed, the city, namely, of confusion and of vices, etc., up to: 'and he expressed the irremediable captivity of the Jews.'
1.7: 1.7 Your land is desolate, etc. The same, ibid. These things were partly fulfilled under the Babylonians, etc., up to: 'whence: Unless the Lord guard the city, he watches in vain,' etc.
1.8: 1.8 The daughter of Zion, etc. The same, ibid. The affection of a most loving father. And: For by nature we are all sons of God (John 14), but by our own fault we are made strangers. Hence Babylon is often called a daughter.
1.9: 1.9 Unless the Lord. The same. This is from the person of the Prophet, etc., up to: 'so the Almighty is the Son of the Almighty.'
1.10: 1.10 Hear the word. The same. The remnants being saved, etc., up to: 'and now is perceived by the mind, when the invisible is believed.'
1.11: 1.11 I am full. The same. As if He were to say: Do you think that I need these things or am delighted by them? But I am full, that is, I need nothing. For the earth is mine and the fullness thereof. Or, I am full, that is, affected with weariness, because you do not offer well. Holocausts of rams, etc., up to: 'Judge for the orphan,' etc. He rejects the sacrifices of the Jews and commends the obedience of the Gospel: Holocausts of rams, etc. He points to the final destruction of the temple, which lasts forever. For after the Babylonian captivity the temple was built by Zerubbabel, and sacrifice was offered in it for a long time. The same. Holocausts of rams. This can also be taken of those who, while they despise God's commandments, wish to appease Him with a multitude of sacrifices, and to buy a license to sin. Or those who offer plunder and avarice at the altar and give to the poor. I would not. Using the past tense, he shows that He never loved the sacrifices of the Jews, but endured them for a time on account of what they signified; and, the true sacrifice having been fulfilled, He counted them as nothing.
1.12: 1.12 When you came. The same. God did not seek these sacrifices as though He needed them, but that they might not sacrifice to demons, and that through carnal and typical things they might more easily come to the spiritual and true sacrifice. Who has required? Let the Ebionites hear this, who think that the law is to be kept after the Passion of Christ; let their associates hear this, who decree that it is to be kept for the race of Israel alone.
1.13: 1.13 New moon, etc. The feast of the new moon, which they celebrated at the beginning of the months: neos, new; mene, moon; whence: Blow the trumpet at the new moon (Ps. 80). Your assemblies are wicked, etc. The same. Because they do not offer spiritual sacrifices; whence: A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit (Ps. 50). Verse 14
1.15: 1.15 For your hands are full of blood, etc. The same. Of the Prophets and finally of their Lord, etc., up to: 'they keep watch in prayer day and night.'
1.16: 1.16 Wash yourselves, etc. As if He were to say: This I have hated; the truth of the Gospel pleases Me: Wash yourselves, in the blood of Christ, in the water of baptism. Be clean, remaining in innocence of life. For baptism alone avails for the remission of sin, whence: Unless a man be born again (John 3), etc. And elsewhere: Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, etc. JEROME, as above. The principal order, etc., up to: 'but also in the sight of God, from whom nothing can be hidden.' Cease to do perversely. The same. That echoes the Gospel, etc., up to: 'whom those follow in the Apocalypse who shine with the whiteness of virginity.'
1.17: 1.17 Learn to do well. The same. Not trusting in nature, etc., up to: 'the thresholds of teachers must be worn down.' Seek judgment, etc. The same. The commandments of the Gospel succeed the victims of the Jews. Provision is made for orphans and widows, so that martyrs, secure about their wives and children, may go forth to battle.
1.18: 1.18 As scarlet, etc. The same. Coccus and scarlet and worm are the same, namely, a grave sin, and murder and adultery, etc. But what is signified by snow, this is signified by wool: namely the purification and washing away of sins. Like snow. Because they will be cold against the incentives of vices; and like wool, because they will be clothed against the cold of unbelief. White wool, etc. The same. From which the garment of Christ is made.
1.19: 1.19 If you are willing and listen, etc. The same. Free will is preserved, etc., up to: 'that religion might pass over to the praise of God.' The same. Morally: the faithful soul, full of judgment, while it obeys God, God dwells in it, who is justifying justice; but if it withdraws from God, not in place but in merit, it is inhabited by malignant spirits, who are the murderers of souls.
1.21: 1.21 Justice. The same. Justice, in Hebrew sedek, which rather signifies 'just,' so that we may understand the Lord dwelling in her, of whom it is said: But the just man, what has he done? which in Ezekiel is signified by Oholibah, which is interpreted 'tabernacle,' or 'my tabernacle in her.'
1.22: 1.22 Silver, etc. That is, bright and shining, they have returned to vices. Into dross. The same. Dross, in Hebrew siggim, which is the rust of metals, or the refuse and filth that is smelted out by fire. Your wine, etc. Others: Your tavern-keepers mix wine with water. Symmachus: Your wine is mixed with water. Morally: Your wine is mixed with water: because he softens to their own will the precepts of Holy Scripture, by which they ought to correct their hearers, and by mixing in his own sense he spoils the wine. Your wine, etc. Heretics also corrupt the Gospel, the worst tavern-keepers, making water out of wine, whereas the Lord turned water into wine, at which the master of the feast marveled; and the Queen of Sheba, at the banquet of Solomon, praised the cupbearers and servants of the wine.
1.23: 1.23 Companions of thieves. The same. Receiving from the Scribes and Pharisees the gifts which they took away from the poor. In the Lord's Passion also they were unfaithful, unwilling to believe in Christ; and companions of thieves, namely of the Scribes and Pharisees and of Judas the traitor. Companions of thieves, etc. We too ought to beware lest we receive gifts from those who gather riches from the tears of the poor, lest we be companions of thieves, and lest it be said of us: If you saw a thief, you ran with him, etc. Then follow rewards. The same. Because they do not regard them as friends, etc., up to: 'that is, bear patiently.'
1.24: 1.24 The strong one of Israel. The same. The Septuagint: Woe, you strong ones of Israel, etc., up to: 'or in morals.' Alas, I. The same. With the affection of a pious father He laments and strikes them, though enemies, because they perish and are unwilling to repent. I shall be comforted, etc. The same. He is comforted by vengeance, etc., up to: 'in which he signifies that they will suffer torments.'
1.25: 1.25 Your tin. The same. The false doctrine of the Scribes and Pharisees, which is like the true, as tin is like silver. And I will give pure and perfect knowledge of the law and of the Gospel.
1.26: 1.26 And I will restore your judges, etc. The same. Not only after the captivity, such as Zerubbabel, Ezra, and others, who ruled the people until Hyrcanus; but also after the coming of the Lord, the Apostles and other teachers of the Church. City of the just, faithful city Zion, shall be redeemed in judgment. The Church, in which they are recalled to living justly. For a city is a gathering of men for living justly.
1.30: 1.30 Like an oak whose leaves are fading. The same. As from an oak shaken by dryness, etc., up to: 'nor does it even bear herbs for the sick man to eat.'
2.2: 2.2 In the last days. JEROME. Of which Jacob, etc., up to: 'it grew into a great mountain.' Mountain. The mountains are angels, prophets, patriarchs, apostles, martyrs, and others who shone with miracles. The hills are the lesser, receiving light from the greater. And it shall be lifted up. The same. Above all the saints, because all receive from His fullness; of whom it is said: Mountains are round about it, which are called mountains from the mountain Christ.
2.3: 2.3 The house. The same. This is said so that we may accept the Old Testament, and not, according to Manichaeus, seek some other house than the house of the God of Jacob. His ways, which others have trodden. The Lord also, ascending the mountain, taught His disciples. First, therefore, the ways are to be learned, afterward one must walk in the paths. From Zion. JEROME. Not from the rock of Sinai, but from Mount Zion, in which is Jerusalem, in which is the temple and the religion of God. The Lord also taught in the temple, because it was not fitting for a Prophet to die outside Jerusalem. The law and the word. As above, he put the word and the law together, so that the princes might hear the word and the people receive the law by ear. For he who has fulfilled the law will come to the word of God; the law will go forth from the word as from a fountain, to water others.
2.4: 2.4 And they shall beat their swords. The same. All zeal for warring will be turned to peace, etc., up to: 'let us eat in the time of harvest,' namely of death.
2.5: 2.5 House of Jacob, etc. The same. After the calling of the Gentiles and the showing of the mountain of God, he invites his people, who are of Jacob, that, coming out of the darkness of unbelief, they may receive the light of Christ. In the light. The same. While you have the light, believe in the light. Draw near to Him and be enlightened, etc. As if He were to say: He who does evil hates the light; but come with me, let us walk in the light of the Lord, who says: I am the light of the world, etc. Verse 6
2.7: 2.7 The land is filled. The same. Both the avarice of the Romans and of the Jews is rebuked; for Greek and Latin histories testify that nothing is more avaricious than either nation: among idols, avarice is condemned.
2.8: 2.8 With horses and innumerable. The same. This too is against the Lord, who forbade the multiplying of chariots and horses: for these animals were given to help, not to be proud of, whence they are also called beasts of burden.
2.9: 2.9 He bowed down. Where once was the temple and religion of God, there is the statue of Hadrian and the idol of Jupiter. Therefore not. Isaiah does not curse, but blesses, etc., up to: 'and they are filled with idols,' etc. From the face of the fear of the Lord. From the wrath of judgment. And from the glory of His majesty. Because He will come with great power and majesty.
2.11: 2.11 The eyes of the lofty, etc. Jerome. Neither riches, nor power, nor nobility of birth will save anyone; one captivity will come upon all. These things can also be taken of the day of judgment, when every creature will be humbled in the sight of God and will feel that it is nothing in comparison with Him. But the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
2.12: 2.12 Of the Lord of hosts. Wherever he speaks of the victory or vengeance of the Lord, he calls Him the Lord of hosts, lest we doubt the victory of Him whose power is so great.
2.14: 2.14 High mountains. JEROME. According to the variety of virtues, some are called mountains of the good, others hills. According to the diversity of vices, some are mountains of the impious, others hills, to whom it is said: I will bring a sword upon you, etc. And upon every tower. The same. Literally: when the Romans came, both towers and walls were overthrown from the foundations, etc., up to: 'lest perverse doctrine prevail over the truth.'
21.14: 21.14 Meeting the thirsty, bring. This can be said against those who have given themselves to idleness and sloth and are content with their own salvation, and do not stretch out a hand to the penitent and converted. Bring water to the thirsty. To brethren wearied by the heat of the sun and by thirst, bring water, lest they perish in the wilderness.
21.16: 21.16 Yet in one, etc. As if He said: Because you had no mercy on them, you will soon endure the misery of captivity. A year after the Jewish captivity and the overthrow of Jerusalem, these also were laid waste. As in the year of a hireling: The same. Which is: As a hireling his year, etc., up to: 'and have eaten the heavenly bread.'
22.1: 22.1 The burden of the valley. Jerusalem, once the mistress of nations, etc., up to: 'who from the sublime sense of the Scriptures have fallen to the lowest.' Valley of vision. The Septuagint: Zion, that is, of the watchtower, namely, of the Church. What ails you also. As if He said: When philosophy and worldly wisdom, disputing about lofty things, despise the simplicity of the Church, why do you also pursue high things?
22.2: 22.2 Full. The doctrine of heretics is full of much talk and clamor. Your slain. JEROME. The valley, namely Zion; by their own will they passed over to the heretics. In comparison with those who were conquered after battle, they who give themselves up of their own accord are wounded more unhappily: as in martyrdom, he who denies after the torments is punished more lightly than he who denies Christ without necessity.
22.3: 22.3 All your princes, etc. As is read in Jeremiah, Zedekiah by night through a hole in the wall, etc., up to: 'and were led into Babylon.' They fled. In flight they agree, whose prince is the fleeing dragon, the twisting serpent.
22.5: 22.5 And of weeping. The same. Septuagint: of error. Not that weeping and error come from the Lord, but from the occasion of the Scriptures which He gave them to read, the occasion of error arises, and they can say: Why have you made us err from Your way? (Isa. 63).
22.6: 22.6 Elam. A city in the province of Persia, in which are the best archers: Elam took up the quiver. Elam, their ascent, that is, the pride of heretics, took up the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart. The wall. The firmaments of the Church, with its shield, that is, with assault, he laid bare.
22.8: 22.8 The covering. The temple, which was previously covered and closed to the Gentiles and the polluted. The armory. Near the temple was the house which David built to store arms, around which were many trees; whence it is called the house of the forest. It too was not of stone but of wood: for from the moisture of the mortar and stones, as they say, iron rusts.
22.9: 22.9 And you gathered. The land of promise, although most fertile, etc., up to: 'the lower, which could be taken by enemies, the upper, which could not.'
22.11: 22.11 And a pool. The same. Not a well which has living and eternal water, but broken cisterns which cannot hold water. Between the two walls. Namely, both the New and the Old Testament, they have made for themselves new waters, which they think more inward and to contain greater mysteries than the Old Testament.
22.12: 22.12 And the Lord God of hosts will call. Daily the Lord calls heretics to penance, etc., up to: 'but despising and despairing they said: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die (Jer. 34).'
22.14: 22.14 You shall die. The same. To vices, or may you go down with them to the lower world, etc., up to: 'what is said here does not pertain to the captivity made in the time of Hezekiah.'
22.15: 22.15 Shebna. JEROME. Turn now, etc., up to: 'whence the Lord threatens him with these evils.'
22.16: 22.16 What do you here? As if He said: Why do you want to build a house for yourself? etc., up to: 'than to be called a sepulcher and memorial.'
22.18: 22.18 Crowning, he will crown you. You who once had the crown of the high priest, and the sanctification in the plate of gold on which the name of God was written, will be crowned with tribulation and distress. Tribulation. In place of the golden plate on which the name of the Lord was written, which the priest bore on his forehead once a year. Like a ball. As a sphere cannot stand in a sloping and spacious place, so your people will be scattered to the ends of the earth.
22.20: 22.20 My servant Eliakim. Through the proud Shebna, etc., up to: 'son of Hilkiah, that is, of the Father of the Lord.'
22.22: 22.22 The key. By the key which he carries upon his shoulder, the scepter of the kingdom and the sign of victory, we can understand the cross, which Christ Himself carried on His own shoulder. The house of David. He calls the house of the Lord the house of David, in which was the golden key. And he shall open. Whence: He who opens and no one shuts, shuts and no one opens. What He unlocked in the Passion cannot be closed; what He closed in the ceremonies no one will open.
22.24: 22.24 And I will hang upon. Whence in the Gospel: All the people hung upon Him. Today also they hang upon the word of His wisdom.
22.25: 22.25 The peg shall be taken away. The things that are said, etc., up to: 'the Jews will be converted to the faith.'
23.1: 23.1 The burden of Tyre. Tyre, a most noble city of the Canaanites, etc., up to: 'Isaiah foretells this misery: The burden of Tyre, etc.' Howl. In the Greek more openly: Howl, ships of Carthage: you, namely, who were accustomed to come to Tyre for trade. Carthage was a colony of the Tyrians, built and cultivated by them. Ships of the sea. In Hebrew Tarshish, that is, 'exploration of joy' or 'contemplation,' because the contemplation of joy and gladness will be turned into tears.
23.3: 23.3 The merchandise. JEROME. Merchants, etc., up to: 'and from other vices they pass to others.' The seed of the Nile, the harvest of the river, the crops, etc. It is construed thus: the seed of the Nile river was the harvest and its crops, namely of Tyre. The land of the Canaanites, in which Tyre is, is infertile; Egypt, which the Nile waters, is fertile in crops, which Tyre exchanged from the Egyptians.
23.4: 23.4 The sea. Of the world, namely, in which are small animals with great, the dragon whom the Lord formed to mock him, seeing them seized by the hunters of Christ, who had been seized by demons, says to the contrary strength of the hunters, which Sidon signifies: Be ashamed, Sidon. I have not travailed. As if He said: It profited nothing to have travailed, to have borne and nourished young men, because Tyre was taken without defense.
23.5: 23.5 When it shall be heard in Egypt, etc. This is felt both of all vices and of heresies, because when one is taken, another fears greatly, and in the confusion of one the other feels that it will be taken.
23.6: 23.6 Pass over, howl, you who dwell. As was said above, when they could not resist Nebuchadnezzar, those who could hastened to board ships; others remained in the city.
23.7: 23.7 Is not this your city, which gloried from the days of old in antiquity, etc. As if He said: I command these things therefore, because your city Tyre, laying aside the old error, will pass over to the truth.
23.8: 23.8 Whose merchants are princes, her traders the nobles of the earth, etc. The same. Among other merchants, or even in kingdoms.
23.9: 23.9 To bring to shame, etc. The Lord is not the author of shame, but He shows what is shameful, according to that: With contamination he shall contaminate him; not that the priest is the author of contamination, but that he shows to be contaminated one whom many thought clean.
23.10: 23.10 The river. Of the Babylonians. By the rivers of Babylon there we sat and wept, when we remembered Zion (Ps. 136). The girdle no more to you. Strength of resistance, for with a girdle we bind our loins: we are said to have strength in the loins.
23.11: 23.11 He troubled the kingdoms. Namely of the Egyptians and the Moabites, and of others round about. For Tyre being taken and overthrown, the other kingdoms were troubled with fear. The kingdom of Egypt also was given to Nebuchadnezzar in place of the overthrown Tyre.
23.12: 23.12 Daughter of Sidon. The same. In the land of Canaan are Tyre and Sidon; whence: A Canaanite woman came out of the borders of Tyre and Sidon, meeting the Savior (Matt. 15). Cross over. We often see some pass from their purpose to another, from soldiering to trade: from lawsuits to arms they change their effort in order to change their misfortune. But, by God's dispensation, all things turn out contrary, so that, compelled by miseries, they may trust not in themselves but in the Lord their Creator.
23.13: 23.13 There was never such a people. Until the death of Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldeans and Assyrians were the strongest above all; afterward the people of the Greeks and Romans was stronger. They undermined. When Nebuchadnezzar attacked Tyre with ships, he overthrew not only the wall but also the houses; and what had been the trade of cities became for seventy years a drying place for nets.
23.14: 23.14 Ships of the sea, etc. In Hebrew Tarshish, etc., up to: 'the churchman destroys and subjects to himself.'
23.15: 23.15 Seventy years. JEROME. Tyre, once afflicted, etc., up to: 'who then would not have hope of salvation, if he sings well, if he arranges the strings, that is, the virtues, well?' The same. The number seven and seventy, which is completed either by single days or by seven decades, signifies perfect penance, so that, the time of penance being fulfilled, Tyre is rightly restored to her former state. The song of a harlot. Who, forsaken by her lovers, is wont to compose songs for consolation and to recall past things; so also Tyre returned.
23.16: 23.16 Take a harp. What follows of this burden looks to the return of Tyre. Sing well, often. He warns her to sing always the song of her miseries, lest she suffer the same again. For they say that this is the nature of music: if it finds one joyful, it makes him more joyful; if sad, it makes him sadder.
23.18: 23.18 And her merchandise and her hire shall be. As Jerome says on Jeremiah, etc., up to: 'they sacrificed their hire to the Lord.'
24.1: 24.1 Behold, the Lord will lay bare, etc. JEROME. After the special rebuke of the individual nations, etc., up to: 'from the burden of the Egyptians and many others he passes to the general burden of the last judgment.'
24.2: 24.2 It shall be. The same. All alike will either be rewarded for good or condemned for evil. There will be no difference between noble and ignoble, priest and layman, servant and master, etc. For all will stand equally before the tribunal of Christ; nor will there be respect of persons with God. As the priest. The good people with the good priest will receive the crown of life; the wicked together will endure the torments of hell without respect of persons. The earth. The same. Earthly works will be reduced to nothing, so that, the image of the earthly man being abolished, the image of the heavenly may remain. For flesh and blood shall not possess the kingdom of God, because this mortal shall put on immortality.
24.6: 24.6 The curse shall devour the earth. As in the beginning God blessed every creature, so in the end He curses those who are earthly; not strangers, but dwellers on the earth: and those who sin in it, forgetful of their condition, raging against one another. And few shall remain who bear the image of the heavenly.
24.7: 24.7 The vintage has mourned, the vine is weakened. The same. At the consummation of the world, the memory of past delights will be the matter of torments; whence the rich man in purple, who had received good things in his life, lifting up his eyes from hell, sees Lazarus at rest (Luke 19); whence: Woe to you who are filled, for you shall hunger (Luke 6). All who were merry have groaned, etc. We bring this testimony against those who at banquets indulge not only gluttony and drunkenness but also their ears, so that through all the senses the strength of the soul grows soft.
24.10: 24.10 The city of vanity is broken down. The world, in which all is vain, vanity of vanities, and all is vanity.
24.11: 24.11 There shall be a cry over the wine. By wine, error; for the drunk err. By the streets, which in Greek are named from breadth, we understand the spacious and broad way that leads to death. Over those, therefore, who have erred in the broad and spacious way of this age, there will be a cry of sorrow on the day of judgment.
24.13: 24.13 In the midst of the earth. Jerusalem, which is, as they say, the navel of the earth. And many think that the Lord, about to judge, will sit in the air over Mount Zion, from which He ascended, and will come in a cloud. As if a few olives, etc. A few being left, when persecution has devoured the earth, etc., up to: 'and the clusters also being gathered, scarcely a few remain on the empty vines.'
24.14: 24.14 And they shall praise: when the Lord shall be glorified. The same. They will praise who shall be able to remain and flee the oppression of Antichrist, or the burning of impending hell. They shall neigh. After the likeness of horses, exulting in the greatness of joy.
24.16: 24.16 From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one. In the Hebrew, from the wings of the earth. The wings or ends of the earth are the prophets and apostles, who fly from earthly to heavenly things, and by certain bounds of precepts set the limit of the manner of living. The saints therefore say: As we heard from the prophets and apostles, so now we see it fulfilled. My secret to myself. The same. He can neither fully relate the rewards of the good nor the punishments of the wicked, which he foresees through the Spirit; and he therefore grieves, saying: Woe to me.
24.17: 24.17 Fear and the pit. These things can be referred both to the times of the martyrs, etc., up to: 'so it will also be in the time of Antichrist.'
24.18: 24.18 The floodgates are opened, etc. That God may see the iniquities of Antichrist and judge. For while He does not punish sins, He pretends not to see them. The foundations of the earth. The princes of the age, earthly works.
24.19: 24.19 It shall be utterly broken. Not that the earth will be reduced to dust or to nothing, but because all earthly things will pass away. And as a drunken man knows not what he does, so all who dwell on the earth will be drunk with the greatness of evils and will be stupefied at everything.
24.20: 24.20 A tent of one night. The same. Which is moved by the traveler so that no trace remains; so the fashion of this world will pass away (1 Cor. 7), and the earth will be desert, so that there is no longer any dwelling of men in it.
24.21: 24.21 And it shall be, etc. As if He said: The windows of heaven are opened, so that the Lord, looking upon earthly sins, may cause every form of earthly works to pass away and fall, and not rise again in its former stature. Therefore the Lord will visit in that day the host of heaven, that He may judge not only earthly but heavenly things. Upon the host. The same. My sword is drunk in heaven. The stars are not clean in His sight. And in His angels He found wickedness (Isa. 34; Job 15, 4). The kings of the earth. JEROME. The rulers of darkness, against the spiritual wickedness in the heavenly places (Eph. 6); whence in Daniel: The prince of the kingdom of the Persians went out to meet me, and the prince of the kingdom of the Medes (Dan. 10).
24.22: 24.22 And they shall be gathered together. The same. Origen says that, after this sentence: Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire (Matt. 25), after many days, that is, after a thousand years, they are to be visited and freed. But the Church does not accept this. For it has been said: The wicked shall go into everlasting punishment, but the just into life everlasting (Matt. 13). And what is eternal lacks every end, and as the joy is eternal, so is the punishment. One bundle into the pit. Whence: Bind them in bundles to burn. And after many. It should be noted that he does not add: by the Lord or by the angels, etc., up to: 'which is left to the judgment of the Lord.'
24.23: 24.23 And shall be ashamed. Whence the creature groans and travails, etc., up to: 'such as Abraham was, who died in a good old age.'
25.1: 25.1 Amen. JEROME. A Hebrew word, which the Lord often uses in the Gospel: Amen, amen, that is, truly, truly I say to you.
25.2: 25.2 The city. Overthrown by Nebuchadnezzar, it was restored by Nehemiah and by Jesus the high priest. Overthrown by the Romans, it was restored by Aelius Hadrian; but not in the same place, nor to its former state. And forever. The same. So that the fable of the thousand years' kingdom and of the golden and jeweled Jerusalem may cease.
25.10: 25.10 And Moab shall be trodden down, etc. The same. Although he spoke generally of the consummation of the world, etc., up to: 'by Moab, therefore, we rightly understand the devil, always the adversary of the sons of God.' Straw in the wagon. Straw is threshed with iron-shod wagons, so that the animals may more easily feed on it and chew it.
26.1: 26.1 In that day, etc. The same. This can be referred to the present Church and to the day of judgment. Now the Church sings a new song: the nativity, passion, resurrection, ascension of Christ. For it is old for the ancient man to descend to the lower world; new, to ascend to heaven. A city of strength. The voice of the just, both now and in the future.
26.2: 26.2 Open the gates. This song suddenly changes persons. The gates. Of justice; whence: Open to me the gates of justice. The gates of life and of justice, etc., up to: 'and through many gates to Him who says: No one comes to the Father but by me (John 14).'
26.3: 26.3 Peace. The same. Repetition is confirmation. He has this peace of whom it is said: Man, man of the children of Israel (Ezek. 14); and elsewhere: Man, man whose wife shall have defiled the bed (Num. 5), so that the double man and the double husband may obtain a double peace.
26.6: 26.6 The foot shall tread it down, etc. Because Everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled (Luke 1). We can refer this also to the contrary powers. Of the needy. JEROME. Of the apostles, whom the Jews drove out of their borders, who, imitating the poverty of the Lord, obtained the privilege of virtue.
26.9: 26.9 My soul has desired, etc. Not the flesh; whence: My soul has thirsted for God, the living fountain (Ps. 41). The flesh lusts against the spirit (Gal. 5).
26.10: 26.10 Let us have mercy. The same. The Lord to the prophet: Shall we have mercy on the wicked, so that he may learn, namely my clemency, while he himself is saved? as if, this is better. And the just shall not learn, etc. As if He said: How will he be able to know Your justice, having experienced Your clemency? And he shall not see. The Lord to the prophet: as if it is better that he see and be ashamed of his evils. And he shall not see, as if He said: for punishment it is enough, that he will not see me reigning in heaven with my saints. Septuagint: Let the wicked be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God.
26.11: 26.11 Let the zealous be confounded. Septuagint: Zeal will seize an uninstructed people.
26.12: 26.12 Lord, You will give. The same. It should be noted that after He has repaid us our works, He will also give peace, and that they therefore ask peace because He has worked in them. They say that they have endured, namely, torments, that after them they may obtain mercy.
26.13: 26.13 Lord, they have possessed. The same. The demons, whom we worshipped in idols. Septuagint: Lord, besides You we know no other; not absolutely another, but besides You: for the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father. Only in You let us remember. The same. We ask nothing else, but that after our errors we may be worthy to remember Your name. You have destroyed all. The same. Septuagint: their male, etc., up to: 'he interpreted memory as male, against that: Do not err, God is not mocked.'
26.15: 26.15 Surely. He did not do penance, and this is: Surely, etc., as if He said: Security begets negligence, negligence contempt.
26.18: 26.18 And we have brought forth. Others punctuate thus: And we have brought forth wind; we have not wrought salvation on the earth. Spirit: by salvation, etc. That we may believe with all our mind, and learn through torments those by whom we did not perceive benefits.
26.21: 26.21 The earth shall disclose. The same. The earthly then will not be able to hide those whom they killed, because then all things are open; or, the earth which received and covered the blood of the martyrs will then be uncovered when they rise again.
27.1: 27.1 In that day, etc. The same. The Hebrews relate that the devil, etc., up to: 'that a sword be brought upon him.' The bar. JEROME. Septuagint: the fugitive. For then he will flee, etc., up to: 'but a serpent, because he softly pours in ambushes.' The whale. The Hebrews, Tanniu; whence the Hebrews fabled that Leviathan dwells under the earth and in the air, but Tanniu in the sea.
27.2: 27.2 The vineyard of pure wine shall sing. To which Jeremiah offers the most unmixed cup. Merum in Greek, purum in Latin.
27.5: 27.5 Or rather? The voice of the Father deliberating, etc., up to: 'who were not saved by the authority of the law.'
27.6: 27.6 Israel, that is, the people of the Jews converted, seeing the world flourish by the teaching of his sons.
27.9: 27.9 Therefore. As if He said: Therefore the iniquity of the house of Jacob will be forgiven: and the rest, on account of the merits of the apostles, who through the world broke down the altars of idols.
27.11: 27.11 They shall be broken. The same. As Deborah went to war and judged the people to the shame of the Jews; and, with the captivity of the Chaldeans imminent, Huldah prophesied while the men were silent: so, with the captivity by the Romans imminent, women perhaps came and taught them. Women. The various synagogues; or plainly women, who with bared breasts strike their bleeding arms. Teaching her. JEROME. A great misfortune and reproach of the people, to learn songs of lamentation from women.
27.12: 27.12 From the channel. Septuagint: from the Euphrates, etc., up to: 'because it has turbid waters, and not perpetual.'
28.1: 28.1 Woe to the crown of pride. The same. Up to this point to the consummation of the world, etc., up to: 'nor had the fruit of the salvation of penance.' Of the very fat valley. Gethsemane, by the fertility of its crops; through it was their ascent into the city, and there some pitched tents for sport while they stayed in the city.
28.5: 28.5 In that day. The same. According to the prophecy, when the Lord, etc., up to: 'for the Scribes and Pharisees were drunk with wine and strong drink.'
28.6: 28.6 Strength to those returning. The same. The wars of Hezekiah are not read, but the Lord waged war for him, one hundred and eighty-five thousand Assyrians being slain, whose spoils the Jews gathered; and they returned with joy to the gates of Jerusalem.
28.8: 28.8 For all. While they do not digest the foods of the Scriptures, nor make them vital for the body, but void them immature and foul, so that the Lord finds no place in them.
28.9: 28.9 Weaned from milk, drawn from. Not others, because they cannot bear it. For these are they who can now use solid food; to others the Apostle says: I gave you milk to drink, not meat (1 Cor. 3).
28.10: 28.10 For command, command again, command, command again; wait, wait again, wait, wait again, a little there, a little there. The same. As if He said: You cannot be taught, because mocking the prophets through whom the Lord foretells to you the evils to come, that you may do penance and be delivered, you object, command, command again; as if to say: O Prophet, command what you will, threaten what you will; yet these things which you threaten do not happen.
28.11: 28.11 For with the speech. As if He said: You say these things to your own harm, because the Lord henceforth will not foretell evils to you, but will bring them at once. And this is: For with the speech of lip and another tongue they shall speak to this people, etc.
28.16: 28.16 A stone. The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner.
28.19: 28.19 Vexation alone will give understanding to the hearing.
28.21: 28.21 For as. David, coming upon the gathered Philistines with the help of the Lord, separated the living from the dead and scattered the perverse places; whence that place received the name Baal-perazim. A strange work. The same. The proper work of God is to have mercy, to spare, to forgive. Not His own, but strange, is to be angry, to punish. GREGORY. He will come into the world to do His work, namely to redeem the human race; but His work is strange to Him; for it is not fitting to the Godhead to be spat upon, scourged, crucified.
28.24: 28.24 Does the plowman plow all day? JEROME. God, pious and merciful, plows the human race, that it may bring forth the fruit of good work, like a farmer with the plowshare of preaching, breaks it up with the scourge of tribulation, now by plague, now by captivity corrects it; and this is: Does he plow all day, etc.?
28.25: 28.25 Gith and cumin. Gith and cumin, which are beaten out with a rod, etc., up to: 'having the key of knowledge.'
28.29: 28.29 And this also comes forth from the Lord God.
29.1: 29.1 Woe to Ariel. The same. To Jerusalem with the affection of one who suffers with her: Because if you had known, even you (Luke 19); Ariel, lion of God; for Jerusalem was the lion of God, most powerful and strong. He fought. The same. When she was most powerful, the blind and lame resisting, when Joab first climbed to the high places of the roofs. A year is added. When they were in captivity under Nebuchadnezzar, they had neither temple nor sacrifice, and this for many years: and this is, year added to year.
29.3: 29.3 Like a sphere round about you. Retaining the ancient likeness of the temple, not the magnificence.
29.4: 29.4 Of Python, etc. The same. The pythoness who was in Endor raised up Samuel, or rather a demon, by necromancy; and foretold such future things to that people. Mania, madness, whence Manichees, manthos, divination.
29.6: 29.6 In thunder. The Romans were seen rushing in with thunder, and the earth moved at their coming, and with a flame of fire, because they burned both the city and the temple.
29.9: 29.9 Be astonished and wonder. JEROME. After the overthrow of Jerusalem and the temple, that is Ariel, the prophecy is directed against the Scribes and Pharisees.
29.11: 29.11 For it is sealed. These things were fulfilled when they lost both dignity and priesthood, and the city was destroyed, and the temple, by the Roman princes.
29.13: 29.13 Because this people draws near. The same. The Lord uses it in the Gospel of Matthew, etc., up to: 'having used their own words.' With their lips. The same. Septuagint: With their lips they honor me, but their heart is far from me: and in vain do they worship me, teaching the precepts and doctrines of men.
29.14: 29.14 For shall perish. The same. From this place the Apostle takes a testimony: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject; in other words, the same sense: Truly God worked a great miracle among the people, in that at the same time the city burned, and the temple fell, and all the knowledge of the teachers perished.
29.15: 29.15 To hide from the Lord. The same. As though God did not see. By this error Adam and Eve hid themselves; Cain also said: From Your face I shall be hidden.
29.16: 29.16 This is perverse, etc. The same. As though the Creator were ignorant of the creature; whence the Apostle: O man, who are you to answer back to God? Shall the thing formed say to him who formed it: Why have you made me thus? (Rom. 9).
29.17: 29.17 In a little and in a short time. JEROME. A little and a short time from when this was foretold until the ascension of the Lord: for all times, compared with eternity, are short and momentary. Lebanon into Carmel. Lebanon, a mountain in Phoenicia, etc., up to: 'if she were with an adulterous husband.'
29.21: 29.21 And they turned aside in vain from the just one. The demons tried, etc., up to: 'the Scribes and Pharisees turned aside in vain from the just one, saying: We have no king but Caesar (John 19).'
29.22: 29.22 He redeemed Abraham. From the fire of the Chaldeans, etc., up to: 'for their tongue is a fire, as it is said.'
30.1: 30.1 Woe to the rebellious children, says the Lord. The same. After the prophecy against Ariel and the rest, etc., up to: 'they fled into Egypt: and this is: woe to the rebellious children.'
30.2: 30.2 You who walk. As Jerome says: Jeremiah went with them, etc., up to: 'that you might dwell in your land.' For they were in Tahpanhes. As if He said: Did you therefore withdraw from me, to flee as far as Tahpanhes and Hanes? Tahpanhes is the city in which the magicians did signs against Moses; Hanes is situated on the borders of Egypt: perhaps, troubled by fear, they did not dare to remain in Tahpanhes and fled as far as Hanes.
30.6: 30.6 The burden of the beasts. The same. After ten burdens of various nations, he sets down the eleventh burden of the remaining two tribes, who remained when Zedekiah and the other princes were led to Babylon. In the land. The same. The desert through which the high priest Johanan son of Kareah and the other leaders brought the remnant into Egypt against the command of the Lord; or Egypt itself, in which they endured many tribulations and straits.
30.8: 30.8 Now therefore. The same. The Lord to Jeremiah, or to Isaiah according to the Hebrews, etc., up to: 'because I did well by them, taught them well, and they themselves despised.'
30.12: 30.12 Because you have rejected the word. The same. Heretics also and every doctrine contrary to the truth, etc., up to: 'and at least to offer muddy and little water to the thirsty.'
30.13: 30.13 As a falling breach. As if: As a breach in a very high wall, which has drawn a long ruin, can be restored only with difficulty and receive its former beauty, so sudden destruction will come upon you.
30.19: 30.19 Weeping you shall not weep. The same. The Jews refer this to the time when under Zerubbabel, etc., up to: 'on the watchtower, namely, and the vision of peace, that is, the Church.'
30.21: 30.21 Behind your back. In the first condition, as if in his face, Adam heard from the Lord, etc., up to: 'and this is: Your ears shall hear the word of one admonishing behind your back.' Neither to the right. On either side, whatever is beyond measure is in vice. Neither to the right, etc., must one turn, but walk by the public road, that is, the royal one, which does not deceive.
30.22: 30.22 And you shall defile the plates. The same. The idols, namely, which a skilled tongue has composed in the likeness of truth, in the splendor of eloquence, which silver signifies, and in the reason of wisdom, which gold signifies, you shall break in pieces and scatter, and judge unclean.
30.23: 30.23 And rain shall be given. The same. In the volume of Kings it is written, etc., up to: 'for unless they cast away vices, virtues do not enter.' It shall feed. Some contend that these things were hyperbolically fulfilled in Judea in the times of Cyrus, who released the captivity of the people.
30.24: 30.24 Mixed fodder. Isaac sowed barley, etc., up to: 'through chaff and barley they gradually advance, and pass over to wheat.'
30.25: 30.25 And there shall be. On the day of judgment upon mountains and hills there shall be streams, etc., up to: 'for he who drinks of its waters shall not thirst forever.' Of the slaughter of many. The same. For many are called, etc., up to: 'whose tongues were confounded in Babylon, and upon whom the tower in Siloam fell.'
30.26: 30.26 And the light shall be. When they receive the reward of labor, because the creature will be freed from the slavery of corruption. It is no wonder if the moon receives the brightness of the sun: for The just shall shine like the sun (Matt. 13).
30.27: 30.27 Behold the name of the Lord. The Son in the name of the Father, for there is one name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit: whence: Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: not in names, but in the name, which is God.
30.28: 30.28 His spirit as a torrent overflowing. JEROME. As an overflowing torrent, when it reaches the neck, suffocates a living thing, so the spirit of God's wrath in judgment will suffocate the wicked. Signifying that the end of all has come; as a torrent suffocates him to whose neck it comes, so God's judgment will pass over no one unpunished. Which was in the jaws. That they may be carried about at the devil's will, the Lord will destroy these on the day of judgment, or in the preaching of the apostles when the Gentiles come to the faith and abandon idols.
30.29: 30.29 You shall have a song. After the punishment of the wicked he treats of the glory of the saints. As the children of Israel, having crossed the Red Sea, when they saw Pharaoh and the Egyptians drowned, said with joy: Let us sing to the Lord, for He has gloriously, etc.; so on the day of judgment, the world having passed and the devil and his members condemned, the saints will exult with joy in the praises of God; in the same way in the conversion of the Gentiles. As one who goes. The children of Israel were commanded to offer a tenth of their goods to the Lord, glorifying the Giver of goods: so the saints at the judgment will offer their sheaves, exulting and praising God, and the converted Gentiles likewise.
30.33: 30.33 Of brimstone. In hell there is intolerable stench and unquenchable fire.
31.1: 31.1 Woe to those who go down into Egypt. The same. He has dealt with the glory of the good and the punishment of the wicked; now he returns to the remnant that remained in the land of Judah, when Zedekiah and the others were led to Babylon. But first he warned them not to go into Egypt: now because they went he threatens evil. They have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel. They did not seek Him with the heart, but with words; for they said to Jeremiah: Pray for us to the Lord, what we ought to do; and they were unwilling to obey. Like which: They have not called upon God. This was said of wicked priests.
31.2: 31.2 But He is wise. Whence Jeremiah: Cursed is the man who trusts in man, etc., up to: 'the place where the Lord was crucified is specially called Sodom and Egypt (Apoc. 11).'
31.4: 31.4 For thus says. JEROME. This is about those who, led into captivity with Zedekiah, returned after seventy years by the mercy of the Lord, the Israelites and the Egyptians, in whose help they trusted, having been slain in Egypt.
31.5: 31.5 So will the Lord protect. So the Lord did against the Samaritans, who tried to hinder the building of the temple. And in the time of the Maccabees He routed many by few.
31.6: 31.6 Return. In prophecy he keeps neither the order of time nor of history, etc., up to: 'so with the whole affection of the mind they would return.'
31.9: 31.9 There is a fire in Zion. Zion, the Church, in which is the fire and furnace that devours sinners, that is, consumes wood, hay and stubble.
32.1: 32.1 Behold a king shall reign in justice. JEROME. The prophecy concerning those who went down into Egypt being finished, he begins concerning the coming of Christ and of His apostles.
32.2: 32.2 And a man shall be as. The same. As if He said: So he shall be safe in tribulations, as one who, fleeing wind and whirlwind, hides himself safely in a place; and who finds the purest springs in the desert; who avoids the heat of the sun beneath an overhanging rock.
32.9: 32.9 Women. The same. He addresses the matrons about to be captured by the Romans, that they may repent; or by women he marks the Synagogues, or the cities of Judea. Rich women, rise up: After the calling of the Gentiles, over whom Christ ruled in justice, the speech is directed to the rich women.
32.10: 32.10 After days and a year. Whence: Behold, now is the acceptable time, behold, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor. 6); and elsewhere: The acceptable year of the Lord (Isa. 61). After days. That is, the preaching of Christ. For those who were impenitent, though not immediately taken captive, were yet immediately troubled, because they would not receive the preaching of the Lord.
32.12: 32.12 Mourn over the breasts. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not over me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
32.14: 32.14 Of wild asses. The same. Of any wild animals and birds that dwelt there for a long time.
32.15: 32.15 Until the spirit be poured out. May the Holy Spirit, with Elijah and Enoch preaching, descend upon us, as at Pentecost upon the apostles. The prophet joins himself to them by compassion. The desert. The solitude of the Gentiles, namely, will be turned into the riches of Israel, and Israel will be reckoned among the Gentiles.
32.17: 32.17 And the service of justice. That we may pray in silence, not in the streets, not crying out, not with much speaking.
32.18: 32.18 In tabernacles. The same. Now he dwells confidently in the mansions of heaven, whence: In my Father's house there are many mansions (John 14); or in the Churches which hope confidently in the Lord.
32.19: 32.19 Hail, as if He said: When the Christian people sit in the beauty of peace, then the wrath of God will rage against the forest.
32.20: 32.20 Blessed are you who sow. The same. In the exposition of Ecclesiastes. That teacher is held worthy of blessedness who sows upon the watered heart of his hearers, a people gathered both from Jews and from Gentiles.
33.1: 33.1 Woe to you who plunder. The same. Against Sennacherib: these things can also be referred to any robber and to the devil himself.
33.2: 33.2 Lord, have mercy on us. The same. In the person of the people besieged by Sennacherib, or rather, of the apostles and all the faithful. In the morning. Those who remained of the army of Sennacherib saw their companions dead and were turned to flight.
33.3: 33.3 Of the angel. Of Michael, namely, who is the prince of the Jews, or of Gabriel, the strength and leader of battles.
33.4: 33.4 The caterpillar. The caterpillar is born of the locust, etc., up to: 'even the dead beget caterpillars.'
33.6: 33.6 Yours. O Hezekiah; or his, according to others, namely of the delivered people. His. JEROME. Namely of salvation: for without fear neither wisdom nor knowledge profits anything, whence: You shall have many good things if you fear God (Tob. 4); and: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord (Ps. 110).
33.8: 33.8 The covenant. Which the Lord made with Abraham, namely: I will multiply your seed as the stars, etc. (Gen. 22); and elsewhere: You shall dwell in this place from now and forever (Zech. 11).
33.9: 33.9 Lebanon. The temple; Bashan, the region of Og, which Moses gave beyond the Jordan to the two and a half tribes: this too is most fertile. Carmel, a mountain of the promised land, most fertile. By these, therefore, we should understand that the Jews have lost all fertility.
33.14: 33.14 Who shall be able. He relates the great works of God and calls God a fire.
33.17: 33.17 The land. Of the living. Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land; or, being placed in heaven, they despise earthly things.
33.20: 33.20 The tabernacle which. The same. The tabernacle which the Jews had through the desert, etc., up to: 'but the Church is founded immovable upon the firm rock.'
33.22: 33.22 For the Lord. The same. He will judge the world in justice.
33.23: 33.23 Your ropes are loosened, etc. He returns to the earthly Jerusalem and speaks of it under the figure of a ship: the things said above were of the city of our solemnity, which the Lord surrounds with His rivers.
34.4: 34.4 All the host of heaven. JEROME. The sun, moon, and stars will seem to be darkened, the true light, which is Christ, shining forth. The evil spirits too, having lost power, will be shut up in hell. And they shall be rolled up like a book. Not the inner, namely, etc., up to: 'for nothing will afterward be written in them.'
34.6: 34.6 In Bozrah. The same. In the city of the world fortified against God. For Bozrah means fortified, or from God; for the world is made firm by the will of the Lord; whence: He has founded it upon the seas; and: I have established its pillars. The teachers of the Hebrews want Bozrah and Edom to be understood as Rome, and everything to be said of her that is contained in the following chapter.
34.8: 34.8 For it is the day of the Lord's vengeance, the year of recompense. After the general vengeance of the world, he returns to Jerusalem, to whom he first spoke, and describes in plain speech her destruction, which was done by the Romans.
34.11: 34.11 The ibis. A water bird, enemy of serpents: Josephus says that Moses brought these birds into the war against the Ethiopians, because serpents abound in that land through which he was about to go.
34.12: 34.12 Her nobles. For the apostles had already passed to the Gentiles; other faithful, by the admonition of the Holy Spirit, with captivity imminent, crossed the Jordan into the kingdom of Agrippa, who had peace with the Romans.
35.1: 35.1 It shall be glad. The captivity of the Jews having been set out, he treats of the conversion of the Gentiles.
35.2: 35.2 Sharon. The peoples of the Jews; whence: Sharon shall be like a desert (Isa. 32).
35.7: 35.7 The greenness of the reed. The fulfillment of the Scripture, which is through the reed (pen); and the help of intention, which is through the rush: for the reed and the rush spring up and are green beside the waters.
36.1: 36.1 And it came to pass. JEROME. The books of Kings and Chronicles agree, etc., up to: 'he besieged Jerusalem.'
36.3: 36.3 Shebna. The same. Shebna the scribe, another, not the proud one, who, as the Hebrews relate, terrified by the threat of Rabshakeh, handed over the lower part of the city, the citadel and the temple remaining.
36.4: 36.4 Thus says. As perhaps he had heard from his father, Thus says the Lord: and that his words may have greater weight, he marks arrogance: Thus says the great king, as it were a contrary power.
36.6: 36.6 Behold, you trust. The same. He plainly lies. For nowhere is it read that Hezekiah put his hope in Egypt.
36.8: 36.8 Nor will you be able. Not from weakness, but by the observance of the commandments of the Lord, who through Moses commanded concerning the king of Israel, saying: You shall not multiply horses and chariots for yourself, nor many wives.
36.16: 36.16 Make a blessing with me, etc. Praise me, bless me. Or as another edition has: Do what is useful to you, that you may receive me and peace may remain with you.
37.1: 37.1 And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments. The same. They tear their garments because they had heard Rabshakeh blaspheming. The king tore his, believing that this came about from his sins and those of the people.
37.2: 37.2 Isaiah son of Amoz. In the book of Kings it is read: who sent to Isaiah the prophet. But here, because Isaiah wrote the history of himself, he names himself not the prophet but the son of the prophet.
37.4: 37.4 For the remnants. For the ten tribes had already been led away, the cities of Judah and Benjamin laid waste; the lower part of the city also had been handed over into the hands of the enemy by the impious and proud high official Shebna. Lift up your eyes, etc.
37.7: 37.7 Behold, I will give him a spirit, etc. As if He said: I will not tell all that I will do to the Assyrian, lest I seem to boast of my power, but this one thing: Behold, I will give.
37.8: 37.8 And he found. That Sennacherib king of the Assyrians fought against the Egyptians, etc., up to: 'the writers of Chaldean history.'
37.15: 37.15 He prayed. JEROME. Now more secure about deliverance. For before he went up, but it is not read that he prayed, because he feared that this would be on account of his sins.
37.18: 37.18 For truly, Lord: it is proved by many histories that the kings of the Persians came into Greece and overthrew and plundered temples.
37.21: 37.21 And he sent. The history of the book of Kings and Chronicles is mixed with the prophecy, because it is a prophecy about the deliverance of the city, the destruction of the Assyrian, the return of the sun, and the added years of Hezekiah.
37.22: 37.22 Daughter of Jerusalem. Who had not answered before, now certain of vengeance, secure about the punishment.
37.25: 37.25 And I dried up. So great was the army that they dried up the streams, and therefore made wells by lack of water.
37.29: 37.29 Pride. The same. I will no longer endure, that you may know that you could not do these things by your own strength, but by my decision. For the impious nations and fruitless trees deserved to be cut down through you as by an axe.
37.30: 37.30 But to you. The same. All these things the Prophet speaks to Hezekiah through messengers, what Sennacherib said, what the Lord answered him: now he turns the words to Hezekiah himself, that he may not doubt the things to come which he foretold. For in this the prophets were chiefly believed, that they testified of things not only far in the future but to be fulfilled soon. And in the year. Namely, with the harvest imminent, the Assyrians rushed in and laid waste the harvests and vineyards and olive groves: and because of the extreme siege, what was found of the grain they had for food in the first year and the second; for since in the year of the siege they could not sow, they took what they found of fruits and crops.
37.33: 37.33 Therefore. The same. He returns to his purpose, and after the hope of future things shakes off present fear. For the joy will not be so great over the things he promised for the future as the care over the things at hand.
37.35: 37.35 For my own sake. It signifies that they are preserved not by their own merit but by the clemency of God, and indeed by the memory of their father David. In this they are reminded of their negligence, and of that man's faith and justice, which God loves so much that He protects the descendants of saints for their merit.
37.37: 37.37 And returning. He was reserved for this, that he might know the power of God, and that blasphemers might close their mouths, and he might proclaim the majesty of Him whom he had before despised.
37.38: 37.38 His sons. Envious, according to the tradition of the Jews, Esarhaddon, etc., up to: 'reserved to be slain by his sons in the temple of his god.' Ararat. JEROME. A region of Armenia, a plain through which the Araxes flows, of incredible fertility, at the foot of Mount Taurus, which stretches there. The ark of Noah was not carried to the mountains of Armenia in general, which is called Ararat, but to the very high mountains of Taurus, which overhang the plains of Ararat.
38.1: 38.1 In those days he was sick. JEROME. Because for the victory he did not render thanks worthy of God, but vanished away in pride, as the book of Kings and Chronicles makes clear; whence: Whom God loves, He chastises, lest he be lifted up in pride after incredible triumphs. You shall die. Like which: Nineveh shall be overthrown: and many things are foretold under threat that are not fulfilled; not that God changes His sentence, but He calls us to the knowledge of Himself. For the Lord is patient over malice.
38.2: 38.2 To the wall. The same. Of the temple, namely, beside which Solomon built the palace.
38.3: 38.3 I beseech You, Lord. About to go to the Lord, he recounts his works. Happy is the conscience that in a time of evils can recall good things. I beseech You, Lord. Hearing that he is to die, he does not ask for many years, but leaves it to God's judgment what He wishes to grant: he knew that Solomon pleased God because he had not asked for longer years of life. And what is good. He destroyed the idols of his father, opened the doors of the house of the Lord which that one had closed, broke in pieces the bronze serpent which the Jews worshipped at Gibeon, and scattered it to the wind. And he wept. He wept because he was dying without sons, etc., up to: 'and we read that very many were raised after death.'
38.4: 38.4 And the Word of the Lord came. In a reversed order the history is related here, which is read more consecutively in the volume of Kings.
38.5: 38.5 Behold, I will add to your days. According to what seemed, etc., up to: 'and concerning the added years of Hezekiah.'
38.7: 38.7 And this shall be a sign to you from the Lord, that the Lord will do this word which He has spoken. The same. Of the present time, that is, and of the future, so that as the sun returns to its beginning, so the life of Hezekiah may return to years already run. For us also, living in the seventh and eighth after the resurrection of Christ, may the spans of life be prolonged.
38.10: 38.10 I said. The same. When God had given Hezekiah victory without labor, etc., up to: 'sinners die in the midst of their days.' In the midst of my days. Whence: Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days, because they do not fulfill works of virtue, nor amend their faults by penance. To the gates of hell. I sought. Where the house is appointed for every living man before the coming of Christ.
38.11: 38.11 Of rest. Some codices have: My generation has rested, which Jerome also once translated, deceived by the ambiguity of the word, and afterward corrected.
38.15: 38.15 He will answer me. The same. What I have erred in I will amend; be You surety and protector: For it is not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy (Rom. 9). When he himself. These things justly to me, as if he said: nothing remains but to endure patiently and entreat the strong One Himself, who did what He willed. I will think over. What is past does not help the one enduring; whence foolish is the opinion of Epicurus, who asserts that present evils are mitigated by the recollection of past goods. In the bitterness of my soul, as if he said: and these also are in bitterness, because present tribulation feels nothing of past good, and human happiness is always sprinkled with some adversities.
38.18: 38.18 For hell shall not confess. The damned without end neither do penance in hell nor render praises to God.
38.19: 38.19 The living, the living, etc. Not hell or death. The father to the children. Whence: Ask your father, and he will declare to you, etc.
38.21: 38.21 Upon his wound. The Hebrews say that Sehin means an ulcer, not a wound, etc., up to: 'when God has made it.'
39.1: 39.1 At that time. JEROME. It was said above that Esarhaddon succeeded Sennacherib, etc., up to: 'and, having lost manly strength, he is reduced to womanly softness.'
39.2: 39.2 And in all his power. The same. In the treasures of the house of the Lord, in which he chiefly offended. For this was not in his power. Yet he had already taken plates of gold from those doors of the temple. In his treasures. He is silent about the treasures of the Lord, fearing to be rebuked, namely that he showed them whatever he had in his power, the furniture of the temple, that is; whence:
39.7: 39.7 And they shall be eunuchs. The same. The Hebrews relate that this was fulfilled in Daniel and his companions, who, Joachim son of Josiah being taken, were taken with his people and led to Babylon and made eunuchs, or unmanned; yet it is not to be thought that they were eunuchs in body, but in mind, like those who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven (Matt. 19).
39.8: 39.8 Only let there be peace. He ought to have confessed his sin with David and removed the wrath of God from his descendants, or have shared in suffering with Moses, who says: Forgive them this fault, or blot me out of the book which You have written (Exod. 32). Because he did not do this, therefore He does not answer him; but, turning to the people, says: Comfort, etc.
40.1: 40.1 Comfort. As if He said: Because your king does not sympathize with you, be comforted in Christ. It can be referred to the Gentiles, of whom the Lord says through Zechariah: I will gather the people of the east, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God (Zech. 8). Speak to the heart. JEROME. He speaks to the heart who comforts the sorrowful, as it is said of Shechem: Shechem spoke to her heart and comforted her (Gen. 24). Jerusalem. Jerusalem by the Chaldeans and Romans in body and soul; the Church by persecutors, tormented in body, distressed in mind. Her malice. Malice means affliction, as in: If there is evil in the city which the Lord has not done (Amos 3). Is put away. The cause of comfort, the remission of sins, etc., up to: 'because they are purged and loosed through punishments.'
40.3: 40.3 The voice of one crying. The same. Mindful of this voice, the Jews sent to John to ask him: Who are you?
40.4: 40.4 Every valley shall be exalted. He who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself, etc. The teachers cry this to this day in the desert of the churches of the Gentiles.
40.5: 40.5 And all flesh shall see. Being suddenly carried from the first coming to the second, he says: And all flesh shall see. The mouth of the Lord. The prophets who preached the coming Christ, namely the salvation of our God.
40.6: 40.6 What shall I cry? The same. Not without cause does he ask: for when he offered himself willingly, saying: Behold, here I am, send me, he announced hard things to his people, and now he fears the same. All flesh. He who bears the image of the earthly, etc., up to: 'so man, through the succession of ages, loses beauty and falls into death.'
40.8: 40.8 But the Word of the Lord. The Word is Christ with His body, which is the Church.
40.9: 40.9 Zion. The same. By Zion and Jerusalem he understands the apostles and other teachers, whom he admonishes to preach what they have received from the Lord, and, ascending the heights of virtues, to teach by word and example.
40.11: 40.11 His flock, etc. Now in contemplation, in the future in the vision itself: now by teaching, afterward by saving or satisfying. Those with young. The teachers daily giving birth to children for God.
40.12: 40.12 Who has measured? The same. Lest there be doubt about the calling of the Gentiles, the greatness of the One who calls is described. In his fist. The fist, with the fingers drawn together, a clenched hand; the palm, the hand stretched out from the thumb to the little finger, so that by the palm and the fist we may know the heavens stretched out and the globe of the earth.
40.13: 40.13 The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He has anointed me to preach to the meek; He has sent me: And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.
40.15: 40.15 As a small dust. The same. The Hebrews think that by this word the finest dust is signified, etc., up to: 'and the poverty of both the Greek and the Latin tongue.'
40.16: 40.16 Lebanon shall not be enough. Lebanon is a very great mountain, most rich in pastures and trees; but even if all the trees were cut down for burning, and all the animals sacrificed as a holocaust, they would not suffice to fulfill or appease the power of the Majesty.
40.19: 40.19 Surely. He rebukes the folly of the Gentiles, that they may withdraw from idolatry.
40.20: 40.20 Perhaps wood. The same. In Hebrew mesuchan, because it is a kind of wood that does not rot, of which idols are chiefly made: he says this so that, idols being rejected, the doctrine of the Gospel may be received and the glory of the Lord revealed, that all flesh may see the salvation of God.
40.21: 40.21 From the beginning. Of the law of Moses, or from the beginning of the world in the creatures themselves, which all in their own way proclaim their Maker.
40.22: 40.22 Above the circle. From this some contend that the earth is as a point and a globe. As locusts. In comparison with Him, or considering the greatness of the earth. A tent. From this too they contend that the heaven is in the likeness of a sphere, and that its hemisphere hangs over the lands.
40.23: 40.23 Who gives searchers of secrets. God has made foolish the wisdom of this world, and this is: Who gives searchers of secrets as though they were not (1 Cor. 1).
40.25: 40.25 To whom have you likened Me, or made Me equal, says the Holy One. As if He said: Why do you compare God to a likeness, and do not understand God the Creator from the greatness of creatures? If you do not believe words, believe your eyes, and think of the omnipotence of the Lord from the service of all the elements.
40.26: 40.26 By number. The same. To Him are numbered the things which Abraham could not number: and they serve their appointed office, as the sun completes the course of heaven in one year, and the rest in their own way. Their host, etc. The angels, namely, whence: Thousands of thousands ministered to Him (Dan. 7). Hence He is also called Lord Sabaoth, that is, of the host, or of armies, or of powers.
40.27: 40.27 Why do you say, etc. The same. When the prophet said these things, etc., up to: 'we are without a judge, and are afflicted undeservedly.' My way. Good works; earthly things do not pertain to God, He does not consider what each one does. Hence one is unjustly oppressed, like beasts and fish, without a ruler.
40.28: 40.28 He created. He knows all things, contains all things, dispenses all things by His majesty. His wisdom. The same. From this place the apostle seems to have taken another saying: His judgments are incomprehensible, and His ways unsearchable; as if He said: God alone is eternal and impassible; all else will fail.
40.30: 40.30 The boys shall faint. Who, namely, rejoice in bodily health and think boyhood and youth to be perpetual.
40.31: 40.31 They shall change. That they may be strong in God, they will become weak to the world, and after the death of the flesh will become immortal. Like eagles. As the eagle, according to the naturalists, by striking its beak, hooked from excessive age, against a flint, is renewed, so they who mortify the old age of sin through the rock, which is Christ, being dead to the world are renewed for God, whence: Your youth shall be renewed like the eagle's (Ps. 102).
41.1: 41.1 Let the islands keep silence. JEROME. Because the nations are in the salty deep, namely, those who are beaten by the salt and bitter waves of the world.
41.2: 41.2 Who raised up from the east. The same. Some of the Hebrews refer this to Cyrus king of the Persians, etc., up to: 'who knew these things from the beginning.'
41.3: 41.3 The path under his feet. He will not feel the labor or weariness of that life: He rejoiced as a giant to run the way.
41.5: 41.5 The islands saw. The same. That is, the nations round about, etc., up to: 'and strengthened him with the key of the commandments, that he might remain in the fear of the Lord.'
41.8: 41.8 And you, Israel, my servant. The same. The Lord to the apostles with affection, etc., up to: 'afterward, chosen, we are joined in the friendship of God.'
41.9: 41.9 And from afar. The Jews are now scattered to the farthest parts, and from there many are called at the end.
41.14: 41.14 Worm of Jacob. The same. The apostles are called worms, as imitators of Him who says: I am a worm and no man (Ps. 21). And as a worm penetrates the earth, so their preaching penetrates the hearts of the hearers. You who are dead of Israel. Like him who says: I die daily for your glory, brethren (1 Cor. 15); and elsewhere: I live, now not I; but Christ lives in me (Gal. 2).
41.15: 41.15 I have made you as a wagon. The churchman has the beaks of preaching, etc., up to: 'that those badly gathered may be well divided.'
41.19: 41.19 I will give in the wilderness the cedar. The same. The varieties of trees signify the diversity of spiritual grace, so that not even one string of the Lord's harp, and no virtue of the graces, may seem lacking to the Church: whose loftiness, hastening to heavenly things, the olive tree illuminates, tinder of light, rest of the laboring or weary. The thorn, and the myrtle, and the olive tree. Septuagint: Sethim, which is a tree like the white thorn, etc., up to: 'and therefore it signifies the consolers of the holy Church.'
41.22: 41.22 Declare. The same. It signifies that idols have neither the faculty of hearing nor of answering, etc., up to: 'it is clear that idols lost their voice after the coming of Christ.'
41.23: 41.23 If you can. Neither can demons, save by God's permission, because they attend upon idols, since they could not destroy the swine, nor the beasts of holy Job, without God's permission. Paul also handed some over to Satan.
41.25: 41.25 I have raised up. The same. He still speaks against idols and their worshippers, etc., up to: 'that they may believe in Him who comes from the rising of the sun.'
41.26: 41.26 Who declared from the beginning? As if He said: There was none among the Gentiles who announced the coming of the Son. But if there is one who announced it, we will say, he is just; at the coming of the Son the demons, who in idols announced things to come, became mute. Hearing your words. Because the dull hearts of the Gentiles understood their error and abandoned false prophecies.
