41.27: 41.27 The first shall say to Zion. They signify the Church; behold, your sons stood by, namely yours, whom by my faith I gave to you, namely the apostles, by whose preaching sons were born to you.
41.29: 41.29 Behold, all are unjust. Whatever we have said of idols or of the Gentiles, let us refer to the heresiarchs and the doctrines of perversity, because, Christ announcing peace to the Church and showing the truth, they themselves follow errors, and are compared to wind and whirlwind.
42.1: 42.1 Behold my servant. JEROME. It should be noted that the apostles are called Jacob, Israel, and the seed of Abraham, to whom afterward, as to servants and men, it is said: Fear not, worm of Jacob, etc. But Christ is called not the seed of Jacob or Israel but servant. I have given the Spirit. In the conception; whence: The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, etc. (Phil. 2). And at the baptism it shone forth, when the Spirit in the form of a dove rested upon Him (Luke 1).
42.3: 42.3 Smoking flax. The priesthood now almost extinguished; the priestly vestment is made of linen. He shall bring forth judgment. He will judge, not fearing the Scribes and Pharisees.
42.4: 42.4 He shall not be sad. The same. Matthew did not include this, or between 'judgment' and 'judgment' the middle was removed by a scribe's error. The sense is: he will preserve an evenness of countenance at all times: the philosophers falsely boast this of Socrates, that he was no more sad or joyful than usual. Judgment on the earth. Whence: For judgment I have come into this world, that those who do not see may see, etc. (John 9).
42.6: 42.6 Justice. It was just that he should pass over through the apostles to the Gentiles, being rejected by the Jews.
42.7: 42.7 The bound. With the cords of sins: in the Gospel, the Lord looses him whom Satan had bound.
42.8: 42.8 To another. The Son and the Holy Spirit in the Godhead are not other than the Father, and therefore have the same glory and praise.
42.9: 42.9 To you I will do. That you may know that I am the Lord, there is no other besides me: and you who see the former things fulfilled may believe what I promise for the future.
42.10: 42.10 A new. In newness of the Spirit, not in the oldness of the letter; and not only in the Old Testament, but also in the New. You who go down to the sea. The same. First fishers of fishes, afterward of men; whence literally: they crossed many seas.
42.11: 42.11 Kedar. The son of Ishmael: from him the Saracens, or better the Hagarenes; but by the name of the free woman they covered the disgrace of the handmaid. For Ishmael was the son of the handmaid Hagar, from whom the Saracens. For he begot twelve chiefs. The province itself is also called by his name. From the top of the mountains. JEROME. Go up upon a high mountain. From the top of the mountain. From the height of virtue and contemplation, so that by example they may also teach what they preach.
42.13: 42.13 He shall cry aloud. Whence: They have provoked me with that which was not God (Deut. 32); and I will provoke them with a foolish nation.
42.14: 42.14 As a woman in labor. The birth of my counsel I will bring into the light like a woman her infant; so I will bring forth the concealed sorrow.
42.16: 42.16 In the paths. The same. In the knowledge of the prophets, who are the paths to Christ, when they preach His nativity, resurrection and ascension.
42.17: 42.17 Let them be confounded. When the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. Then Israel also, converted, will repent of its error, having formerly served idols.
42.22: 42.22 A snare of the young men. He returns to the preaching of the Lord, rebuking the Scribes and Pharisees: for these were snares to the simple, that they might not be converted to the Lord.
42.23: 42.23 Who is there. The prophet exhorts them, that at least some may hear, and understand the cause of their captivity, and beware.
42.25: 42.25 Upon him. So that what He had before kept silent He would no longer keep silent, but would rebuke not with words but with torments. And he did not know. As the histories relate, neither did the Gentiles understand that this was done in vengeance for the Son, nor the Jews, blinded by their malice.
43.1: 43.1 And now these things. Above he spoke of the captivity of the Jews who refused to believe; now he addresses the primitive Church, which is of the Jews, that they may understand the Creator of their soul and body. Creating you, Jacob. Jacob the supplanter, Israel the man seeing God. These are the apostles and apostolic men, who both supplanted vices and merited to see God.
43.2: 43.2 Through the waters, etc. The same. According to the Hebrews: The Egyptians through the waters, etc., up to: 'the apostles also passed through these kingdoms preaching, and the Lord everywhere with them.'
43.3: 43.3 I have given propitiation. That from it you may acquire for yourself mercy and a crown, by preaching, namely, to the Egyptians, and the Ethiopians who are almost the farthest, and the Sabeans: Saba is a city situated on the borders of Ethiopia: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and to the ends, etc.
43.5: 43.5 From the east. Many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from all parts of the world, that is.
43.8: 43.8 Bring forth. The voice of the Father to the Son concerning the Jews blind of mind. And note that the calling of the Jews was done first, then of the Gentiles.
43.9: 43.9 All nations. The prophet to the Gentiles, rebuking them for idolatry and marveling that none among the Gentiles could foreknow this, but only the people of God who received the law of God and had prophets.
43.10: 43.10 Was not formed. Some codices have plasmatus; but it does not fit well; yet it can be explained thus: Before me no idol was formed, because I made man just, by whom the idol was unjustly formed.
43.12: 43.12 I have declared and saved. Through the prophets the nativity of the Son, the calling of the Gentiles, the expulsion of demons.
43.14: 43.14 Thus says the Lord your Savior, etc. These things, namely those that follow: the Father to the apostles. For your sake, who are my witnesses, who preach the Gospel. To whom He said: Fear not. The Chaldeans in ships. According to the history, the Chaldeans abound in rivers, and are vigorous in ships, and boast of this.
43.15: 43.15 I am the Lord your Holy One. Formerly to the children of Israel, now to you, apostles, in the world, demons being cast out and all princes conquered.
43.19: 43.19 I make new things. Many that refresh souls, not bodies: of old I brought forth from the rock only one fountain to refresh bodies.
43.20: 43.20 Dragons and ostriches. The malignant, the venomous, who dwelt in the solitude of the Gentiles, beastly with the blood of idolatry and the ferocity of their customs. The ostrich has the appearance of wings, but lacks flight. So the hypocrite has the appearance of holiness, but not the reality.
43.22: 43.22 You have not called upon me. JEROME. He speaks to the Jews, who worshipped idols before the coming of the Lord; or to those who after the coming refused to believe. Nor have you labored. I did not make you labor after the coming of the Son, to offer every costly thing, because: A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit, etc. (Ps. 50). Or: You have not labored for me alone, you who offered to idols.
43.23: 43.23 In incense. By incense and the sweet cane, which is the shoot of an aromatic tree, understand all aromatics.
43.25: 43.25 I am. The same. As if He said: You made me labor under the burden of your sin; therefore I no longer call you my servant, nor my boy, but simply call you Jacob and Israel, to show and rebuke sinners.
43.26: 43.26 Bring me back. The good things that I did for you. What more ought I to have done for you, and have not done? Or: If you have anything just, I will gladly receive it.
43.27: 43.27 Your father. Abraham, namely, who, when the Lord promised the land of promise, answered: Whereby shall I know that I shall possess it? Or Abraham himself, who is said to have sinned in doubting the promise of a son; or the people in the desert murmuring against God, as if He said: he will know that he is begotten of sinners. Interpreters. As if He said: between parties, namely those bringing peace.
44.1: 44.1 And now hear, Jacob. He addresses the first believers from among the Jews, the others being hardened, with a certain privilege of name and dignity of honor; namely, the chorus of the apostles. Hear, Jacob my servant. The first is service, the second election.
44.2: 44.2 Your helper from the womb. In which you seized your brother's heel, or, in the beginning of the Church you escaped the hands of persecutors. And most righteous whom I have chosen. Israel, according to the Hebrew truth, upright or most upright. What was said before, 'a man seeing God,' is held not from the property of the word but from the sound of the voice.
44.3: 44.3 I will pour out my Spirit. Namely in baptism by the laying on of hands.
44.4: 44.4 Like willows beside the flowing waters. The willow is an unfruitful tree, etc., up to: 'which quickly believed the preaching apostles.'
44.5: 44.5 This one shall say. He describes the variety of believers. And shall be likened in the name of Israel. That they may receive the law, and the prophets, and the graces of the Holy Spirit which were promised to Israel.
44.6: 44.6 I am the first and I am the last. After the calling of the Gentiles, who, idols being cast away, believed, he speaks against those who refused to be converted. Besides me there is no God. He does not say that He alone exists, but that apart from His power and wisdom there is no foreign God, condemning the opinion of many gods and images.
44.12: 44.12 He shall hunger and faint. JEROME. By the hunger and thirst of the craftsman, etc., up to: 'whose god is the belly, and their glory is in their shame.'
44.23: 44.23 Shout for joy, ends of the earth. The same. The angels preside, as it were, over the inhabitants of the earth; or the apostles, or the prophets, over whom others also stand; whence to the Ephesians it is said: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, etc.
44.24: 44.24 Thus says the Lord your Redeemer, etc. The same. Above he spoke of the overthrow of idols and the redemption of penitent Israel; now of the greatness of his power, that no one may doubt the salvation he promises.
44.26: 44.26 Who say. He speaks of the restoration which was made by Zerubbabel and other leaders, Cyrus permitting; though the captivity was yet to be fulfilled.
44.27: 44.27 Your rivers. Under Darius, namely, and Cyrus his grandson. For on the night in which Belshazzar was slain by them, the river Euphrates, which flowed through the middle of the city, was divided by their army into streams, so that they entered the city by its bed.
45.1: 45.1 Thus says the Lord to his Christ. Among the Romans the diadem, among the Jews the anointing, makes both kings and priests, from which they are also called christs. Cyrus is a christ, not by anointing but by dignity. And the backs of kings. The same. What city did not lie open to him? Which of the kings did not turn his back? What walls, formerly impregnable, were not overthrown by his siege? You will find these things more fully fulfilled in the history of Xenophon.
45.3: 45.3 Hidden treasures. Of all the cities, that, idols being cast aside, invited by benefits, you might perceive the one God, who foretold your name before you were.
45.4: 45.4 And I have called you. The same. As I called Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, etc., up to: 'but the Son, Christ, anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows.'
45.5: 45.5 Besides me. Because the Son and the Holy Spirit are in the Father; for apart from my Word and reason and power and wisdom which is in me, there is no other God.
45.6: 45.6 That they may know. Ezra says that Cyrus wrote to all nations that there is no God but the God of Israel. Or, from the liberation of the captives the clemency and power of God were made better known to all. Josephus, in the book of Antiquities, says that the people were released for this reason, that Cyrus read in the book of Isaiah what the Lord had said of him beforehand through the prophet.
45.7: 45.7 Darkness. Night or captivity. As taking pity on penitents I bring them back from captivity; angry with sinners I make them captive. Evil. The same. War, namely affliction, according to what is said: Sufficient for the day is its own evil. Let them therefore be confounded who think God the maker of evils. For here evil is put not as the contrary of good but for affliction and war.
45.8: 45.8 Drop down dew, you heavens. The same. He fittingly adds this concerning the coming of Christ, signified by Cyrus, because He will free the human race from the captivity of the devil. Or these things can cohere with what goes before, so that, Cyrus releasing the captivity, heaven and earth may rejoice by metonymy. And the clouds. The prophets, watering our hearts with saving rain, and announcing the nativity and resurrection and ascension of Christ, whence: I will command my clouds that they rain no rain upon it; and elsewhere, Your truth reaches to the clouds. I have created him who: namely, he who was a worm, and is read to have sprung from the earth according to his humanity.
45.9: 45.9 Woe to him who contradicts: as if He said: Believe what I preach, namely that Christ will come, because, Woe to him who contradicts his maker (Ps. 35); or Cyrus, under whom, by the liberation of my people, I will subject all kingdoms.
45.10: 45.10 To the woman, what do you bring forth? The husband has power over the wife, the wife over the husband.
45.11: 45.11 His maker, of the Son, according to humanity in the virginal womb, whence: The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you, etc.
45.12: 45.12 And to all the host. On this occasion some think the stars are rational; for they say that He would not command things senseless, which would not understand the commands.
45.13: 45.13 I have raised up. The same. As if He said: I who have done the above things, what wonder if I also send the Son into the world to redeem the human race and raise Him from the dead? I will direct his ways. Who did no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth (1 Pet. 2). He shall build. The same. Of whom it was said: You have not known me. Neither did he himself build the city or temple, but permitted them to be built; nor was it completed in his time, but in that of Ahasuerus.
45.14: 45.14 The labor of Egypt. The worship of idols. For it labored much in carrying out the sacrifices of idols. But, the apostles preaching, they were converted, and above all kingdoms the religious orders of monks abound there, that where sin abounded, grace may abound the more (Rom. 5).
45.19: 45.19 Not in secret, etc. The same. Of old on Mount Sinai He spoke to one people only: You shall have no strange gods (Exod. 20). But the Gospel He preached through the apostles to all nations, whence: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth (Ps. 18). I have not said. JEROME. First, indeed, I came to the Jews; and I admonished them, leaving the shadow of the law, to follow the truth. Declaring right things. That the creature may adore the Creator, that, figures being left, it may follow the truth of the Gospel.
45.20: 45.20 They have not known. Some remaining in error were unwilling to know, burdened with the load of images, and hoping in those in whom there is no salvation.
45.21: 45.21 Take counsel. That all, going through the world, may announce the same. For hence they together composed the Creed, about the Trinity and unity, the communion of the Church, the general resurrection. I have foretold it. That the Gentiles are to be saved, but the idol is nothing: when I spoke to Abraham, or when I gave the law.
45.23: 45.23 It shall go forth: into the world visibly in the flesh. The word of justice, the Son, until He has fulfilled obedience, etc., up to: 'which the Jews, showing pride of mind, do not do at all.'
45.25: 45.25 In the Lord he shall say. All nations, even the barbarian, confessing not in synagogues but in the Churches.
46.1: 46.1 Bel is broken. JEROME. After the calling of the Gentiles, the destruction of idols is added. Nebo. Nebo is gold, etc., up to: 'and the prophecy of demons and the divination of magicians came to nothing.' Beasts and cattle. The same. For they adored beasts and cattle, and their region gave to most towns names from the beasts and cattle they adored, as Leonata from the lion, and others of the kind.
46.2: 46.2 And their soul. Not that the images have a soul, etc., up to: 'which he subjected to the devil and demons.'
46.3: 46.3 House of Jacob. He does not say Jacob, my servant, my elect, with an addition of honor, but simply: and addresses them as carnal and withdrawing from his commandments. Who are carried. Who are borne like offspring conceived through the desert to the land of promise. For He waited for them patiently a long time, both in the land of promise, and after the Passion for forty-two years.
46.5: 46.5 To whom have you likened? He inveighs chiefly against those who in the time of Ahaz and Ezekiel worshipped idols in the corners of the streets, in gardens, in groves, on the housetops.
46.8: 46.8 Remember this. Because I begot you and carried you to old age, forsake the idols you have made, and return to the worship of the one God. To the heart. To understanding, you who have lived like beasts, venerating images, like madmen striking against wood and stones.
46.10: 46.10 Declaring. Through the prophets, that when I have fulfilled the things foretold through divination, that is, a prophet foretelling the future, I may prove my divinity. The last. We are those upon whom the ends of the ages have come (1 Cor. 10). And elsewhere: But when the fullness of time came, God sent His Son (Gal. 4). And John: Little children, he says, it is the last hour (1 John 2). Counsel: of redeeming the world through the Son; as if, I now state my counsel as fixed, that when you see the effect, you may know that there is no God but He who knew the future and commanded it to be done.
46.11: 46.11 Calling a bird from the east: The same. According to the Hebrews, Cyrus king of the Persians, etc., up to: 'and whom the Magi coming from the east adored.'
46.12: 46.12 Hard of heart. You who always resist the truth, first the prophets, at last the Son also.
47.1: 47.1 Come down, sit, etc. JEROME. Because we are all creatures of God; nor, according to the heretics, is the nature of Babylon damnable; or on account of the luxury and adornment of a most powerful city, which, already old and near its setting, boasts itself a little maiden and girl.
47.2: 47.2 Meal, or offer intercourse to the Medes and Persians, who are most ardent in this. According to this the Hebrews say that the Philistines made Samson, his eyes put out, grind, that is, have intercourse with their women, so that from him they might beget men of great and invincible stature.
47.3: 47.3 And he shall not resist, as Moses to God willing to destroy the children of Israel. It signifies the angel set over Babylon, who with the others says: We have healed Babylon, and she is not healed.
47.5: 47.5 Sit. The speech is addressed to Babylon, and as once a queen, now a handmaid, he addresses her. Sit humble and lowly. Be silent as one sad, considering your misery.
47.6: 47.6 I was angry. He gives the reason why he so afflicted the Chaldeans, lest he seem to have done it without cause, who does nothing without cause; and that the Chaldeans may know that they did not overcome the people of God by their own strength.
47.9: 47.9 Suddenly. Unexpectedly, Cyrus and Darius rushing in. For she did not fear that she could be overcome by the Medes and Persians, who in comparison with her were of no strength and subject to her.
47.11: 47.11 You shall not know the rising. Calamity will come unexpectedly, foretold neither by magicians nor diviners, for they did not fear a despised and subject people.
47.13: 47.13 Augurs of heaven. Astrologers, who think that all things are governed by the stars. As if He said: Did they not provide all things for you? These are commonly called mathematicians, who think that worldly affairs are ruled by the course of the stars, whence: Magi came from the east, saying: We have seen his star in the east (Matt. 2). Or, provoked by the prophecy of Balaam, who said: A star shall rise out of Jacob (Num. 24).
47.14: 47.14 They are become as stubble, etc. Septuagint: Having coals of fire, you shall sit upon them, these shall be a help to you. As if: Gazarenes and magi lead you by error to pride. But the burning of Babylon calls through punishments to repentance.
48.1: 48.1 Hear this. JEROME. It is the custom that when carnal Israel is treated, Jacob or Israel is said simply and without addition to the name, as in this place, where he addresses those who are called Jacob or Israel only in name. And from the waters of Judah. He mentions Judah because, ten tribes having been taken captive, Judah and Benjamin and the Levites remained in the land of promise, and had a king from Judah.
48.2: 48.2 For of the holy city. The same. As if he said: You boast that you are inhabitants of Jerusalem and have the privilege of the Lord of hosts, when you take to yourselves vainly the names of Jacob, Israel, and of the holy city of Almighty God.
48.3: 48.3 The former things from then. I foretold that the Babylonians would be overcome, and I will suddenly do what I threatened: that when what was foretold has come, you may know that it happened neither by chance nor by the nod of your gods. The former miracles, namely those which I did in their midst since they came out of Egypt, and with the captivity under Nebuchadnezzar imminent: but now, before they are taken captive, he foretells their liberation and the devastation of the Chaldeans; whence suddenly, namely, I have wrought the things I foretell are to come.
48.4: 48.4 Neck an iron sinew. Hence Stephen: stiff-necked and uncircumcised in hearts (Acts 17). Your forehead brass: whence Ezekiel: For all the house of Israel is of a hardened forehead (Ezek. 3), etc. And Jeremiah: You had a harlot's forehead, you refused to be ashamed (Jer. 3).
48.6: 48.6 And they are kept. As if he said: I was about to announce very many things, but because you do not remember what I say, I reserve what I was about to say.
48.9: 48.9 For my name's sake. Namely, that it be not violated: I will put far off; I did: namely my fury, that I might not destroy you, because you adored the calf: and with my praise, namely that you should praise me: I will restrain you by my law.
48.10: 48.10 In the furnace of poverty. The same. Purging by poverty, giving your riches to enemies; or in Egypt, where it is shown that most are tried by riches and poverty.
48.12: 48.12 Hear me, Jacob. JEROME. He still speaks to the same, etc., up to: 'but calls those who are called.'
48.14: 48.14 Assemble all of you. Why then does earth and ash, ignorant of its own frailty, glory? He has announced these things. That Cyrus would destroy Babylon, or that my Son would be born of a virgin. The Lord loved him. These properly pertain to Christ. They can, however, be referred to Cyrus and to Darius up to that place: His way is made straight. His: because he shall take it. Or, the Son in the world to be redeemed, who also cast out the Chaldeans, namely demons, whence: The prince of this world shall be cast out.
48.15: 48.15 I have called him. Cyrus, or the Son, through Gabriel saying: And you shall call his name Jesus.
48.16: 48.16 Has sent me. The same. He distinguishes the whole Trinity briefly, fully and openly.
48.17: 48.17 I am the Lord. Who promise future things to Israel. He gives the reason why he afflicted them before.
48.21: 48.21 They thirsted not. The same. Literally, of those coming from Egypt, etc., up to: 'satisfied with the water of wisdom.' He cleft the rock. The rock was Christ. The divine word is cleft into parts, so that what we cannot receive whole we may take in parts. And the waters flowed. One of the soldiers opened His side with a lance, and immediately there came forth the blood of our redemption, and the water of baptism, dedicating to us baptism and martyrdom.
49.1: 49.1 Hear, O islands. JEROME. After the calling of the remnant of Israel and the rejection of the unbelievers, of whom, There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord, under the name of islands he addresses, in the person of the Son, the Churches from the Gentiles.
49.2: 49.2 A sharp sword. I came not to send peace but a sword (Matt. 10), separating the wicked from the good.
49.3: 49.3 I will glory. Which is not in other servants: Father, I have glorified your name (John 17). And elsewhere: Arise, my glory (Ps. 56), etc.
49.4: 49.4 And I said. The same. As if he said: How have I glorified you, who could not recall to you a great part of the Jews? Here man's free will is shown: for it belongs to God to call, to us to believe, yet with His help, that the just may obtain the reward of the will. Therefore my judgment, etc. The same. The Father will judge whether I have done for them all that I ought: I have manifested your name to the men whom you have given me. And elsewhere: I have glorified you on the earth (John 17). My work. Others: My labor and my sorrow: because he wept over the city, and said in the Psalm: What profit is there in my blood? (Ps. 29). According to the Hebrew, hanging on the cross, far from my salvation are the words of my lamentations.
49.5: 49.5 Glorified. As if he said: I have lost the Jews, but I am glorified among the Gentiles, whence, All power is given to me in heaven and on earth (Matt. 28).
49.7: 49.7 The abominated. Christ and his Nazarenes, whom the Jews daily curse in the synagogues, because on their account they lost kingdom, place and nation. Kings. The prophet to the Son. Kings shall see you coming to judgment: Kings, namely the apostles and others who will judge with the Lord.
49.8: 49.8 In an acceptable time. Of the Passion, of the Resurrection, in which it pleased God to redeem the human race.
49.16: 49.16 Behold, in my hands, etc. The same. From this we learn that Jerusalem is not to be sought in the region of Palestine: which, the worst of the whole province and roughened by rocky mountains, suffers a lack of springs.
49.17: 49.17 Builders. The apostles and others: By the fault of the Jews, that is, of the Scribes and Pharisees, you were destroyed; by the preaching of certain Jews, that is, of the apostles, you were gathered both from Jews and from Gentiles.
49.18: 49.18 All these gathered. Jews from every nation, etc., up to: 'are daily gathered to the faith of the Church.' With an ornament. With the various graces of the Holy Spirit, by which the splendor of the bride is adorned, of whom it is said: The queen stood at your right hand in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety (Ps. 44).
49.21: 49.21 I am barren. Because after Haggai, and Zechariah, and Malachi, who is also Ezra, they had no prophets to nourish them in the law, until John the Baptist.
49.23: 49.23 Queens. The same, but more affectionately. Whence: The queen stood, etc. Who daily nourishes the little ones of Christ and leads them to perfect age. They shall adore. They shall venerate, according to that: They will adore his footstool (Ps. 98), in which foot majesty is signified. The dust of your feet. JEROME. All earthliness, namely, they will cleanse by word and example, according to what was said, Whatever you shall loose upon earth shall be loosed (Matt. 16), etc., whence: Shake off the dust of your feet (Matt. 10).
49.25: 49.25 For thus says the Lord. The same. He answers the question, that these things will be fulfilled at his coming.
49.26: 49.26 With their own flesh. Not by another's death, but by their own, etc., up to: 'lying open to the bites of fierce beasts.' The strong one of Jacob. Who gave strength to Jacob for wrestling, etc., up to: 'as if also by prayer you shall prevail against Esau whom you fear.'
50.1: 50.1 Thus says the Lord: Who is it? JEROME. After the calling of the Gentiles, after the capture of the strong one, whose prey was divided among the apostles, he speaks to the people of the Jews upon Zion, which above says: The Lord has forsaken me, etc. I sold. But I am carnal, sold under sin (Rom. 7). He who commits sin is a slave of sin (John 8). Whence: Let not sin reign in your mortal body (Rom. 6).
50.2: 50.2 Because I came. The same. This is that you may know that I did not repudiate your mother, but that she withdrew by her own will: after many benefits I assumed flesh, and no longer through the prophets, but present I Myself spoke. There was no man. For Herod because of malice, etc., up to: 'concerning all in common: The vision of the four-footed beasts in the desert (Isa. 30).' I called. As if he said: Rational ones, Incline your ear to the words of my mouth (Ps. 77). He who thirsts, let him come and drink (John 8), and the like. Is it not? The same. He inveighs against those who thought, etc., up to: 'that he may present to me more than twelve legions of angels? (Matt. 26).'
2.16: 2.16 Ships. The same. Jehoshaphat had ships which he sent to Tarshish, etc., up to: 'there are also good ships, of which it is said: They who go down to the sea in ships,' etc. Tarshish. The same. Of any sea whatever, etc., up to: 'if it is said otherwise, it is Syriac.'
2.17: 2.17 Every man shall be bowed down. The same. Allegorically: human speech seems rational, etc., up to: 'they would also be utterly crushed by that by which they had been fashioned.'
2.18: 2.18 And the idols utterly. This in the captivity of the Chaldeans, etc., up to: 'this is to be referred especially to the former sense.' BEDE. Solomon built at Jerusalem a thing for Ashtoreth, the idol of the Sidonians, etc., where, unless I am mistaken, it is shown that Solomon never repented perfectly, because he did not destroy the idols which he had built.
2.20: 2.20 To worship moles. JEROME. Not in reality, but like moles, etc., up to: 'by which the truth is reached.'
2.22: 2.22 Cease therefore. Because these things will come unless you cease. Cease therefore from raging against Christ, who seems a mere man: because he breathes through the nostrils and lives like other men. Most High. The Lord is high above all nations. And the Most High Himself has founded her (Ps. 87:5). The Hebrew, however, signifies 'height,' not 'high.' For He is Himself the very height, not merely high.
3.1: 3.1 For behold. Up to this point they think it is said of the judgment, etc., up to: 'after all the gifts of grace were taken away from the Jews.'
3.2: 3.2 The warrior. JEROME. Among the Jews there is no one who fights for the law, who judges according to it: for all are vain and foolish. And the diviner. Because sometimes they divine true things, like Balaam, and the diviners of the five cities of the Philistines, by whose counsel the ark of the Lord was sent back; as if he said: Both true prophets and false will be taken away from the Jews. The old man. Whom the Septuagint translated 'elder,' etc., up to: 'because he was unwilling to hear the elders.'
3.3: 3.3 The prudent. A teacher or a hearer, etc., up to: 'who would discern by what spirit the prophets were speaking.' Of the builders. Christ Himself is called the Son of a builder; and in Chronicles we read of the valley of the craftsmen. For there were craftsmen there whom knowledge did not puff up, but who followed the humble Christ.
3.4: 3.4 And I will give boys. JEROME. While the rest is in the person, etc., up to: 'the Apostle forbids a neophyte to be chosen bishop, lest he be proud like the devil.' The effeminate. The Septuagint: mockers, etc., up to: 'the holy state of the Church is thrown into confusion.'
3.6: 3.6 He shall take hold. The same. Literally, etc., up to: 'and let our ruin be sustained by your help.'
3.7: 3.7 He shall answer. The same. This is not in the Hebrew, but is added from the Septuagint. For according to the Hebrew it is joined thus: In that day he shall say: I am not a physician. Let us not at once yield to the judgment of the multitude, etc., up to: 'Seek not to be made a judge, lest you be unable to remove iniquities' (Eccl. 7).
3.8: 3.8 For Jerusalem is ruined. From the person of the Prophet. As if he said: They will therefore find no one willing to help them, because they blasphemed the Lord, saying: You have a demon (John 8), and the like. Because their tongue. Although the Romans, so far as they were concerned, came into a siege over the tribute that was refused, nevertheless the death of the Lord was chiefly the cause.
3.9: 3.9 The acknowledgment. They will acknowledge that this happened because of their sins, or they will always have their sins before the eyes of the mind. Woe to their souls. The same. The Septuagint: Woe to their souls, for they have devised the worst counsel against themselves, saying: Let us bind the just one, because he is useless to us (Wis. 1). The same. Let us therefore beware lest we be exactors among the people; lest, according to the impious Porphyry, matrons and women be our senate, ruling in the Churches, and favor toward women decide about the priestly rank.
3.12: 3.12 And the way of your steps, etc. The same. He, then, is the ecclesiastical teacher, etc., up to: 'of which it is said: I am the way, the truth, and the life' (John 14).
3.13: 3.13 He stands to judge. The same. Now as if angry, etc., up to: 'He comes against the princes and elders to judge them, giving them room for defense.'
3.14: 3.14 For you have grazed. The same. I think that what existed among the old men and princes of the old people existed among the elders and bishops of our time. My vineyard. The same. You brought a vine out of Egypt. The vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel (Ps. 79).
3.15: 3.15 Why do you crush My people? Our princes too, etc., up to: 'they make their own riches or those of their kin.'
3.16: 3.16 Because they are haughty. This applies especially to the wives of the Scribes and Pharisees, and can be referred to others as well: for their delights and luxury their husbands plundered the poor. So that they might not think themselves immune from sin, the Lord says: Because, etc.
3.17: 3.17 He will make bald. What is hidden will be laid open, and foul baldness will appear. For nothing is covered that shall not be revealed.
3.18: 3.18 In that day, namely, of the Babylonian captivity, or more truly when they were taken by the Romans and lost all their ornaments. Of the shoes. Which were not worn out in the wilderness, etc., up to: 'so that in place of matronly cleanliness, the filth of the earth is turned.'
3.21: 3.21 Rings. By which we are sealed against the malice of Christ, whom the Father sealed. The prodigal son also received a robe, a ring, and shoes. Jewels on the forehead. By which our faces and head are adorned.
3.22: 3.22 Linen garments. JEROME. That we may enjoy abundant delights in the Lord.
3.23: 3.23 Headbands. Which bind the mind flowing hither and thither. Summer garments. A very thin women's garment, transparent to sight, suited to summer, and named from that: for theria means summer.
3.24: 3.24 Haircloth for a breast band. By which the breasts are chastened, lest they swell.
3.26: 3.26 And they shall mourn and. Whoever has given place to the devil and has not kept his heart with all watchfulness, his gates will mourn, and with the bridegroom absent, she will always be in mourning, and falling in the dust she will sit. Her gates shall mourn, and desolate she will sit on the ground. Metonymically, the judges, kings, princes who used to sit in the gate.
4.1: 4.1 And seven shall take hold. JEROME. When Nebuchadnezzar King Zedekiah, etc., up to: 'in this place we can understand several.' Seven women. The same. The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and fortitude, the spirit of knowledge and godliness, and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him. They are called women because no one is begotten to God except through the Spirit; and in the plural, because the gifts are many, though the Spirit is one. Our own bread. Our bread is Christ, the rod from the root of Jesse, and the flower; the bread of the women is the Father, as also of Christ, who said: My food is to do the will of my Father (John 4). We will eat our own bread: the body of Christ. We will be covered with our own garments. With the ornaments of virtues. Let Your name be called upon us. From Christ may we be called Christians. Take away our reproach. What we suffer from the Jews as being without God, etc., up to: 'we are often compelled to change lodging.' Take away. Because false doctrines will rise up against wisdom, and against the other women, that is, the virtues: against each one its own contrary rises, when false virtues steal its name.
4.5: 4.5 A cloud, that is, the overshadowing of the Spirit, so that in prosperity they may not be lifted up, as to the children of Israel there was a cloud by day and fire by night. And smoke, etc. JEROME. Whence: The house was filled with smoke (Exod. 13); and elsewhere: He touches the mountains, and they smoke (Ps. 103). For upon every. The majority of the Jews, etc., up to: 'but we, at the first coming of Christ.'
5.1: 5.1 I will sing to my beloved, etc. JEROME. A song is sometimes in joy, sometimes in sorrow, as this one, namely, that which He composed who, seeing the city, wept, saying: If you had known, even you, etc. (Luke 19).
5.2: 5.2 A chosen vineyard. The same. Another edition has 'vineyard of Sorec,' which is a kind of the best vine, most fruitful with perpetual fruit. All that is said of the vineyard is referred to the state of the soul, which, planted by God, brought forth not grapes but wild grapes, and was handed over to the beasts to be trodden down; nor did it receive the rain of doctrine, because it despised past gifts.
5.3: 5.3 Now therefore, inhabitants, etc. Similarly Nathan questions David, so that he may pronounce sentence on himself as if on another.
50.3: 50.3 I will clothe the heavens with darkness. The philosophers say that clouds are lifted up on high no more than ten stadia from the earth, and the splendor of the sun is hidden: so, the light of heaven being shut out, the lower air is darkened. I will clothe. The saints, namely, that sinners may know themselves. And I will put on sackcloth. That they may do penance in fear and haircloth.
50.4: 50.4 The Lord has given, etc. The same. Although these things can be referred to Isaiah, yet properly they are referred to Christ, as if he said: I who of old wrought such things, and can now work similar ones, my power has not been diminished.
50.9: 50.9 Like a garment. The same. A garment is consumed by age and the moth. The Jews also were called to penance forty-two years after the Passion: at last the negligent were crushed at the coming of the Romans, and devoured by the moth of an evil conscience.
50.10: 50.10 Who among you. He who fears is not perfect, etc., up to: 'this one keeps the souls of the saints whole and chaste and pure.' He who walked in darkness. The Gentile people in darkness, etc., up to: 'I call to penance; for I do not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he be converted and live (Ezek. 18).'
50.11: 50.11 Behold all, as if he said: Exhortation avails nothing, nor is there hope of salvation after crimes: They have all turned aside, together they have become useless (Ps. 13). Kindling a fire. They kindled the fire of the city by which it was burned by the Romans, etc., up to: 'so for sinners the diverse matter of sin is kindled more or less.' You shall sleep in sorrows. Because neither by benefits nor by torments would they receive the Son of God, whence, Depart, you cursed, into everlasting fire (Matt. 25).
51.1: 51.1 Hear me, you who follow that which. JEROME. Look to the rock. Christ. Of whom, And the rock was Christ, whence you are hewn (1 Cor. 10), Christians being so called from Christ. And to the hollow of the pit. On account of the opening of the side of Christ, etc., up to: 'we are born through the washing of baptism.'
51.3: 51.3 Joy and gladness. Note that in Zion, which is compared to the paradise of God, there ought to be so much joy and gladness and confession and voice of praise, that what they are going to do in heaven with the angels they may constantly meditate on earth.
51.5: 51.5 My just one. Justifying all, or justice elegantly: not that one nation, but the whole world may be saved.
51.6: 51.6 The heavens like smoke. The same. Of the saints it is written, etc., up to: 'some, however, take perish and grow old for abolition and death.'
51.9: 51.9 Arise. The voice of the prophet and of the faithful people entreating the coming of Christ, in whom help was promised.
51.12: 51.12 Who are you that you should fear a man, etc., up to: 'that they may be ashamed and do penance.'
51.17: 51.17 Rise up, rise up. The same. He exhorts to penance those who denied in the Passion, or persisted in unbelief, crying, Crucify, crucify (John 19), etc. The cup of wrath. The same. Physicians are accustomed to give a most bitter antidote, etc., up to: 'whence it is not clear that this is said of the last captivity.'
51.22: 51.22 Behold. JEROME. He foretold the coming captivity; now he exhorts to penance, that they may escape.
51.23: 51.23 I will put. According to the letter they humbled, etc., up to: 'and in the judgment will be altogether humbled.'
52.1: 52.1 Arise, arise. The prophet exhorts those who after the ascension believed the preaching apostles. For he shall no more. This is about the heavenly Jerusalem, which no unclean person enters.
52.2: 52.2 Shake yourself. The soul polluted by filth loses its former whiteness, etc., up to: 'not with corruptible silver and gold, but with the blood of the spotless lamb.'
52.3: 52.3 For nothing. You neither had gain, nor escaped loss, when you betrayed the Son of God.
52.4: 52.4 Into Egypt. JEROME. He reproves the Jews and foretells what is to come, etc., up to: 'so as to oppress him even in his own land, and slander him?'
52.5: 52.5 What have I here? The same. Nothing here, he says, do I find among them, etc., up to: 'that they fixed their Redeemer to the cross.'
52.7: 52.7 How beautiful. The same. Concerning him who said above: I myself who spoke, behold, I am here, the prophet testifies that he himself preached the Gospel upon the mountains. Of the one announcing, Christ, by himself, by the apostles, to whom he said: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you (John 14). Over whom the Lord sitting preached: They are even the feet of Christ, carrying his preaching.
52.8: 52.8 The voice of the watchmen: The same. Of the apostles and others who are always on the watchtower to foresee everything and advance their subjects.
52.9: 52.9 Rejoice. He consoles the primitive Church, etc., up to: 'by the multitude of the Gentiles it was both restored and multiplied.'
52.10: 52.10 The arm. In his arm the Gentiles shall hope (Ps. 97). And elsewhere: Your arm with power (Ps. 88).
52.11: 52.11 Depart. The same. The Jews refer this to themselves, etc., up to: 'admonished by the Holy Spirit.' Go out, preaching the Gospel throughout the whole world, Go, teach all nations (Matt. 18). The vessels of the Lord. The same. The temple of the Lord is holy, which you are, namely golden and silver vessels, whence Paul is called a vessel of election; or the vessels of the Lord, the armor of God, the breastplate of justice, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God.
52.13: 52.13 Behold, he shall understand: lest there be doubt who it was that said, I who spoke, behold, I am here: and the Father plainly teaches what the arm of the Lord is.
52.14: 52.14 As they were astonished. The order of the history is not kept. For above the prophet was speaking in the person of the Father about the ascension of the Son, and suddenly returned to the Passion.
53.1: 53.1 Who has believed? JEROME. The prophet, in the person of the prophets, complains that few of the Jews believe what they hear from them of the coming of the Son. And the arm of the Lord. The same. The Father announced his Son as coming to the world; and before the scandal of the cross, he sent ahead the glory of the one rising. He shall be lifted up and extolled, etc. The chorus of the prophets therefore answers that they have fulfilled their office and announced the arm of the Lord.
53.2: 53.2 A shoot. Symmachus: a branch; signifying the man who came forth from the womb of a virgin. From thirsty ground. Aquila: pathless, where the privilege of virginity is shown, because he was created without seed from earth that was before pathless.
53.5: 53.5 With his bruise. The same. It is clear that as the body was torn and scourged, so the soul truly grieved for us, lest in Christ truth be believed in part and falsehood in part.
53.7: 53.7 He opened not, etc. To Pilate or Herod. For he answered few things lest the salvation of the human race be delayed. And as a lamb. The same. In whose figure the people of Israel ate the lamb in Egypt (Exod. 12). This is the Lamb who takes away the sins of the world (John 1), who was slain from the origin of the world (Apoc. 13), who feeds us with his flesh and blood, and clothes us with the fleece of protection.
53.8: 53.8 From judgment. The judge of all did not find truth in the judgment, but was condemned without fault. Hence the prophet marvels that the God of all delivered himself to the Passion.
53.9: 53.9 He will give the wicked. The same. That is, the Gentiles, who are without piety, to God the Father, because, dead and buried, he acquired them, and the rich, the Jews, namely, glorying in the riches of the law and the prophets. The rich. The Scribes and Pharisees glorying in the riches of the doctrine of the law.
53.10: 53.10 Long-lived seed. The word of the Gospel, namely, which will not grow old like the Old Testament, whence: The sower went out to sow his seed (Luke 8).
53.11: 53.11 He shall be satisfied. By the faith of the Gentiles, whence hungry and thirsty by the well of Jacob he would not use the food that was bought, because he was already satisfied by the faith of the Samaritan woman and of those who were coming out to him from the city.
53.12: 53.12 And with the wicked. To redeem the wicked from sin, made all things to all men: For he bore our sins in his body (1 Pet. 2). His imitator Paul says: I became all things to all men, that I might gain all (1 Cor. 9). He prayed. Father, forgive them. At this voice, according to the Gospel of the Nazarenes, many thousands of the Jews standing around the cross believed.
54.1: 54.1 Praise, O barren one. JEROME. So far concerning the nativity, passion, resurrection, etc., up to: 'gathered both from Jews and from Gentiles.' Praise, O barren one. The Apostle, according to the Septuagint: Rejoice, you barren who bear not, break forth and cry, you who travail not, for many are the children of the desolate (Gal. 4), etc. But we, brethren, as Isaac was, are children of promise.
54.3: 54.3 For to the right: to all places of the world. Or, neither lifted up by prosperity nor broken by adversity. Or, to the goods of the future and the present.
54.4: 54.4 Fear not. The same. When the tower of Babel was being built, etc., up to: 'who the cord.'
54.6: 54.6 For as a woman. The same. Those who follow tropology even in the most difficult places, etc., up to: 'he holds out the robe and the kiss.'
54.9: 54.9 As in the days of Noah, etc. That the congregation of the saints may believe the everlasting mercy of the Lord, and that they were forsaken but for a moment, in order that they may become friends of God by an eternal covenant: he sets down the examples of the ancients.
54.14: 54.14 Depart far. JEROME. He consoled the Church from the Gentiles, promising them spiritual graces: now he teaches what she should do, that she may not fear adversaries.
54.15: 54.15 Behold the stranger. The Jews turn this to themselves, as though there would be proselytes from the Gentiles in the time of their Christ.
54.16: 54.16 Behold, I. Not that I am the cause of their destruction, but an adversary fighting; for the conquered the cause of destruction, for the conquerors the cause of reward.
54.17: 54.17 This is the inheritance. Lest the just man fail under tribulation, he adds rewards.
55.1: 55.1 All you who thirst, come. JEROME. Because he had said that the vessel made against the Church would be crushed, and every tongue armed against the knowledge of God would be overcome, he invites believers to the river of God, which is full of waters. Eat. By hearing, speaking, reading, meditating, working, holding in the heart. Divine Scripture is both drink, when open, and food, when hidden. It is also itself both the water and the bread which comes down from heaven. Why do you weigh out silver? You weigh the sacred words, but not refreshment. You who keep only the appearance of the letter lose from the spiritual understanding the richness of interior refreshment.
55.4: 55.4 Behold a witness. He called the Jews to believe, but because he knew that, they not believing, the Gentiles would believe, he says that he sent the Son to announce his commands to the peoples.
55.5: 55.5 The Lord your God. The same. When he is called Father, the Father of Christ according to divinity is called the Father of glory; according to humanity, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
55.6: 55.6 Seek the Lord. These things pertain to the Jews or to the Gentiles specially, and to each one generally. The prophet to the Jews: Seek the Lord, as if he said: The Gentiles receive the mercies of David, and you disdain them; but do penance, and be converted while you have time. While he is near. The same. Lest he withdraw because of your vices, who draws near to those drawing near to him, and joyfully runs to meet the returning son.
55.8: 55.8 For. Do not think that what I promise is difficult: consider that between my counsels and yours there is great difference: and as great as the difference of nature, so great is the difference of will.
55.10: 55.10 And as. The same. By another likeness he shows that he is abundant in forgiving. Bread to the eater. Hence Solomon: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you shall find it, that is, pour out the bread of your doctrine and spiritual grace to all, for in the end you will receive rewards.
55.11: 55.11 It shall not return. But after it has fulfilled my will on earth, it will return and sit at my right hand, according to that, Sit at my right hand, etc.
55.12: 55.12 The mountains, namely the souls of the saints, which for the variety of virtues are called mountains and hills.
55.13: 55.13 Instead of the thorn. The thorn, full of stings and pricks. The fir, tall, lofty, suitable for building houses, abundant in pitch. And the Lord shall be. Others: And the Lord shall be for a name and for an everlasting sign which shall not fail.
56.1: 56.1 Thus says the Lord. Keep judgment. JEROME. The prophecy of the Gentiles being ended, who at the coming of Christ are changed from the thorn and nettle into the fir and myrtle, he speaks to the hearers of that time, that they may prepare themselves for the coming of the Savior, who is mercy and justice. Keep judgment. The same. Not respecting persons in judgment. For it is the judgment of the Lord, who judges those who judge well.
56.2: 56.2 Keeping the Sabbath. The same. That it be not, namely, of the six days in which the world was made. Of which the apostles were not, to whom it is said: If you were of the world, the world would love its own, etc. I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you (John 15).
56.3: 56.3 And let not say. The same. This is against the Jews, who claimed the coming of Christ for themselves alone, and compelled others to despair. But there is no distinction between Jew and Greek (Rom. 10). The eunuch. The same. For the kingdom of heaven, who mortify their members upon earth, etc., up to: 'which is said of the seed of spiritual work, not of offspring.'
56.4: 56.4 For thus says the Lord. The same. He proposed two, proselytes namely and eunuchs, etc., up to: 'lest they think themselves subject to the curse of the law.'
56.6: 56.6 And the sons of the stranger: after the eunuchs he passes to strangers and promises rewards. For servants. Such as Paul, who says of himself: Paul, servant of Christ Jesus, and Moses, servant of God.
56.7: 56.7 Their holocausts. Mortify your members which are upon the earth (Col. 3). And Present your bodies a living sacrifice to God. A holocaust is offered whole to God and is burned. A part of the victim is given to the priests. He offers a holocaust to God who leaves the world, that he may always be free for prayer. He offers a victim who serves God and justly arranges the things that are of the world. Upon my altar. Faith, upon which all things are offered, without which it is impossible to please God. Whence: But the just shall live by his faith.
56.9: 56.9 All beasts. The voice of the prophet, who summons the Romans to the destruction of Jerusalem, to whom nearly the whole world was subject. Or by beasts, demons: to whom the Jews were handed over to be devoured.
56.10: 56.10 Blind. Not having Christ, the true light, or faith and the other virtues. Dogs. The same. As dogs guard the flock, so prelates ought to guard the people. Most shameless dogs. Which is: As dogs without discernment often persecute even the good, so also the Jews shamelessly cried, Crucify, crucify him (Luke 23), and were not satisfied with the reproaches against the Lord.
56.12: 56.12 Come, let us take. So they perverted those who ought to have corrected. And since all sinned, they were handed over into the hands of the Romans.
57.1: 57.1 The just perishes. JEROME. The Jews refer this to Isaiah, who was sawn in two with a wooden saw by the most impious King Manasseh, and to the other prophets, men of mercy, whom he himself killed. But it is said more truly of him who is supremely just. And there is none. On account of the blind watchmen and dumb dogs. Who may reflect: for the blind and dumb, ignorant of wisdom, do not think of the things that are of God.
57.2: 57.2 Let peace come, let him rest in his bed, who walked in. The same. The prophet prays that Christ come, rising from the dead, rest in his bed in glory, namely of the Father's majesty, or in the Church, in which he walked in uprightness.
57.6: 57.6 Libation. Wine, oil and such liquids: the sacrifice of bread, victim, and the like.
57.7: 57.7 Upon a high mountain. Heretics also, etc., up to: 'that they may be trodden underfoot by men.'
57.8: 57.8 And behind the door: As if he said: Not only on mountains have you worshipped idols, but you have also set them behind the door, that entering you might see and always worship. Because near me you have uncovered yourself. The metaphor of an adulteress, as above of a harlot, etc., up to: 'exposed to all who enter.'
57.9: 57.9 You sent messengers. To bring far-off idols, as if the nearby ones were not enough. And in this he signifies the gods of the Babylonians and Egyptians.
57.10: 57.10 In the multitude of your way you have labored. He who walks the royal road does not labor. There is one way of truth, which says: I am the way, the truth and the life (John 14): there are many ways of the worldly, whence, My ways are not as your ways (Isa. 40).
57.13: 57.13 But he who has trust in me. The same. Those who did not worship idols, or who repented when led into captivity, returned under Zerubbabel and other leaders and worshipped their God in his place, according to the Hebrew. He shall possess your holy mountain, namely the law of the Old and New Testament; for both were given on a mountain. And he invites to the height of rewards, or to Christ.
57.14: 57.14 And I shall say, Christ namely to the apostles, I have made the way, by preaching well, provide the journey as an example to them by working well; take away stumbling blocks by washing away sins through baptism, by removing the worship of idols through preaching.
57.15: 57.15 For thus says. The rebuke against Jerusalem being ended, he comes to those who trust in the Lord, for whose return he had commanded the way to be prepared. Hence he begins from the praises of God, and consequently shows what he has promised to the returning people.
57.16: 57.16 For I will not contend forever. The same. I will not keep my anger forever, nor will I dispute with my creature, but I will strike in the present, that I may heal in the future. For the spirit. Peace, joy, the life of all, etc., up to: 'specially to the Jews.'
57.17: 57.17 I hid from you, etc., namely my help, that you might desire more, saying: Show your face, and we shall be saved (Ps. 79). He went away. The same. Which one understanding says: All the day long I went about sad (Ps. 37).
57.19: 57.19 I created: as if he said: The liberation from captivity, which I promised through Jeremiah after seventy years, I fulfilled in deed. I created the fruit of the lips, peace.
57.20: 57.20 But the wicked. Above, of those who did penance in captivity and were therefore freed, and of those who believed after the ascension. Here he speaks specially of those who remained in their unbelief.
58.1: 58.1 Cry. JEROME. The Lord to the prophets or to the apostles: the previous chapter, namely, being finished, in which peace is announced to the just and no rest to the wicked. Like a trumpet. The same. Where to the apostles, etc., up to: 'so may Israel, dead in sin, hear its crimes.' To my people. As if he said: Let them see what a Father they have lost, who calls even sinners his people.
58.2: 58.2 As. That is, why I will not hear them like those who do justice in the Church, living justly and piously, confessing Christ true God and true man. They ask. The same. Another rashness of the Jews, who, as though trusting in a good conscience, demand just judgment, according to that: Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence.
58.3: 58.3 Why have we fasted? They forgot the ancient history, that the Lord did not regard the gifts of Cain, because he did not divide rightly with his brother, whose charity toward God he envied. Behold, in the day. The fast acceptable to God is not only to abstain from foods, but from all unlawful things. You exact again. He who demands again from one who has not, does violence to God.
58.4: 58.4 Do not fast as until this day. Lest he seem to reject fasting, he teaches how one should fast.
58.6: 58.6 Bonds. The same. We understand sins, etc., up to: 'do not despise your own kin.'
58.7: 58.7 Break your bread to the hungry. The same. We break bread to the hungry, etc., up to: 'but the satiety of the soul.' And your own flesh. The same. In any need recognize your neighbor as like yourself, considering that you are mortal and subject to suffering.
58.8: 58.8 Your light. As morning light dispels the darkness, so the light of truth drives away errors. Justice. Christ, who justifies all, will go before you to glory. And the glory of the Lord shall gather you, that is, will receive you to himself, who said: Where I am, there shall my minister also be (John 12).
58.9: 58.9 To stretch out a finger. To mark neighbors, to detract. That is, not only do not think and do not do these things, but do not detract.
58.11: 58.11 A watered garden, a paradise of delight, which the Lord God planted from the beginning, namely the Church. The fountain in the midst is Christ, whose waters of spiritual doctrine do not fail, which water the Church. And this is, And you shall be like a watered garden, O faithful soul or Church. Like a fountain. You will be likened to Christ, your head.
58.12: 58.12 They shall be built. JEROME. The Jews refer this to the restoration which was made under Zerubbabel and Jesus the great priest; or to that which they rave will be at the last. These things can better be referred to the Church. The foundations. The same. The apostles, prophets and the like: whence, Her foundations are in the holy mountains (Ps. 86). But the Foundation in the singular is Christ, whence, For other foundation no one can lay, but that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus (1 Cor. 3). Of iniquities, elsewhere into rest, namely the paths of error into rest or true peace.
58.14: 58.14 Of the land. Of the living, which is above, not below, whence to Lot it is said: Save yourself in the mountain. Inheritance. Heavenly, which I gave to Jacob, whose son you are by faith and works, supplanting vices and sins. For whose imitator one is, his son he is called.
59.2: 59.2 But your iniquities. He shows why they were not heard and were led into captivity.
59.3: 59.3 His hands. JEROME. He sets out the iniquities in parts, etc., up to: 'and at last crying out against the Son of God: His blood be upon us and upon our children.'
59.4: 59.4 They conceived. The same. Those who await Antichrist. For him whom they seek with much labor they will receive in iniquity.
59.5: 59.5 Eggs. The same. From the egg the offspring, from the heart the counsel, from which the act. They broke the eggs, therefore, when they showed their iniquitous hearts and venomous counsels in words, saying: He is guilty of death (Matt. 26). Of asps. The asp, at the first voice of the charmer, presses one ear to the ground and stops the other with its tail, that it may not be charmed: so the Jews, clinging to earthly things, fearing to lose place and nation, rejected the preaching of Christ, venomous sons of venomous parents. It shall break forth into a basilisk. From the eggs of the asp comes the basilisk, which is also a cockatrice; from the Jews, Antichrist. For he will be born of them, killing by his breath, that is, by venomous speech, many flying toward the heavenly homeland. For the basilisk kills with its breath birds flying through the air.
59.9: 59.9 For this. The same. The prophet, in the person of the penitent people, answers, after the accusation, what penitents ought to say.
59.11: 59.11 We shall roar like bears, all. The meditation and teaching of the Jews in the sacred Scripture is compared to the roaring of a bear and the moaning of a dove, as useless and vain as these. Against subjects they also rage like bears; against superiors or equals they moan like doves.
59.15: 59.15 Truth in. The same. Christ, who is the way, etc., up to: 'that the person of Christ may be shown, whom forsaking they followed falsehood.'
59.16: 59.16 And he saw. The same. Having shown that they repented, he shows that their repentance did not please the Lord, because many did not repent with a pure heart. For there is no man. All are effeminate in mind, as also that: I called and there was none to hear. And he saved for himself. The Father, namely, through the Son the Gentiles. And his justice, or mercy according to the Septuagint, will confirm him who shall wish to be converted: not by merit but by mercy and justice. For it is just that the Creator spare the repentant creature, which could not be saved by its merits.
59.19: 59.19 And they shall fear who. The vengeance of God upon the Jews through the Romans having been shown beforehand, he describes the faith of the Gentiles, coming from the four parts of the world, having heard the preaching of the apostles. Like a river. Because most swiftly it filled the world with its preaching and faith. Which the Spirit of the Lord. The same. To redeem the human race, the Holy Spirit, namely. Whence: Who was conceived of the Holy Spirit. And, The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him (Isa. 11), etc.
59.21: 59.21 This covenant, namely that I will redeem them by the blood of the Son, and they themselves will do my commands and hold me fast by morals; and this is, My Spirit that is in you,
60.1: 60.1 Arise, be enlightened. JEROME. The Jews refer this to the time of their Christ, etc., up to: 'that either for these they may receive the Son of God.' Arise. The same. In the Churches, you who were killed in the synagogues: arise among the Gentiles, you who fell among the Jews. Arise by confession, by virtues, you who fell by trafficking, by vices; and when you have risen, be enlightened, that is, receive the faith of Christ. The light. Promised to you long before, to come for your redemption, which enlightens every man coming into this world, namely him who says: I am the light of the world (John 1, 8), by whom you will be enlightened if you receive the faith of Christ. The glory of the Lord. To enlighten. The Son, namely, as the risen sun enlightens the world, in whose figure the glory of the Lord is shown to Moses and Solomon, building the tabernacle for one, the temple for the other. The glory of the Lord also was the raising of the dead, the cleansing of the leper, and the like.
60.2: 60.2 The earth. The same. The Jews who love earthly things, to whom it is said: You shall eat the good things of the land, which they take carnally.
60.3: 60.3 Your rising. The same. Since, namely, you were born of water and the Holy Spirit, we all walk in the splendor of the rising of the primitive Church, because we have the same faith, we are reborn by the same baptism.
60.4: 60.4 Lift up your eyes round about. Like which: Lift up your eyes and see the regions, for they are already white for harvest (John 4). Your sons. JEROME. Whom you begot in faith: whence Paul: Through the Gospel I begot you (1 Cor. 4). The first believers from the Jews, when the Holy Spirit was given, were in Jerusalem religious men of every nation under heaven (Acts 2), or the Gentiles from all parts of the world. They shall come from afar. Because they were far from God through idolatry, whence: You who were far off have been made near (Eph. 2). From the side. The same. Some codices have, etc., up to: 'nor does the sense of Jerome incline to this.'
60.6: 60.6 Of camels. The camel is a humped animal and a bearer of burdens. These are the rich, carrying the hump of the burden of riches and sins. Dromedaries. Dromedary or dromas, for both are said: it is an animal smaller than a camel, but swifter, in which are figured the Gentiles running swiftly to the faith. Midian and Ephah. Regions beyond Arabia abounding in camels and dromedaries, etc., up to: 'which is figured by incense, they offered to the Lord.'
60.7: 60.7 All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered. The same. The simple who before were darkness and sorrow, etc., up to: 'where the Saracens, born of that stock, dwelt.' Rams. Preachers, leaders of the flock, sons of the prophets, who taught that what the prophets foretold of Christ has been fulfilled. Nebaioth, son of Ishmael, and it is interpreted prophecy. They shall minister to you. Holy bishops, priests, ministers of the Church, administering the body and blood of Christ to the faithful.
60.8: 60.8 Who are these. The prophet marvels at the Gentiles running so quickly to the faith, or the primitive Church: To the windows. At their windows stand the saints, guarding the five senses of the body, lest through them, as through windows, death enter into souls.
60.9: 60.9 Their silver. This is: With the heart one believes unto justice, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation (Rom. 10).
60.10: 60.10 Sons of strangers. The princes of the Gentiles who built churches throughout the world, as Constantine, who made twelve churches at Rome in honor of the twelve apostles, and many others who built many churches and supplied what was necessary.
60.13: 60.13 The glory of Lebanon. Lebanon is a mountain bordering the land of promise, etc., up to: 'kings and princes who came to the Church.' The fir. The same. The proud, namely the rich and philosophers. For pride follows riches and knowledge. Cyprian and Hilary, trees high in the world, built the Church of God. The diversity of trees signifies the diverse orders in the Church. Of all of which the Church is built, distinguished with wondrous beauty. The place of my feet. The Church, in which the apostles, etc., up to: 'they support the Church by institutions, miracles and examples.'
60.14: 60.14 The city of the Lord. For a city is so called from community, etc., up to: 'who might go about attentively and give help.'
60.15: 60.15 Hated. By the Jews, because it preached the faith of Christ and destroyed the observances of the law; by the Gentiles, because it brought one God and affirmed that the idols are nothing. There was none who passed through you. Who would pass through and bless you, etc., up to: 'moreover pride is sometimes evil, sometimes good:'
60.17: 60.17 For wood, bronze. The same. By wood and stones, etc., up to: 'others strong in faith, like Cyprian, and other martyrs, like iron.' Your visitation. The same. Christ, or the peaceful apostles, and just superiors, that they may rightly teach and judge.
60.19: 60.19 It shall not be. This is of the day of judgment. In this chapter we are compelled to refer whatever has been said or is to be said to the last time, since the office of heaven and earth, of sun and moon, will cease for us, and the Lord himself will be the light forever.
60.21: 60.21 The shoot. The same. The angels, all the elect, who fulfill by works the faith they have. They themselves are the shoot of the Lord's planting and the work of his hands, because created by him and planted in the Church by faith to glorify their Creator.
60.22: 60.22 In its time: the coming of Christ. Or in the opportune or appointed time. When the Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all scandals.
61.1: 61.1 The Spirit of the Lord. JEROME. Christ according to humanity, who had said above, I the Lord, in its time I will gather them, etc. Because he has anointed me: with the oil of gladness, the abundance of grace. The same. This anointing was completed in baptism, because the Spirit of the Lord descended in the form of a dove and remained on him. To proclaim. Septuagint: To preach the Gospel to the poor. The opening, namely the release; for so Symmachus more plainly translated.
61.2: 61.2 The day of vengeance: The same. Of damnation, which came through the Romans, according to that: The day shall come, etc. And, when you shall see Jerusalem encompassed by an army, etc.
61.3: 61.3 A crown. When, namely, they see that very many of the Jews have believed, and receive a most clean robe in place of mourning garb. For ashes. For the mourning and sorrow of their fruits, when they see the Gentiles flocking to the faith, they shall have the oil of joy for mourning, the mantle of praise for the spirit of sorrow.
61.5: 61.5 Vinedressers. The same. The wicked cultivators of the vineyard, the Scribes and Pharisees, of whom it is said: He will miserably destroy the wicked, and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen.
61.6: 61.6 But you. This is to the preachers from the Gentiles, etc., up to: 'who were priests in the house of the Lord.'
61.7: 61.7 Their portion. The Lord's. Whence the Psalmist: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance, etc. Which no one says truly who seeks another portion.
61.8: 61.8 For I am the Lord: As if he said: The Lord will do this, who loves more the justice of the poor and true judgment than the gifts of the rich, which are often from plunder, and neither the hire of a harlot nor the price of flesh is pleasing as a sacrifice, nor if one should immolate his son to the Lord. In truth. That in truth they may eat the lamb, that they may make the circumcision of hearts, and do in truth all that was given in figure. An everlasting covenant. The eternal Gospel, not like the Old Testament, which the Gospel succeeds.
61.9: 61.9 Their seed. The faithful, to whom the apostles entrusted the seed of the word which they received from the Lord.
61.10: 61.10 Rejoicing I will rejoice in the Lord, not in the world. With the garments of salvation: with virtues, with Christ himself, etc., up to: 'yet the Church is one in head and in members.' And as a bride. He sets down examples of another comparison, of which the first refers to the bridegroom, the next to the bride.
61.11: 61.11 And praise: his own, etc., up to: 'will render to the Lord the fruit of praise and good works.'
62.1: 62.1 For Zion's sake. JEROME. The prophet in his own person, exceedingly gladdened by all that the incarnate Son confers on the world. And this is, For Zion's sake I will not be silent, although he forbids speaking, although he threatens death. Let the lamp be kindled. Lampas in Greek, flame in Latin, whence: I came to cast fire on the earth, and what will I but that it be kindled? The apostles, set on fire by this, spoke in various tongues.
62.2: 62.2 A new name. The same. It is the custom of the Hebrews to give new names from new things, etc., up to: 'similarly first Simon, afterward Peter.'
62.3: 62.3 A crown of glory. From all parts of the world, as it were a crown, believers coming.
62.4: 62.4 You shall not be called. He addresses the Church from both peoples, as if: you will not be content with this end of names.
62.5: 62.5 And he shall rejoice, etc. For this reason a man shall leave father and mother (Gen. 2; Matt. 19). This is a great sacrament in Christ and in the Church (Eph. 5).
62.6: 62.6 Upon your walls. The same. The apostles, the preachers, who fortify the Church, whose guardians are angels. Whence: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent for the sake of those who receive the inheritance of salvation (Heb. 1). Or the walls of the Churches are the disciples of the apostles, whose guardians are the apostles themselves.
62.7: 62.7 Till he make Jerusalem. Which is, either that she herself, spread far and wide, be praised everywhere, or that she everywhere always praise her Creator.
62.8: 62.8 He swore by the Son, namely, who is the power of God and the wisdom of God. By his right hand. In the Son. Whence: You made all things in wisdom (Ps. 103), who is also the arm and strength of the Father: Whence, All things were made by him (John 1). If I give your wheat. The wheat of the Jews and wine I often gave to their enemies, as is read in the book of Judges (Judg. 6): that in the time of harvest the Midianites rushed in and gathered their crops. And when they were led captive, Samaritans were put in their place to eat their harvests. But in this place he understands the food of the Church, virtues, and good works, the body of Christ and the blood. That is, the praises and works which you spent on idols the demons ate. But after the coming of the Son the Lord was delighted in them. The wheat, therefore, and the wine, the food of the Jews namely, signified the body of Christ and the blood. Whence, My flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink (John 6). This today is not taken by heretics, pagans, Jews, enemies of the Church.
62.10: 62.10 Through the gates. The ministers of the Church, who bring others in. Or the virtues, which lead into heaven, as from virtue to virtue. Make the way plain. By removing scandals; by remitting sins in baptism. Choose. Or, cast out according to the Septuagint, which is, take away the hardness of unbelief from the hearts of men; or, the reprobate and hard from the fellowship of the faithful.
62.11: 62.11 Say to the daughter of Zion. Namely, to the primitive Church, which was first from the Jews: whence, The sons of my mother have fought against me (Cant. 1). Or according to that: But as many as received him (John 1), etc. And they shall call him, saying: You are a holy people, you are redeemed by the Lord God. For so some codices have it.
63.1: 63.1 Who is this? Some angels, not fully knowing the mystery of the incarnation, passion, resurrection, seeing the Lord ascend to heaven with a multitude of angels and holy men by his own power, not by the help of angels, marvel at the mystery of the incarnation and passion and resurrection and ascension: and how he opens the kingdom of heaven for himself and for others; whence also to the angels accompanying the Lord they say: Who is this? And David likewise: Who is this King of glory? (Ps. 23). Yet Augustine seems to say on Genesis that all the angels from their very creation immediately knew in the contemplation of their Creator whatever he was going to do. But Jerome openly declares that some angels did not fully know until the mystery of the incarnation was completed. From Edom. Edom, from Jerome, from the dish of red lentils, etc., up to: 'or from despoiled hell, a victor with his faithful.' Beautiful in his robe. Formosum means warm. Hence formosus as if calidus, because from the color the face becomes red and rosy, and thence comely.
63.2: 63.2 Why then. The same. As if the angels were saying: We have learned, etc., up to: 'clemency suits you more than cruelty.'
63.3: 63.3 Alone. Samson alone, his hair cut off, is exposed to the Philistines, neither an angel nor an archangel nor any heavenly spirit. Finally, of the human race, none, neither Jew nor Gentile, is a helper: he alone fights, he alone conquers. Sprinkled. JEROME. My blood by their rancor, etc., up to: 'whose blood is often sprinkled on the garments of the victor.'
63.5: 63.5 And there was not, etc. Whence: All my friends have forsaken me, and those whom I knew have withdrawn from me like strangers (Job 19). And he saved. Jerome to Augustine and Alypius: Avoiding the impiety of Sabellius, we distinguish three persons expressed under their proper character, not saying that the Father is the same as the Son, nor the Son the same as the Father, nor the Holy Spirit the same: but that there is one person of the Father, another of the Son, another of the Holy Spirit. For we confess not the names only, but the properties of the names.
63.7: 63.7 Of the mercies. JEROME. The prophet in the person of the Jewish people, repentant and acknowledging the mercy of the Lord.
63.9: 63.9 He was not afflicted. The same. The voice which is, etc., up to: 'there is no helper but Michael your prince, who stands for the sons of my people (Dan. 10).' And the angel. The same. Septuagint. Not an envoy nor an angel himself, but the Lord saved them.
63.10: 63.10 His holy spirit. That is, of Moses: whence, They provoked Moses in the camp, and Aaron the holy one of the Lord (Ps. 105). Or of his Holy One, Christ, whom they would not believe. For the Son of God who redeemed us delivered them from Egypt and the Red Sea. The Holy Spirit, or, of his holy one. Some codices have, namely the Holy Spirit, whom he grieves who grieves a spiritual man: whence, He who touches you touches the apple of my eye (Zech. 2). Or the angel sent as guardian, whom they often offended by doing evil.
63.11: 63.11 Of Moses. Because there is no other who prays for them. Where is, etc. The prophet, seeing the casting away of his people, the misery and affliction already imminent because of the denial of the Son of God, cries out in compassion, saying: Where is? as if to say: the clemency of the Almighty. Where is he who put? Of Moses, namely, because at Moses' prayer the Lord took of his spirit and gave it to seventy men.
63.12: 63.12 Who divided the waters before them. It is also said: When Moses struck the sea and divided it into twelve ways, and the others hesitating, the tribe of Judah entered, and for this obtained the dignity of the kingdom.
63.14: 63.14 The Spirit of the Lord. The angel, namely; whence: And my angel shall go before you (Exod. 14). For spirit is the name of a nature, angel of an office.
63.15: 63.15 Look down from heaven and see. The Lord is everywhere whole and always, whence: I fill heaven and earth (Jer. 23).
