Yet he is said to have his seat in heaven, according to that: Heaven is my throne (Isa. 66), because his will is chiefly done in the heavenly angels and just men whose conversation is in heaven. Where is your zeal, etc. As if he said: Because we have sinned and you began to hate us, your zeal has withdrawn: and with it withdrawing, strength has withdrawn, and the affection of a father's heart is overcome.
63.16: 63.16 Abraham knew not. JEROME. As if he said: Because we have offended you, etc., up to: 'let him not forget his children, lest through them the name of God be blasphemed among the Gentiles.'
63.17: 63.17 Why to err. Paul, writing to the Corinthians, namely to the people of one city, according to the variety of its inhabitants, saints and sinners, now praises, now reproves: so the present chapter, which is woven from the prayer of the people entreating God, now praises the Lord, now accuses, according to the second rule of Tyconius, which is about the body of the Lord.
63.19: 63.19 As in the beginning. JEROME. Before you called us, etc., up to: 'they shall not be called the people of God, namely Christians from Christ.'
64.1: 64.1 O that you would rend. JEROME. In his own person, etc., up to: 'likewise David: He bowed the heavens and came down (Ps. 17).'
64.2: 64.2 The waters would burn. SYMMACHUS: The waters of the sea would burn with fire. Which is, the peoples of the world would be inflamed with the fire of charity. Whence: I came to cast fire on the earth, and what will I but that it be kindled? (Luke 12) and so your name, which is Christ Jesus, would be made known to your enemies, namely the Jews.
64.3: 64.3 We shall not endure. We Jews, but we shall blaspheme, saying: In Beelzebub the prince of demons he casts out demons (Matt. 12). For the prophet says this in the person of the unbelievers. You descended. As though their prayers had been heard, he says: You descended, etc. Mountains. Power lost: Now the prince of this world shall be cast out (John 12). And to the Jews it is said: The kingdom of God shall be taken from you (Matt. 21), namely the holy Scripture and all glory and all dignity.
64.4: 64.4 From the beginning of the world. Hence Paul takes a testimony to the Corinthians, expressing the sense, not word for word. Eye. Because it is not body or color. What the Apostle puts, has not entered into the heart of man, because it is greater, and the heart must be directed thither. For he prepared himself, the knowledge of himself, the knowledge of the Holy Trinity; whence: This is eternal life, that they may know you the only true God and Jesus Christ whom you have sent (John 17). No one can see him; whence that: No one has ever seen God (John 1).
64.5: 64.5 Behold, you, etc. In the person of the unbelieving people, who, wishing to pass over to the truth of the Gospel, professed with the mouth a repentance which they did not have in the heart.
64.6: 64.6 Menstruous, etc. Mene in Hebrew, Luna (moon) in Latin; whence menstruous, women who every month are wont to endure a flow of blood. And then men ought to abstain from them. For then are conceived the condemned in their limbs, the blind, lame, leprous, and the like: so that, because the parents were not ashamed to be joined in the bedchamber, their sins lie open to all and are openly reproved in the little ones. Wind. A commotion of the air, as there, He commanded the winds and the sea (Matt. 8). Or the Holy Spirit: Of a mighty wind coming (Acts 1). For here the Spirit is put for wind, signifying the Holy Spirit. Or the temptation of demons and wicked men, as that: The floods came, and the winds blew (Matt. 7): and this is as a wind.
64.8: 64.8 And now, Lord. As if he said: If we consider our merits, we must despair; if your clemency, who scourge every son whom you receive, we dare to pour out prayers, for you are our Father. The works of your hands. As if he said: Look upon your work, not our merits. The right confession of the mystery of the Trinity is the ignorance of knowledge.
64.9: 64.9 Be not angry, Lord. That is, we do not avoid wrath, nor do we any longer seek patience, through which we treasure up wrath for ourselves in the day of vengeance: but we beseech that you be not angry with us overmuch, namely, that at the time of vengeance you do not remember our iniquity.
64.10: 64.10 Zion is a desert. Zion and Jerusalem in this place mean the same, the temple, namely, and the city, where once was the watchtower of virtues and the vision of peace. But after the people of the Jews denied their king, and added that: We have no king but Caesar (John 19), Jerusalem was forsaken by God: whence, Your house shall be left to you desolate (Luke 13); and that, Arise, let us go hence (John 14). And in the temple voices were heard, as the ecclesiastical history says: Let us depart from these seats.
64.11: 64.11 The house. Allegorically. The house of God is the Church, and each faithful soul, which is sometimes corrupted by the fires of luxury and avarice.
65.1: 65.1 They have sought, etc. JEROME. To this the Son answers, etc., up to: 'and strange sons have lied to me (Ps. 17).'
65.2: 65.2 I have spread out my hands. The same. On the cross praying for them, etc., up to: 'yet they themselves always remained unbelieving.'
65.3: 65.3 A people that provokes to anger. The same. Allegorically. Every heretic provokes God to anger, etc., up to: 'and to build in a square, and to strengthen with lines in the side of the cut dust.'
65.4: 65.4 In the shrines. Delubra are so called from deleo (to wash away), because there it was thought the soul was washed. Or because nearby were pools where both the priest and the victim were washed. Allegorically. JEROME. Heretics in the memorials of their teachers, etc., up to: 'so that whoever is not like them is detested as lost.'
65.5: 65.5 In my fury. We ought to take fury, forgetfulness, anger, repentance in God in the same way as hands, feet, eyes, ears, and the other members which he is said to have: not that he is subject to these disturbances, who extinguishes them in us, but through our words we understand God's affection toward us.
65.6: 65.6 I will not be silent. He who said above: I have been silent, I have always kept silence, I was patient, now says: I will not be silent, that is, I will not spare any more, nor will I endure their iniquities.
65.7: 65.7 The iniquities of the fathers, etc. That is, that you may be punished not only for your own sins, but also for the iniquities of your fathers whom you have imitated. Otherwise the son does not bear the iniquity of the father. Who sacrificed upon the mountains. When in Bethel and in Dan they adored golden calves. The heretic also, despising the simplicity of the Church, sacrifices on the mountains, and reproaches God while he despises his commandments.
65.8: 65.8 As. JEROME. As if he said: For the sake of the wicked I will not destroy the good: but as, etc. For he had said that Israel would perish.
65.9: 65.9 Seed out of Jacob. The seed of Jacob and of Judah, the apostles, possessing mountains, others, namely believers, eminent in virtues: whence, Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us seed, we should have become as Sodom (Rom. 9). My holy mountains. Septuagint: My mountain, namely Christ, who is the mountain of mountains. For the mountains are the apostles, who from the Jews possessed Christ, in whom they are founded. And they shall inherit. JEROME. Whence: The seed of Abraham his servant: the children of Jacob, his chosen ones. Whoever are still seed, etc., up to: 'you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons of God (Rom. 9).'
65.10: 65.10 The plains. The same. Others, the forests, whence: The Lord will reveal the thick places of the woods (Ps. 18), that robbers may cease to lurk there, and beasts and venomous animals pass into the Church of God. Into the folds of flocks. Another translation has Sharon, which is a region between Joppa, Lydda and Jamnia, fertile and pastoral, but infested by robbers: whence it is interpreted a valley pouring out blood. And the valley of Achor. Where Achan son of Carmi, having stolen from the spoils of Jericho, perished with his whole house. And because he troubled the people and perished there, the place is called the valley of Achor, that is, of trouble or tumult. In which Gentilism is signified, as also by Sharon, which is interpreted valley pouring blood, which, full of the shedding of blood, remained in the tumult and trouble of vices. But the valley of Achor was turned into folds of flocks or sheepfolds, and into a resting place of herds, that is, churches, and the rest of the preachers and other faithful, who are designated by the herds and flocks of sheep. Of herds. Of preachers, who arm and defend the Church. For armentum is so called from arming.
65.11: 65.11 And you who have forsaken, etc. Allegorically. All who desert the Church and forget the holy mountain of God, giving themselves to spirits of error or the unclean doctrines of demons, prepare a table for Fortune, and, believing that nothing pertains to God, but that all things are governed either by the course of the stars or by the variety of fortune, these will be handed over to eternal punishments, so that none of them can escape. A table for Fortune. JEROME. The goddess of the Egyptians, for whom at the end of the year they prepared a table, filled with all foods and cups of wine mixed with honey: either as if she had provided a happy year, or because she would provide a happy one to come.
65.12: 65.12 I called. Through the prophets, saying: Be converted to me and you shall be saved (Isa. 45). And through myself: Do penance (Matt. 3). And elsewhere: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened (ibid. 11).
65.13: 65.13 Behold my servants. JEROME. As if he said: You shall not only fall by the sword, etc., up to: 'and, I shall be satisfied when your glory shall appear.'
65.15: 65.15 And you shall leave your name. So that some affirming may say: If I do otherwise, may it happen to me as to the Jews slain by the sword of the Romans. Or thus: I swear by God, in whom the Jews once believed. Or, because God was their oath, which Christians now swear under compulsion of necessity, The Lord lives, namely. And he shall slay you. That you may not have him who says, I am the way, the truth and the life (John 14). Nor will you be called circumcision, but concision.
65.16: 65.16 Because forgotten. JEROME. That they may not remember idols, etc., up to: 'perhaps even in the future the memory of the former way of life will be entirely wiped out.'
65.18: 65.18 For behold. Of angels and men, namely, one Church, and they shall exult and rejoice, that I who created may exult and rejoice in them. Exultation. Of the whole earth, so that what was the joy of the old only-begotten may be a new gladness to all nations. Joy. Which we can understand either after the resurrection, or after baptism in the first resurrection. This to the general resurrection in which all will rise in perfect age. And this is: There shall not be, etc.
65.20: 65.20 A boy of a hundred years, etc. He, namely, who though long, yet lived childishly, serving vices: and Gregory explains it thus. A boy of a hundred years. And a sinner of a hundred years. The life of the boy is indeed drawn out long, so that he may be corrected from childish deeds: but if he is not restrained from the commission of sin even by the length of time, this very length of life, which he received through the mercy of God, grows for him to a heap of curse.
65.21: 65.21 Houses. JEROME. The virtues for which they will rest in the heavens, etc., up to: 'For many saints build houses, but do not dwell in them.'
65.22: 65.22 For according to. The same. As Christ, etc., up to: 'It is a tree of life to those who lay hold on it, namely, wisdom, which is Christ.'
65.23: 65.23 The seed of the blessed. The apostles, and other teachers in preaching, or in other works, like the Jews, because they will receive an eternal reward, for they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves (Ps. 125). Grandchildren. Whom their sons begot in the faith, like Mark, the disciple of Peter, and Luke, the son of Paul.
65.24: 65.24 Before they cry. Not in disturbance, in sorrow of mind, but in joy and gladness: whence, For what is our joy or crown of glory? Is it not you? (2 Thess. 2), etc.
65.25: 65.25 The wolf. The wolf Saul, that is, the persecutor, of whom, Benjamin a ravenous wolf (Gen. 49). The lamb. Those, namely, who in white garments follow the Lamb wherever he goes: To Peter of whom it is said, Feed my lambs (John 21). And the lion and the ox shall eat. A man eloquent and most powerful in the world, having despised the eloquence of philosophy, shall eat the straw, that is, the usefulness and surface of the history, with the oxen, that is, the preachers of the Church. The lions eat these until by many labors they come to the depth of the mystery, like Augustine and Cyprian and others. Neither shall they kill. Their ferocity laid aside, either in the present or in the future, and this is: In all my mountain, etc. The Jews take this carnally, saying that in the time of their Christ there will be such peace and security for them that wolves and lambs, lions and oxen, serpents and men will live together, and eat, and not hurt those who dwell in the temple and the holy mountain. From which it is gathered that all others will be killed. But this is shown to be false by these words: Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth my footstool, etc., yet the Jews understand this carnally.
66.1: 66.1 Heaven. All the saints, whose conversation is in heaven; whence: The soul of the just is the seat of God. Heaven is my throne. As if he said: Do not think that these things are to be fulfilled literally. What is this. As if he said: You think me local, and dwelling only in the temple, but what is this house, etc.
66.2: 66.2 To whom, etc. The altar and earthly temple which human hand built being taken away, the victims of the Jews will rightly be taken away, lest perhaps they should say: We are not so foolish as to think that God can be confined in this place, but in a separate place we sacrifice victims for the glorifying of God as is commanded in the law.
66.3: 66.3 He who sacrifices an ox. JEROME. As if: Your sacrifice does not please me after the immolation of the true sacrifice: in whose shadow I granted you those sacrifices, so that you might not sacrifice to idols. A dog. Of which through Moses: You shall not offer in the house of your God the hire of a harlot, nor the price of a dog (Deut. 23). And well are dog and harlot coupled, because they are alike in lust. They have chosen in their ways. Not by my will, since the true lamb was sacrificed, Whence: Christ our Passover is sacrificed (1 Cor. 5).
66.4: 66.4 And what they feared. The Romans; whence: The Romans will come and take away our place and nation (John 11). Or famine, pestilence, captivity.
66.5: 66.5 Those who hate you. Because you are not of the world, because you believe in me, because you have my name, being called Christians from Christ: whence, For the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed Christ he should be put out of the synagogue (John 9). Let him be glorified. JEROME. As if: Let him appear glorious, etc., up to: 'with great power and majesty and virtue, or even in the present.'
66.6: 66.6 The voice of the people from the city. At the coming of the Roman army, according to Josephus, the Jews were divided into three parts, contending for the leadership. Some set another prince over themselves; a part of the people and of the priests held the temple, a part of the people and princes the citadel and the royal house, and the third part and chiefly the common people the rest of the city. They fought therefore both outside against the enemy and inside against fellow citizens. When the Romans broke into the city, there was heard the voice of the people lamenting from the city, the voice of the priests, and of those who were with them, from the temple. The voice of the Lord also was heard in the exulting Romans, who even by God's will came, rendering recompense to his enemies, namely the Jews, through the Romans.
66.7: 66.7 Before she was in labor. JEROME. Not little by little, nor over a long time, etc., up to: 'and David, he says, The hope of all the ends of the earth and of those afar off at sea (Ps. 74).' A male, a strong people, of which Stephen, Paul, who says: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? (Rom. 8).
66.8: 66.8 In one day. The Apostle begot his sons as it were together in one day, because in Christ, who is light and day; and in the unity of faith.
66.9: 66.9 If I. As if: I who created all men from nothing will create for myself from all nations one Church, which is built of living stones:
66.10: 66.10 Rejoice, etc. JEROME. O angels, O apostles, sad over the perdition of the unbelieving Jews, rejoice, consoled by the faith and salvation of the Gentiles, of whom the Church is built.
66.11: 66.11 That you may suck. The faith of the simple, and good works, delighted by it. The faith of believers is milk and food for preachers. Whence also Christ: I have food to eat which you know not (John 4). And be filled. The woman in childbed who has borne a male does not lack abundance of milk in the rearing of the nation and of the little ones who were born together, that she may offer them the two breasts of the Old and New Testaments. And it should be noted that little ones need the milk of consolation as still living in the flesh: but those who after the milk of consolation have advanced to solid food overflow with the delights of the truth and of knowledge of every kind of glory. That you may milk. Holy Church, one in all, in some has milk, simple faith, namely, and work. In others there overflows every kind of glory, the abundance of charisms, namely, and knowledge of the divinity and of the humanity of Christ. The holy preachers therefore are delighted in all, as culling this from some, that from others. From the breast. From the apostles and preachers to the gifts of the Holy Spirit, or to the doctrine of the Old and New Testament. What they preach they show by works, that thus they may give leadership to their hearers.
66.12: 66.12 They shall caress you. JEROME. Sustaining, giving milk, as he who says, I beseech you, brethren, by the mercy of God, that you present your hearts (Rom. 12), etc. And: I beseech you as strangers (1 Pet. 2), etc.
66.13: 66.13 As. Almighty God, as merciful and compassionate, compares himself now to an eagle, now to a hen, now to a caressing mother, that he may at least allure you with caresses. As the eagle also prepares her nest in inaccessible rocks, that access may be open to none, and in the middle places an amethyst stone, which drives away all poisons, according to the naturalists, to keep off serpents, and some other secrets of nature: so he himself in our hearts places a stone, that is, his faith, namely himself, who is the stone cut out without hands from the mountain, by which all the poisons of the devil are put to flight. For the eagle loves her young more than all beasts, cattle, sheep and birds, as say those who have written of the natures of living things.
66.14: 66.14 You shall see, O apostles, a multitude of the living to the faith. And your heart shall rejoice at their salvation, and your bones, the virtues, shall spring up in the hearts of others, the fruit of good will and work. For as the body is sustained by bones, so the soul by virtues. And your bones. On the day of judgment your bodies will revive in immortality, that as you served God in body and soul in the present life, so in body and soul you may receive rewards. He shall be known. In the judgment, to the good the Son will be known as sweet and mild; to the wicked, as avenger and strong; he who is the hand of the Father, through whom he works all things.
66.16: 66.16 In fire. Which will be eternal for the wicked whom it will wrap, and will lead to eternal punishment by which what is to be purged in the good will be purged. His chariots. A chariot, because he will then triumph and conquer all adversaries: not that he needs the ministry of angels. In fire the Lord. In judgment. Or, his discernment and justice are shown, as he divides the good from the wicked by just judgment, not by power. With the sword. JEROME. The sentence: whence Amos, All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword (Amos 9). For while he renders to each what he deserves, all will know him as a just judge and will praise his judgment.
66.17: 66.17 Who were sanctified. The same. In their opinion in fountains and baptisms, etc., up to: 'but yet it is said to the confusion of those who are not ashamed to do it.' Who were sanctified. According to tropology we can say that all lovers of pleasure rather than of God are said to be sanctified in gardens and on thresholds, according to the Septuagint, because they cannot enter into the mysteries of the truth and eat the foods of piety: because they are not holy in body and spirit nor do they eat the flesh of Christ, that they may have eternal life. For Christ our Passover is sacrificed (1 Cor. 5), who is eaten not outside but in one house and within. In gardens. Not in the sacrifice of the red heifer, which was commanded in the law.
66.18: 66.18 But I. As if he said: Therefore I come to judgment with all nations and tongues, to judge together all their works and thoughts, and to render to them all that they deserve. Tongues. JEROME. Which according to the apostles not only of men, etc., up to: 'according to that: My sword is drunk in heaven, and has come down even to the earth (Isa. 34).'
66.19: 66.19 And I will set a sign among them. Of the cross, of Christianity, of salvation, by which those signed in Ezekiel are not slain; by which in Egypt the doorposts are marked and the Israelites saved. This sign Ahaz refused to ask, to which Isaiah adds: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, etc. And I will send some of them. It seems contrary, when the judgment has been spoken of first, to return to the first coming, by which the apostles are directed to the Gentiles and hear: Go, teach all nations (Matt. 28). But the day of judgment is foretold, that terrified by fear of future punishment they may accept the coming of the Savior and the preaching of the apostles, who are to be sent ahead. To the sea. The world, namely, whose parts he adds, Africa, etc., the south, namely the region in which Africa is.
66.20: 66.20 On horses. JEROME. They are brought, who believe quickly and run swiftly to the faith. In chariots and in litters. The philosophers, namely, shining in doctrine and in honesty of morals: whence they came the sooner to the doctrine of the four Evangelists, and, lifted up by the four principal virtues, reached heavenly things with the mind. On mules. On which David and Solomon are read to have sat. For those who are barren of the world's offspring serve the Lord, who is figured by them, as gentle ones. In wagons. Septuagint: in covered vehicles; others simply. These are they to whom it is said: Bear one another's burdens (Gal. 6). How. As if: With such gladness the apostles bring your brethren, whose gifts are faith, hope, charity, pure prayer, good works, etc., pure vessels, hearts and undefiled bodies. They bring. Which according to the law they did three times a year, namely at Passover, at Pentecost, at the feast of Tabernacles; whence, You shall not appear in my sight empty (Exod. 23). The house of the Lord. The temple of God is holy, which you are (1 Cor. 3). And elsewhere: You are the temple of God and the Holy Spirit dwells in you (2 Cor. 6).
66.22: 66.22 For as the heavens. As if: As these renewed things will remain immovable forever, so your seed, O apostles, renewed, free of all corruption of the flesh, will reign with me forever. For as, etc. JEROME. These things up to the end of the book pertain to the day of judgment.
66.23: 66.23 Month after month. Mene in Greek, in Latin moon, whence neomenia, as it were new moon. From mene comes month among those who begin and end the calends not according to the course of the sun and the different lengths of the months but according to the circuit of the moon, which the Hebrews do. By the month, therefore, the moon is understood; by the moon, which now waxes and, as the physicists and philosophers say, receives from the sun the light which it does not have, the Church is understood, of whom, He shall continue with the sun and before the moon (Ps. 71). And elsewhere: Fair as the moon, bright as the sun (Cant. 6), and this is, there shall be month after month.
66.24: 66.24 And they shall go out. As if to see, not by place but by understanding, or by manifest vision, that they may be the more kindled to the praise of God. And they shall see. JEROME. It is no wonder if the saints, already immortal, see the reprobate, when the prophets, still mortal, deserved to see all these things. Carcasses, because they will fall into eternal damnation, according to which even demons can be called carcasses, as even men are so called. Whence: An enemy man did this (Matt. 13). Their worm. Material, or of conscience; whence: As the moth eats a garment, and the worm gnaws wood, and fire devours wood, so sorrow and sadness torment the heart of a man (Prov. 25). To satiety. Because the good will see them separated from themselves by the just judgment of God, with the power lost by which they raged against the good, and the vengeance of God on them so great that they ask no greater. They who now say, How long, Lord, do you not avenge our blood? (Apoc. 6). They will also be satisfied with their own blessedness, giving thanks, having seen the ineffable punishment of the wicked.
5.4: 5.4 Or what I looked for, etc.? According to some, he said this above within himself; here, however, he questions others about what he had thought.
5.5: 5.5 And now I will show you. As if He said: Since you will not answer, I will therefore answer for you. I will take away, etc. So that those who did not perceive God through benefits may perceive Him through punishments; and therefore He threatens punishment, that they may turn to repentance.
5.6: 5.6 And the clouds. The same. Which under Elijah, etc., up to: 'when they had no prophets and drove away the apostles.'
5.7: 5.7 The house of Israel, etc. The same. Since the kingdom was divided, etc., up to: 'because Christ was born of them.' Behold a cry. By which he cried out against the Lord and shouted, saying: Away with him, away with him, crucify him; or, they made a cry for justice, because they killed Christ, whose blood cries to the Lord: The voice of your brother Abel's blood cries to me from the ground (Gen. 4).
5.8: 5.8 Woe to you who join. This is especially for the Jews, who are most avaricious, etc., up to: 'until the earth fails,' that is, sense and human speech.
5.9: 5.9 In my ears. The same. As if the prophet said: These words I heard with the inner ears, which are of the Lord of hosts. Unless the houses, etc. That is, the pomp and construction of heretics, up to: 'which is bound together by unity in comparison with a manifold number.'
5.10: 5.10 For ten acres. The same. The barrenness of the land which will follow the captivity is shown.
5.11: 5.11 Woe to you who rise up. As if He said: Captivity is at hand, etc., up to: 'they do not understand the works of the Lord in themselves.'
5.17: 5.17 And the lambs shall feed. The same. According to the history it is the same as above: strangers devour your land before you. Strangers: The kingdom of God shall be taken away from you, etc. For gathered from the whole world, etc., up to: 'that lambs might occupy the places of the bulls.'
5.18: 5.18 Woe to you who draw. This is to the princes of the Jews, etc., up to: 'they anathematize the name of Christians.' With cords of vanity. The same. In which they were, etc., up to: 'as though we are held by the strongest bonds.'
5.19: 5.19 Woe to you who say. The same. This is especially against the Jews, who chose Barabbas and condemned Christ; generally against all who justify the unjust and condemn the just. Evil, darkness, bitter are put in a similar sense and figure. In Barabbas we understand the devil, of whom it is said: Deliver us from evil.
5.21: 5.21 Woe to you who are wise. With the wisdom of God despised, etc., up to: 'they neither enter to Christ nor allow others to enter.'
5.22: 5.22 Drunkenness. Wine contains every vice. Drunkenness, which in Hebrew is sicera, signifies all things that overturn the state of the mind. From the abundance of bread and wine the sin of Sodom grew.
5.23: 5.23 Who justify the wicked for bribes. It was said above that in place of grapes they brought thorns, and hay, and wood, and stubble, and briars to be burned, because they not only did these things, but also cast away the law and blasphemed the word of God. Of whom: Out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
5.24: 5.24 Their root. The same. Evil thought, from which the work proceeds like a shoot.
5.25: 5.25 Therefore angry. The same. It should be noted that he does not reproach idolatry and the other sins, but that they cast away the law of the Gospel and blasphemed the holy word of the Lord: who had been angry against the princes and the mighty, who were wise in their own eyes and followed bribes; whom the tongue of fire devoured, so that the mighty suffer mightily torments. He is angry. The same. Not that He is subject to human passions; but we who sin, unless we hear the Lord as angry, do not fear. And He struck, etc. He speaks of future things as past, with prophetic certainty.
5.26: 5.26 And He will whistle to it from the ends of the earth, etc. The same. The Hebrews understand this place of the Babylonians, etc., up to: 'he joins himself in affection to the people, and says:'
5.30: 5.30 We shall look. Not daring to look upon heaven, whose Inhabitant, God, we have offended; and our light, which we always had in God, is darkened by the gloom of tribulations.
6.1: 6.1 In the year, etc. JEROME. Uzziah is the same as Azariah, etc., up to: 'falling on his face, he cries out with a loud voice to the Lord.' King Uzziah. The king, namely the leper, who usurped the priesthood. I saw the Lord. Christ, namely. The Son was seen in the garb of one reigning; the Holy Spirit spoke on account of the fellowship of majesty and unity of substance. Upon a high throne, etc. JEROME. He who sees the Lord reigning among the heavenly powers sees Him upon a high and lofty throne, which are the Thrones and Dominations, etc. Some say the seraphim are powers in heaven standing by God and praising, who are sent on ministries especially to those who need purification, and, because of some sins, in part to punishments. The same. The cherubim are a multitude of knowledge, upon whom the Lord is shown sitting after the manner of a charioteer, whence: You who sit upon the cherubim, etc. But the seraphim, apart from this place, I do not remember having read in the canonical Scriptures. Therefore they err who in prayers are accustomed to write: You who sit upon the cherubim and seraphim.
6.2: 6.2 They stood. The same. That is, they stand, attending God; they fly, making God known; they uncover as it were the half; they do not reveal what is veiled; they do not veil what is known. Six wings to one. The same. Victorinus understands the twelve apostles. But we understand the twelve stones of the altar which iron did not touch, and the twelve gems on the diadem of the priest. The same. Angels are said to have wings, because they dwell in the higher places, or on account of their swift running about in all things, as the winds also are said to be winged. With two they covered His face. What came before these things I do not know, etc., up to: 'angels also and preachers teach nothing of it'; similarly: They covered the feet. JEROME. What will be after this world we do not know; yet the middle things, which were made or are made in six days or ages, we know only. With two they covered, because we have knowledge of the present alone. The same. My Hebrew entered by a far other way, etc., up to: 'and then, truly purified in lips, I said to the Lord: Behold, here I am, send me.'
6.3: 6.3 And they cried. The same. They do not say it lightly, but proclaim with a cry a confession saving to all: Holy, holy, holy, because the seraphim themselves are holy: for nothing is holier than these. They marvel, however, that the Son humbled Himself so much and underwent the cross and became known to earthly beings. Holy, holy, etc. The mystery of the Trinity. In both Testaments the Trinity is preached, the Lord Christ, namely, who here is of four letters, which is properly put for God: Yod, He, Yod, He; that is, two ia, which doubled make the ineffable name of God. All the earth is full. The same. And it will be filled, etc., up to: 'forty-two years after the Passion of the Lord.'
6.4: 6.4 The lintels. In the Old Testament the Lord spoke, etc., up to: 'taking which we say: We know in part, and we prophesy in part' (1 Cor. 13).
6.5: 6.5 Unclean. The same. He says this on account of his fellowship with the people, with whom he was compelled to speak. It is harmful to live with sinners. I dwell. Note that one should not linger with sinners. And I saw with my eyes the King, the Lord of hosts: and one flew to me. So Abraham, after he saw the Lord and heard His voice, confesses himself to be ashes and dust, because however great the dignity of men, it grows cheap in comparison with Him.
6.6: 6.6 Of the seraphim. The same. We say seraphim with m in the masculine gender, with n in the neuter plural. Yet seraphim can be said in the singular, like cherubim and cherub. And in his hand. That is, in his operation, that is, of Christ. The coal, that is, charity, which he had taken from the altar with tongs, that is, the doctrine of the two Testaments, and had set as an example for Isaiah. Coal. The same. The Septuagint: carbuncle, a fiery stone, which on account of its flaming color is called fiery. With tongs. The same. This is the ladder of Jacob, the two-edged sword, etc., up to: 'taking hold of the word of God with the double edge of the precepts.' From the altar. Which John saw in the Apocalypse, which is full of burning coals, by which sins can be purged.
6.7: 6.7 Behold, this has touched your lips: whence: What shall be given to you, or what shall be added to you, for a deceitful tongue? The sharp arrows of the mighty with desolating coals (Ps. 119). This is the word of God, of which it is said: You have coals of fire, you shall sit upon them, these shall be a help to you. And your iniquity shall be taken away. The same. Jeremiah, who was a boy and therefore almost free from sin, is purified by the touch of a hand alone. But to Isaiah, who says: I am a man of unclean lips, an angel is sent with a coal.
6.8: 6.8 Whom shall I send? He does not compel, but seeks the will: for the will alone merits reward. And Isaiah, as one purified, offers himself willingly. Send me. The same. He thinks he will announce good things, etc., up to: 'that his offering himself was not of rashness but of obedience.'
6.9: 6.9 Hear and hear. The same. Luke, according to the Septuagint, in the Acts of the Apostles: You shall hear with the ear and shall not understand, etc., up to: 'and he uses testimonies more from the Greek than from the Hebrew.'
6.10: 6.10 Blind, etc. The same. Like which, etc., up to: 'nor is it the cruelty of God but mercy, when the unbelieving are blinded, to enlighten the humble.' And be converted. Although the sin is grave, if one is converted he can be saved; but these, by the greatness of their crime, are unworthy of repentance.
6.13: 6.13 And still. And for 'still' means: still a tenth of that nation, as though still the tenth part of that nation will remain. And it shall be. Under Hadrian, Judea was laid waste again, in the fiftieth year after the capture by the Romans. For they were forbidden by public laws to enter Judea.
7.1: 7.1 And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz, etc. JEROME. The things written up to this place were seen under Uzziah and his son Jotham; there follow those under King Ahaz, a most impious man, who, forsaken by God, is attacked by enemies. Ahaz. He who shut the doors of the temple and worshipped the Baals, consecrated his son to an idol, took away the bronze altar and set up an altar of idols in the temple. Rightly, therefore, was he forsaken by the Lord: And his enemies rose against him (2 Chron. 28). He went up, a second time. For first the Assyrians from the tribe of Judah, etc., up to: 'Herod and Pilate became friends at the Passion of Christ.'
7.3: 7.3 He was forsaken. By his brother Rabshakeh, who had gone over to the Assyrians, as the Hebrews relate. Shear-jashub your son. The same. Which is interpreted 'the remnant, companion and returning,' because the people of Judah were to be delivered from the hands of the two kings. On the road. There Rabshakeh, afterward by command of Sennacherib, blasphemed the people of God.
7.4: 7.4 Two tails. The two tails, etc., up to: 'and led with the ten tribes into the mountains of the Medes and Persians.'
7.6: 7.6 Tabeel. The same. Tabeel, good God; as if he said: There let us set up the idol of our God; or, literally, he thus calls the Son of man.
7.8: 7.8 Yet sixty, etc. As if He said: In the meantime they will be content with their own borders, and Rezin will rule Damascus as the metropolis of Syria, and Samaria will be the head of the cities of Ephraim, and in it in the meantime the son of Remaliah will reign. Sixty-five years. From the twenty-sixth year of the reign of Uzziah, when he was struck with leprosy, from then his son Jotham reigned twenty-seven years, his father still living. After his death, sixteen years, after whom Ahaz another sixteen, afterward Hezekiah reigning six years. Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes led into captivity, ceased to be a people.
7.11: 7.11 Ask a sign for yourself. The same. So that he who did not believe the prophet might be terrified by the authority of the Lord; as if He said: It seems difficult to you that the most powerful kingdoms should shortly come to an end, and that you and your people be delivered; but ask a sign for yourself. Ask a sign for yourself. Moses received a sign from the earth, etc., up to: 'each looks to the death of the Lord and the ascension.' I will not ask. Not humbly but proudly. For many are read to have asked and received signs from the Lord, but Ahaz answered as one having authority: You shall not tempt the Lord your God. Or, he feared that in the sign God would be glorified and the idols made cheap.
7.14: 7.14 Behold, a virgin shall conceive. The same. In Hebrew alma; in Latin also alma is said to mean 'holy,' etc., up to: 'that it was violently arisen is clear even to fools.' Emmanuel. The same. Some say that Isaiah had two sons, etc., up to: 'on account of which the Word was made flesh.'
7.15: 7.15 To refuse the evil. The same. As if He said: Placed in the swaddling clothes of infancy, He will have the discernment of good and evil. By these words we perceive that the divine wisdom of the Savior was not diminished in His infancy, although it is said: The boy grew in age and wisdom, so that the truth of the human body might be proved: for infancy does not prejudice divine wisdom.
7.16: 7.16 It shall be forsaken, etc. The same. As if He said: The land of Syria and Samaria will be laid waste from the invocation of His name, and the house of Judah will be delivered from the two kings.
7.18: 7.18 The fly. The same. That is, the Egyptians, an unwarlike people, foul with idolatry. We read that Josiah was killed by the Egyptians and the people of Israel subjugated, and not long after, Nebuchadnezzar with an innumerable army took Jerusalem, burned the temple, and placed Assyrians as inhabitants in Judea.
7.20: 7.20 A razor. The same. The king of the Assyrians, who in Jeremiah is called the dove of God; in him as in a very sharp razor, and in those who are beyond the river, namely the Assyrians, the Lord will shave in Judea the head and the hair of the feet, that is, all the strength of kings and princes and subjects.
7.22: 7.22 He shall eat butter. He will delight in the Passion of Christ or his own. For butter is made from many preparations.
7.25: 7.25 And all the mountains that shall be dug with the hoe. The same. Leaving the plains for fear of enemies, they will flee to the hill country, cultivating with their own hands the rough places of the mountains, and will sustain a miserable life. The rest will be for pastures.
8.1: 8.1 And the Lord said to me: Take for yourself. JEROME. First the prophet foretells to Ahaz the future, etc., up to: 'whence again the virginal birth is described.' Swift to the spoils. The same. This is the name of the boy, as if He said: Do not suffer the devil to reign any longer; and send neither angels nor Prophets, but come down Yourself.
8.2: 8.2 Uriah, etc. The same. Uriah, light of the Lord; Zechariah, memory of the Lord; Berechiah, blessing of the Lord; by these witnesses the birth of the Lord is confirmed. Hence to the two witnesses going to Emmaus, beginning from Moses and the prophets, He expounded the things that had been said of Himself.
8.3: 8.3 To the prophetess. The same. To the Holy Spirit, from whom all prophecy comes, which in Greek is pneuma, neuter, in Hebrew Ruach, feminine, in Latin masculine, and so it takes various positions, for it belongs to none. Or to Mary, whom no one doubts to have been a prophetess.
8.4: 8.4 The boy. The same. Isaiah is therefore commanded, etc., up to: 'would save the house of David by invocation alone.' Because this people has cast away the waters of Siloam. JEROME. In which the blind man washed himself, etc., up to: 'he tried to possess the land of Judah itself.'
8.7: 8.7 The waters of the river. The same. The army of Sennacherib, whose power, overrunning the land of Samaria, is compared to the flooding of a river.
8.9: 8.9 Gather yourselves together, you peoples. The same. As if: Against Emmanuel you can do nothing, etc., up to: 'because perversity cannot overcome what is right.'
8.12: 8.12 Do not say. The same. As if He said: Do not fear the conspiracy of the two kings against Judah: a conspiracy is the agreement of many to evil. Do not fear nor be afraid. You and the peoples who are with you, because they seem to be feared; because the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.
8.14: 8.14 For a stone. The same. Which the builders rejected, etc., up to: 'joining sins to sins and bound by the snares of transgressions.' For the two houses. Or in the two families, etc., up to: 'through their traditions they have scattered and defiled the precepts of the law.'
8.16: 8.16 Seal the law. As if he said: Open it, Lord, to my disciples, etc., up to: 'we can also understand the doctrines.'
8.18: 8.18 My children, born of God. Others: the Prophets and their disciples. Some read this of the two sons of Isaiah, etc., up to: 'who were for a portent of secular wisdom and of the pride of the Jews.'
8.20: 8.20 You shall not have. The same. That is, if this people refuses to seek the truth from the Lord, it will not have Christ, namely the light of the truth, which it neglects.
8.21: 8.21 To his king. To the devil and to the traditions of the fathers, that is, to ancient errors.
9.1: 9.1 At the first time. JEROME. These two tribes were led into captivity by the Assyrians, etc., up to: 'first saw the light of the preaching Christ.' The land of Zebulun. The same. In which Christ first preached and worked miracles: for there He turned water into wine and chose the apostles. The way of the sea. The sea in this place is the lake of Gennesaret, which is formed by the inflow of the Jordan. On its shore are Capernaum, Tiberias, Bethsaida and Chorazin, in which the Lord especially dwelt, and so: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Galilee of the Gentiles. There are two Galilees: one of the Gentiles, neighboring the Tyrians in the tribe of Naphtali; the other around Tiberias and the lake of Gennesaret, in the tribe of Zebulun.
9.2: 9.2 In the region of the shadow of death. The same. Those who still live in sins are in the shadow of death: in the region of the shadow of death, those who by dead works have already descended to the lower world.
9.3: 9.3 You have not magnified the joy. To us, concerning the salvation of the Jews; for although they rejoice at the conversion of the Gentiles, yet they grieve over the rejection of the Jews. They shall rejoice before You, etc. The Prophet to Christ, concerning the disciples.
9.4: 9.4 For the yoke. The same. Christ has a yoke, but a sweet one; and the devil has one, but unbearable in burden. And Christ has the government upon His shoulder, on which He bore the cross; and the devil has a rod upon the shoulder, with which he exalts himself. Of the exactor. His own, namely, of him who exacts. For daily he demands, with interest, from the descendants the coin of sin which he committed to the first man.
9.5: 9.5 For all violent plunder. The same. As if he said: The human race which the devil plundered, the Lord will take from him by force, that is, powerfully, and with tumult will thrust him down into hell. Whence both of him and of his members it is said: Their memory has perished with a noise (Ps. 9). A mingled garment. The same. The devil, who is full of the blood of all, who is a murderer from the beginning; or men, with whom the devil is surrounded as with a garment, whose hands are full of blood.
9.6: 9.6 A child is born to us. Not to the Jews, but to us, etc., up to: 'but it does not appear to those who do not see it rising.' The government upon His shoulder. The same. While He was being led to the gibbet, He carried the cross, in which He earned the government. The same. The Septuagint: Angel of great counsel. This is not in the Hebrew, but, terrified by the majesty of the names, they did not dare to say of a child that He is plainly to be called God. Therefore, in place of these six names they put this: Angel of great counsel.
9.7: 9.7 The zeal of the Lord. The same. The prophecy began with Emmanuel, where it is said: Ask a sign of God for yourself. Here it ends.
9.8: 9.8 The Lord sent a word. The same. The Hebrew word is Dabar, etc., up to: 'they despise the Church and think its simplicity to be inexperience.'
9.10: 9.10 The bricks are fallen. The same. They were saying above, etc., up to: 'we will fortify the people with strong and warlike princes.' Cedars. That is, we shall set over them princes from among us who are invincible.
10.1: 10.1 Woe to those who make. JEROME. Many think that these things are still said against the ten tribes, etc., up to: 'when the day of captivity or of judgment has come.'
10.5: 10.5 Woe to Assyria. The same. Up to this point against the ten and two tribes, etc., up to: 'and he not only took captive but in part destroyed.'
10.7: 10.7 But he. The same. So the philosophers, so the heretics, and so the persecutors of the Christian name: when God permits some to be scourged by them, they rage against all, and wish not to scourge but to kill; and having overcome a few, they take boldness against all.
10.9: 10.9 Are not my princes altogether. The order: My princes are kings, that is, serving me: for he brought with him many kings whom he had subjugated. Damascus. Damascus is the metropolis in Syria: Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, founded it; in it Rezin reigned.
10.10: 10.10 As my hand has found. The voice of Sennacherib, marveling at his own power. He fully accomplished the things said. For he plundered all the cities of the ten tribes, and of Judah and Benjamin, except Jerusalem, and its lower part, which Shebna the scribe handed over to him.
10.12: 10.12 When the Lord has completed. The overthrows, namely, of the city, and also the siege when Rabshakeh came and did the things that are recorded in what follows.
10.14: 10.14 Chirped. To chirp is of foxes, or, as others say, of birds.
10.16: 10.16 And under his glory. Jerome says, according to the Hebrews, that the bodies of the slain Assyrians were burned up by heavenly fire and reduced to dust, while the garments were unharmed; and the Jews coming, seizing the edge of the garments, shook out the dust. JEROME. Some want this king to signify the contrary power, etc., up to: 'for the Hebrews relate that only ten of his army remained.'
10.17: 10.17 And the light shall be. The Hebrews say that it was the archangel Michael, to whom the guardianship of that nation was entrusted, as Daniel says.
10.18: 10.18 And the glory of the forest. Carmel, a great mountain, fruitful in trees. Like an innumerable army, like the trees of the forests, both in body and in soul he will perish. To the flesh. The same. Heretics also, when ecclesiastical doctrine has shone and their snare has been laid open, will come to such solitude that, of the forest and the unfruitful trees and the innumerable multitude, scarcely a few will remain who follow their error.
10.20: 10.20 And it shall be in that day. JEROME. When Pekah and Rezin wanted to come, etc., up to: 'but place their hope in God.'
10.21: 10.21 The remnant shall be converted. According to Josephus, an innumerable multitude of the Jews having been slain, we understand that few were saved among the apostles and apostolic men.
10.22: 10.22 The consummation cut short. The perfection of the things concerning Christ, foretold so long before, was fulfilled in three and a half years. Justice, because, killed unjustly, He justly conquered death and the devil and redeemed the world by death.
10.23: 10.23 For the consummation. The same. Literally. He did it, because he slew so great a multitude, besides the ten, in the short space of one night.
10.24: 10.24 Upon you in the way of Egypt. The captivity of the ten tribes, etc., up to: 'he took and overthrew.'
10.25: 10.25 A little while, a very little. This was fulfilled a long time after; but all ages are momentary in comparison with eternity, in which all things are present.
10.26: 10.26 His rod upon the sea. The same. As if: Before he comes upon you, he will attack Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, and will cross the Red Sea, and will lift his rod over Egypt, and so with a great army will return against Jerusalem.
10.29: 10.29 They have passed over quickly. Geba is the seat, etc. The past for the future, in the prophetic manner.
10.31: 10.31 Be strengthened, it is still day. The same. After Sennacherib pitched his tents at Nob, wishing to storm Jerusalem in the morning, he did not cease until the middle of the night to threaten the desolation of Jerusalem, saying: Behold, can this city alone be delivered from my hand?
10.33: 10.33 Behold, the ruler, the Lord of hosts, etc. He said the name of the boy to be born of the virgin, etc., up to: 'and Lebanon with its cedars is cut down.'
11.1: 11.1 And a rod shall come forth. JEROME. Up to the beginning of the vision of Babylon, it is a prophecy about Christ, which we explain in parts, lest we confuse the reader's memory. It shall come forth. The Jews interpret the rod and the flower as Christ Himself, etc., up to: 'and You are My firstborn Son, who reign forever.'
11.2: 11.2 And shall rest. The same. Because in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead. Spirit. As the word of the Lord is called light, life and resurrection, etc., up to: 'these are the seven eyes upon one stone, according to Zechariah.'
11.3: 11.3 And the spirit shall fill him. The same. Spiritually, for the sake of the little ones who need fear, which perfect charity casts out. For he who fears has punishment, and is not perfect in charity. Not according to. He will not accept persons, because God is not a respecter of persons, but in every nation he who fears God is acceptable to Him. He will reprove. The same. The Pharisees, and those reprehending the apostles when, walking through the sown fields on the Sabbath, they plucked ears and rubbed them in their hands and ate.
11.4: 11.4 The rod of his mouth. The same. By the rod can be understood the sentence of judgment. For at the beginning of His preaching He said: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; and added: Every tree that does not bear good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire.
11.5: 11.5 He shall slay the wicked. For if Michael will slay, as some say, yet God Himself will do it in Michael. Faith. JEROME. The faithful, by doing good, will cling to Him who was made wisdom, justice and sanctification, who said: I am the light and the life.
11.6: 11.6 The wolf with the lamb. The same. Paul with Peter, whence: Benjamin a ravenous wolf. And: Feed my sheep. The wolf shall dwell with the lamb. It is not the lamb and the kid that dwell with the wolf and the leopard, but the wolf and the leopard; the lambs and kids imitate innocence, namely Christ. The wolf shall dwell. JEROME. Our Jews who judaize, etc., up to: 'nothing evil, except baseness.' The same. The calf and the sheep, humble and innocent, etc., up to: 'let the Church provide this in the world.'
11.7: 11.7 The lion like the ox, etc. The same. For the princes of this age and the simple are content with the surface of the history; for the wheat and the marrow, that is, the inner sense, they do not understand.
11.8: 11.8 The infant. Christ, or the apostles, small in malice, perfect in sense: who cast demons out of possessed bodies. The basilisk. The basilisk, king of all serpents, etc., up to: 'from possessed bodies, namely.' The hand. That is, the divine power will deliver captive the asp or basilisk, that is, the devil, thence seized.
11.9: 11.9 For filled. In his manner, at the end the prophetic words are spread out, so that they may not be taken literally.
11.10: 11.10 Who stands for a sign, whence: Behold, this child is set for the fall and for the resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be contradicted (Luke 2). The Septuagint: He who shall rise up to be a prince, etc., up to: 'the sepulcher signifies the same.' For 'sleep and rest,' by another word but with the same sense, we render 'sepulcher.'
11.11: 11.11 The remnant. The same. The Apostle: A remnant shall be saved. For the histories relate that the apostles, spread through the whole world, preached the Gospel: and they even penetrated the Persians and the Indians, so that Ethiopia might stretch out her hand to God.
11.12: 11.12 A sign. Of the cross, in which is the victory, that all may know in what the devil was conquered. From the four quarters. The same. This seems fulfilled at Pentecost, etc., up to: 'so that the calling of the whole world may be shown.'
11.13: 11.13 And shall be taken away, etc. The same. When Isaiah foretold this, there was implacable discord between the two and the ten tribes, but believers were reconciled in the faith of Christ and the unity of charity.
11.14: 11.14 The command of their hand, etc. What they command they carry out; and they teach both by word and by example.
11.15: 11.15 The tongue of the sea. The same. Which praised idols. The sea, that is, the people of Egypt, which above all worships idols, that it may praise and fear God, and condemn and cast away idols. And he shall lift up. As Idumea, and Moab, and the sons of Ammon will give their hands to the apostles, so also the Egyptians. And he shall strike. That is, he will diminish by setting seven princes in place of one, etc., up to: 'that they might cross with dry feet.' That they may pass over by it, etc. Under a metaphor, the Nile is said to be divided and cut into parts, etc., up to: 'the Lord preparing the way by the Gospel.'
12.1: 12.1 I will confess to You. JEROME. As, the Red Sea having been crossed, they said: Let us sing to the Lord, etc. So, the kingdom of the world being destroyed, the Church says: I will confess to You.
12.3: 12.3 From the fountains of the Savior. The same. Whence: Bless the Lord from the fountains of Israel, etc., up to: 'that the prophecy may agree with the Gospel.'
13.1: 13.1 The burden of Babylon. JEROME. Babylon, the metropolis of the Chaldeans, etc., up to: 'who says: All these things I will give you, if you fall down and worship me.'
13.7: 13.7 They shall be dissolved, etc. Because no work of God worthy of justice will be found.
13.8: 13.8 Burned. Like coals with excessive grief, or in reality. For many were burned. Burned by fire. By the fire which they kindled for themselves, because they cannot say: The light of Your countenance is signed upon us, O Lord (Ps. 4); and: But we, with face unveiled, beholding the glory of the Lord (2 Cor. 3).
13.10: 13.10 The sun is darkened. These things can be referred to the day of judgment, when all the luminaries will seem darkened in comparison with the splendor of Christ.
13.11: 13.11 And I will visit the evils of the world. I will avenge in order to correct, etc., up to: 'But My mercy shall not be taken away from them.' And I will make to cease. As if He said: I will do this so that he who is proud may be humbled.
13.12: 13.12 A man shall be more precious than gold, etc. The same. All rare things are precious, that is, a man of Babylon will be found more rarely than gold. Similarly the word of the Lord is called precious, that is, it was rarely found. In the day of judgment also the Lord will visit the evils of the world, and will make the arrogance of demons cease, and few elect will be found because of the persecution of Antichrist.
13.13: 13.13 I will trouble the heaven, etc. Not that they are animate, but on account of the indignation of the Lord, who looks upon the earth and makes it tremble. Perhaps, with captivity imminent, the heaven was moved by thunder and the earth by shaking. It can be read of the day of judgment.
13.14: 13.14 A fleeing doe. The doe is the devil or perverse doctrine, whose teachers are signified in the doe, which is so called in Greek.
13.17: 13.17 Behold, I will stir up, etc. We read in Genesis 10 that Madai, son of Noah, was the founder of the Medes: his name is interpreted 'measure,' or 'from the powerful or strong.' Therefore against the Babylonians, who are confused in mind, strengths are stirred up by the powerful and strong God for punishment, to render to each according to his works.
13.19: 13.19 And Babylon shall be that city, etc. The same. It was not afterward rebuilt, etc., up to: 'to be devoured by wolves and dogs.'
13.21: 13.21 Beasts, etc. By all these beasts that flee the light we understand the powers of demons or angels, to whom they are handed over for punishment. Ostriches. Of whom much is said in Job, who are not lifted higher from the earth though they seem to have wings. Hairy ones. Wild, bristly men, who are also incubi, or satyrs, or kinds of demons.
13.22: 13.22 Owls in the houses. Of the size of a raven, but spotted with marks, which shriek horribly with their beak in a marsh. Sirens. They are crested and winged serpents, like other sea fish in the form of a woman, or the portents of the devil, which deceive men with a sweet song, who pass the shipwreck of this world without closing their ears.
14.1: 14.1 Jacob. Note the propriety of the words. Jacob, who is still in the struggle, receives mercy; Israel, who received the name after the victory, He chose.
14.4: 14.4 How, etc. Marveling how the devastator of the lands, etc., up to: 'but the last enemy to be destroyed is death.' The exactor. JEROME. He who exacts from his debtors to the last farthing, who say that: Forgive us our debts (Matt. 5). To him debtors will be handed over; to him Paul handed over the fornicating Corinthian.
14.5: 14.5 The staff. He calls Nebuchadnezzar or the devil, because as the impious are scourged by God through him, so through this one they are in the punishments of hell, or daily in sin by suggestion and ambush.
14.8: 14.8 Also the firs. The princes of various nations afflicted by him; or sons whose fathers he killed. Since you have slept. Because the strong one being conquered and his vessels plundered, his attendants have fallen, whence: Go into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels (Matt. 25). Note that the death of the dead is called sleep. Who cuts down. Whence the psalm: The mountains were covered with its shadow, and its branches are the cedars of God (Ps. 79). These the Lord sometimes hands over, sinning, to be crushed by punishment: whence it is said: The Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon (Ps. 28).
14.9: 14.9 Hell. The inhabitants or princes of that hell beneath you. For hell is under the earth, in which that rich man was seen by Lazarus, whence the Lord rescued His bound ones and let the bound devil go. All the princes. Even if these things have not happened, yet they could have happened. It is a comfort to the wicked to have their enemies as companions in punishment.
14.10: 14.10 You are wounded. You who seemed immortal and God. We, because of the weakness of our senses, thought that we could not resist the power of God, and that you alone remained in your height.
14.11: 14.11 Beneath. The same. Corruption, the moth and the covering of worms, etc., up to: 'who said to Christ: All these things I will give you, if you fall down and worship me (Matt. 4).'
14.12: 14.12 You who rose in the morning. JEROME. These are the false apostles, etc., up to: 'and in the sides of the north, in the cold.'
14.13: 14.13 I will ascend into heaven. The same. He was in the firmament; he desired to ascend into heaven, where the throne of the Lord is. All these things are to be referred to heretics, who, though they are below with their prince, boast that they are exalted. In the sides of the north. Whence: From the north evils break forth, and the pot of Jeremiah is kindled. Of which: I will say to the north, Give up: that is, restore the captives. Of the clouds. That is, of the prophets, of whom: I will command my clouds that they rain no rain upon it (Ps. 35). And Your truth reaches to the clouds. Judas was a cloud with the other apostles, but by his own fault received the devil as his rider.
14.15: 14.15 But yet you shall be drawn down to hell. You who could have ascended by virtues will fall by vices. The saints have the wings of a dove and an eagle, that they may fly and rest; the wicked are sunk like lead in mighty waters, and go down into the deep like a stone (Zech. 5). Iniquity sits upon a talent of lead. You shall be drawn down. Christ was unwilling; He descended willingly. The deep. To the lowest and worst punishments. For the higher the rank, the heavier the fall. Of the pit. That is, of hell, etc., up to: 'but through lukewarmness and pretense of faith they are rejected by the Lord.'
14.16: 14.16 He is a man. The same. Not God; whence: An enemy man sowed cockle over it (Matt. 13).
14.17: 14.17 Cities. The same. Churches, so that he might make them synagogues of the devil and pollute the purity of the faith with heretical perversity. To his prisoners not. Whom the apostles, imitators of the Master, release, etc., up to: 'but shut them up in darkness, so that he would not open even to his son Evilmerodach.'
14.18: 14.18 All the kings. The same. The kings of the nations, etc., up to: 'nor in death does he rest from torments.'
14.19: 14.19 But you. He seems to agree with the fable, etc., up to: 'your father will live again.' Like a corpse. The same. They have rotted by the multitude of sins, and my scars are corrupted (Ps. 37). Virtue is of sweet odor.
14.20: 14.20 Fellowship. Namely, of burial. For the punishment of the author is one thing, that of one compelled by authority is another: This is the sword by which very many were wounded and slain. For you have destroyed the land. As if: In your pride the kingdom of the Chaldeans was destroyed, which would have remained until now had your pride not been. The people. Whom God had entrusted to you to be corrected and ruled. You have slain. Not keeping the living for God, but preparing companions for your punishment. He shall not be called. Therefore he will not be called forever, etc., up to: 'all his offspring was wiped out, for the pride and impiety of the father.'
14.21: 14.21 For the iniquity: The same. The Septuagint: For the iniquity of your father. Some, not understanding this, say that the Hebrews want the dragon who reigns in the sea, whom they call Leviathan, to be the father of the devil, according to that: Because he is a liar and the father thereof (John 8), which they pervert by misunderstanding.
14.23: 14.23 And I will make it. There is nothing in it but royal hunting, and it is enclosed by walls of baked brick rebuilt after very many years. For a possession of the hedgehog. The world also is now possessed by the hedgehog and the marshes, that is, by unclean spirits; but at the end of the world the Lord will sweep, that is, purge it, with purgatorial fire.
14.24: 14.24 The Lord has sworn. Up to this point concerning Babylon and kings, etc., up to: 'and this in the land of Judah and in its mountains, as the Lord had foretold.'
14.25: 14.25 In my mountains. Note the propriety, etc., up to: 'but also those who have advanced in virtues.'
14.26: 14.26 This counsel, that is, let his yoke be taken away, etc., up to: 'it pertains generally to the whole world.'
14.28: 14.28 In the year that King Ahaz died. From the beginning of the book up to here Isaiah prophesied under Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and up to the end under Hezekiah; things foretold and partly fulfilled. Ahaz. While he lived, reigning among sinners, neither a burden against foreigners nor, according to the Septuagint, a word of God could come to the Prophet.
14.29: 14.29 Do not rejoice. When the king is dead, enemies rejoice, as if about to profit from new circumstances: hence the Philistines, whom Ahaz afflicted, rejoice at his death and insult the Jews, because, the mature king being lost, they would be subject to his son, under whose reign they think their borders can be invaded. The rod of the striker. JEROME. The yoke of God being cast off, etc., up to: 'and from them flying serpents, or ones that swallow up birds.'
14.31: 14.31 Howl. The same. As if: Philistines, weep for your misery, which comes through Sennacherib. Howl, O gate; cry, O city. The Philistines falling by drink, etc., up to: 'the soul filled with evil thoughts.' For from the north comes smoke. From the burning arrows of the devil, who is harmful to the eyes and contrary to the light. From the north the pot of Jeremiah is kindled. There is none that can escape his army. None except Jerusalem, etc., up to: 'and Jerusalem alone is to be delivered.'
14.32: 14.32 To the messengers of the nation. To the angels who preside over cities and nations: each marveling why Zion alone avoided or escaped the bitterness of the smoke. He has founded Zion. Upon the foundation of prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance, which are Christ.
15.1: 15.1 The burden of Moab. This is the vision of Isaiah concerning the burden, that is, the destruction, of Moab. Moab, the son of Lot, from whom the offspring and the province was called Moab: in it is Ar, now Areopolis, the metropolis. The burden of Moab. JEROME. There is a carnal and a spiritual circumcision, etc., up to: 'Lot also, Sodom perishing, came to Zoar, and the sun rose.' Ar, that is, adversary, etc., up to: 'afterward they were laid waste by the Chaldeans.'
15.2: 15.2 The house went up. To the high places, in which it had been proud, not to sacrifice, but to lament where it had sinned. Dibon. The same. Their flowing: A lie passes and flows, and never remains in the same state; but the word of the Lord is firm and stable. Hence the manna seems like ice: it does not flow, but holds together. Over Nebo. The same. Because there is one sense of all this prophecy, etc., up to: 'when their soul has howled for itself.'
15.3: 15.3 Every howling. Another reading: Everyone howls, namely Moab, and so shall go down into weeping. As if: He went up to the high places to weep before the idols. But when he found no help there, he went down to weeping on the ground or in his house.
15.4: 15.4 Heshbon shall cry out. From the beginning of the kingdom, which is in Heshbon, to the city of Jahaz where it ends, everywhere is crying, everywhere mourning. The armed men of Moab shall howl. From their wives, strong warriors. Hence Abraham is said to have chosen the home-born servants of his house who were unencumbered, that is, without wives.
15.5: 15.5 My heart for Moab. Namely, that I may provoke them to repentance, etc., up to: 'which is interpreted lion of God.' To Zoar. The same. Zoar is one of the five cities of Sodom, etc., up to: 'if after the deliverance he had not sinned.'
15.6: 15.6 Nimrim. Nimrim is a town upon the sea, etc., up to: 'and therefore the grass will dry up.'
15.7: 15.7 And their visitation. Visitation for evil: I will visit their iniquities with a rod (Ps. 88); visitation for good: The Dayspring from on high has visited us (Luke 1). To the brook of the willows. So far concerning the captivity of the Moabites by the Assyrians; now concerning that by the Chaldeans.
15.8: 15.8 Its howling. As if: Moab will therefore howl, because where before there was luxury and delight, on account of the well-watered ground and the pleasant springs, there now are streams of blood.
15.9: 15.9 The water of Dibon. Dibon, silence; Dibon weeping; and yet it is one city.
16.1: 16.1 Send the lamb. JEROME. Therefore the prophets are scarcely understood, etc., up to: 'who shall rule in the whole world.' The rock of the desert. The same. Ruth, namely, because according to the command of the Lord, etc., up to: 'for as Christ came for both peoples, so He willed to be born of both.' To the mountain of the daughter of Zion. Jerusalem, or rather to the Church, which is in contemplation as a daughter of watching. In Jerusalem also He especially preached, worked miracles, suffered, died, and rose again, and redeemed the human race.
16.2: 16.2 So shall they be. So shall they pass into captivity through Arnon, which is the boundary of the Moabites and Amorites. JEROME. Arnon, which is interpreted 'their illumination,' of those who, leaving errors behind, pass over to the knowledge of the truth.
16.3: 16.3 Take counsel. Do nothing without counsel, and be not carried about with every wind of doctrine; follow the angel of great counsel. Gather a council. Namely, by making the Church out of the wandering and erring. Make as it were night. The tabernacle, namely, in which you thought to rest, etc., up to: 'that it may receive and hide with itself the fleeing people of God.'
16.4: 16.4 My fugitives. Those who fled from me, who went out from the Church, who followed their own sense and not the doctrine of the Holy Spirit. For the dust is ended. Suddenly he passes to the slaying of Sennacherib, who was dust and wretched, because his glory was like dust, which the wind casts from the face of the earth, and he departed wretchedly from this light, slain by his sons in the temple of his god.
16.5: 16.5 And shall be prepared. The Jews explain this of Hezekiah, who after the death of Sennacherib reigned in peace. But it is better referred to Christ, and some things are referred to the first coming, some to the second.
16.6: 16.6 He shall sit upon it. Resting and judging, upon the hearts of the good. We have heard the pride of Moab. In the manner of Scripture, because he had announced joyful things, to keep them from becoming negligent he terrifies by threat. And the indignation. The same. Against God he set his mouth in heaven, disparaging the prophets. Adding that gospel saying: All who came before me were thieves and robbers. He calls Moses and David murderers, Joshua bloodthirsty.
16.7: 16.7 Shall howl. One to another; that is, all the diversities of heretics and philosophers will bellow against each other in torments. Upon the walls. Not built of squared stone, as the temple of God is, in which the stones are so polished that neither hammer nor axe was heard.
16.8: 16.8 The suburbs of Heshbon. All their thoughts, which Heshbon signifies, do not belong to the city of God, of which it is said: The stream of the river makes glad the city of God (Ps. 45); but they are suburbs, so that they may be believed to belong to the city of the Lord. Sibmah. Lifting up height, etc., up to: 'therefore the apostles and apostolic men of the Lord of the nations cut down the vines of Sibmah with scourges.' They wandered. Traversing the whole land of Moab. In the desert. So that at last they had none to kill. The branches. He continues the metaphor of the vineyard. They passed over the sea. The same. That they might see the wonders of the Lord in the deep, delivered from temptations.
16.9: 16.9 The vineyard: The vineyard of Moab, from the neighborhood of the place, is such as Sodom. Sibmah. He who exalts himself against the sentence of God.
16.10: 16.10 From Carmel. Carmel is a mountain between Phoenicia and Palestine, overlooking Ptolemais, on which Elijah prayed. And it is often put for any fertility; whence here also: Joy and exultation shall be taken away from Carmel (1 Kings 18), that is, the fertility in which the Moabites rejoiced. He shall exult. Because heretics boast that they have knowledge of spiritual circumcision. The voice. Lest the venom of the dragon be pressed out from it, and those who drink be slain.
16.11: 16.11 My belly. The prophet, who like a harp, composed by musical art and conceiving from the fear of God, begets many children, so that every string yields its own sound. And my bowels. As a harp does not give forth a composed sound, etc., up to: 'and James, to whom one is lacking, all are lacking.'
16.12: 16.12 His holy things. To the holy place, namely of the Church, he will try to make his own things, but will not prevail: for we do not at once attain virtue perfectly. He shall not prevail. They will find no help in those things in which he hoped, and so it appeared that he had worshipped in vain.
16.13: 16.13 This word. In the preface, etc., up to: 'For what had begun for you is here completed.'
16.14: 16.14 In three years: as if He said: As a few clusters remain, etc., up to: 'but, error abandoned, converted, he is left in three years only small and modest and inglorious.' Hirelings. The same. False doctrine does everything for the sake of gain, etc., up to: 'it is a lighter sin to sin openly than to feign holiness.'
17.1: 17.1 The burden of Damascus. Behold Damascus. The same. Damascus, the metropolis of Syria, etc., up to: 'but because they did no penance, they were taken captive.'
17.2: 17.2 Aroer for flocks. The tamarisk, which is an unfruitful tree, growing in deserts and rocky places; as if He said: All the Syrians will be unfruitful and desolate. Others say that by magical arts hatreds are stirred up from this tree.
17.3: 17.3 And the kingdom. That sin may not reign in her who before loved blood. The remnants of Syria. Ironically, for disgrace, etc., up to: 'both therefore taken captive ignominiously.'
17.4: 17.4 And it shall be in that day. The same. When Syria shall have been laid waste by the Assyrians, etc., up to: 'others were moved to Cyrene, which is a region beyond Egypt.' It shall wither. The same. They will have no prophets, nor signs, nor miracles, nor kingdom, nor priesthood; but the whole body of the nation will wither.
17.5: 17.5 In the harvest. It is said of the Gentiles: The harvest indeed is great, but the laborers are few (Matt. 9). But they, poor, gather the remnants of the harvest which were saved by the apostles, and the rarest ears. Not on the mountains but in the valley of Rephaim, that is, in humility, in the truth of the letter. For Rephaim means giants.
17.6: 17.6 As the shaking. The same. The people of the Jews being struck, the olive tree which under Moses had six hundred thousand armed men, and under David, when Joab numbered, a countless people, scarcely offered a few fruits to the Savior. Of two or three. Paul and Barnabas. And of three: Peter, and James and John, who beheld the Lord transfigured on the mountain and saw the daughter of the ruler of the synagogue raised. Or four. JEROME. These are the remaining nine, in whom Matthias took the place of Judas the traitor. These, unknown to us in respect of the diversity of graces, were set apart in four or five, to show in themselves the number of the Gospels and the volumes of the law, as preachers of both Testaments.
17.7: 17.7 In that day shall bow down. As if He said: The Lord, hungry, scarcely a few, etc., up to: 'as is read in Chronicles, and they cast away the idols.'
17.9: 17.9 In that day shall be. The Assyrians rushing in, and laying waste not only Damascus but also the land of the ten tribes. The plows. The same. Of the Amorites. This is against the ten tribes, as if He said: As of old, when the children of Israel came, the Amorites left their plows and fled, so now the ten tribes at the coming of the Assyrians.
17.10: 17.10 A faithful plant. A faithful plant is when one plants and tends and gathers the fruit. An unfaithful plant and foreign shoot is when a stranger gathers: Every plant which my Father has not planted shall be rooted up (Matt. 15). Foreign shoot. Not receiving the Father, because you do not receive the Son; for he who believes in the Father believes in the Son. Foreign shoot, of blasphemies against Christ.
17.11: 17.11 In the morning your seed. The same. When, namely, the shoot has been seen, etc., up to: 'all the saints with the branches of the wild olive to be saved at the root.'
17.12: 17.12 Woe to the multitude. To Sennacherib and his army, etc., up to: 'to one desiring to oppress and seize everything.'
17.13: 17.13 He shall be snatched away. He was snatched from Jerusalem when with a few he fled to Nineveh. He was snatched from the world when he was quickly killed by his sons, as is clear.
17.14: 17.14 This is the portion of those who have laid waste. The prophet, from the person of Israel, as if He said: Thus God is wont to bless our enemies.
18.1: 18.1 Woe to the land. The same. Because he had spoken of the other persecutors of the Church, etc., up to: 'as though by wandering he had made them useless.' Woe to the land of the winged cymbal. He turns again to Egypt, and calls it, etc., up to: 'they took from them the fear of the Lord.'
18.2: 18.2 In vessels of papyrus, that is, in ships made of papyrus, etc., up to: 'passes by and slips away.'
18.3: 18.3 A nation waiting and trodden down. For all heretics promise themselves great things, etc., up to: 'that is, they hear their doctrine.'
18.4: 18.4 A cloud of dew. Pleasing to wearied reapers, to whom it gives refreshment, and by moistening makes the dry stubble cuttable: so my word against Egypt will be pleasing to all who believe in me, and to the Assyrians the victory given them by me.
18.5: 18.5 Little branches. The same. Useless ones: whence: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman: every branch in me that bears no fruit He will take away, and every one that bears fruit He will purge.
18.6: 18.6 And all the beasts of the earth. Hyperbolically. For not all the beasts of the earth will winter upon him. But it signifies both an immense slaughter and a very great multitude of beasts that will come, for whom the corpses will suffice for food in summer and winter.
18.7: 18.7 In the time. The Prophet returns to the people of Israel, and promises them good things, saying: In the time, as if he said: Egypt being laid waste, Judah will no longer hope in its shadow; but will offer to the Lord a gift of faith and good works. Which was fulfilled in the seventieth year after the captivity under Zerubbabel and the other leaders.
